name: Gabby Giffords
subject: How many more children will have to live this nightmare?
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

Friends,
Yesterday morning, our country suffered an all-too-common tragedy when a gunman opened fire at Annunciation Church in Minneapolis, home to a pre-K-8 school.
Students were packed into the pews for mass when the gunman — who was armed with a rifle, a shotgun, and a pistol — fired deliberately at the church. Current reports are that two children were killed and approximately 20 others were injured.
The first week of school is supposed to be filled with joy and making new friends. Instead, innocent kids were forced to hide for their lives from bullets and left traumatized. And now, some families are left with an empty seat at their dinner table forever.
I am heartbroken and furious. How many more children will have to live this nightmare before our elected leaders do something?
Gun violence is a crisis in our country, and we must do more than offer just thoughts and prayers. These children were literally shot in a church while praying — at the hands of weapons designed to kill as many people as possible.
We owe it to all the victims and survivors to demand change, end this crisis, and build a future where we can all be safe. That is my mission, and the mission of GIFFORDS. We will keep working until it becomes a reality.
Please keep Minnesota and the Minneapolis community in your thoughts.
Thank you,
Gabby Giffords

**Please, take a second to read this...**
Gabby Giffords has led the fight against the gun lobby for more than a decade, but she can't do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to take on the gun lobby in Congress and states across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
**If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to contribute to GIFFORDS PAC today.**
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/63973?c0=giffords-em-aug25.orWe61&refcode=em250828-1-b&t=1&akid=10829%2E3935704%2EhAPVYZ)**

Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. www.Giffords.org
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. We try to send only the most important information and opportunities to participate via email, but click [here](https://go.giffords.org/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=2&akid=10829%2E3935704%2EhAPVYZ) if you'd like to unsubscribe. Giffords PAC was started to support elected officials who step up to fight the gun violence epidemic. Thank you for standing with Gabby and the Giffords team.

As Kadida mentioned below, traditional institutions and foundations are falling short of meeting this critical moment, and we need your help.

**We’ve been sounding the alarm:** Republicans see these judicial elections as their best chance to reverse our Democratic majority on the PA Supreme Court and establish a MAGA-controlled court. State supreme courts impact everything from voting rights to reproductive rights, environmental protections, redistricting, and much more. Their work is critical – which is why the GOP is working overtime to replace Democrat-elected justices ahead of the 2026 elections and why we need to ensure that voters in PA understand what’s at stake.

**However, we are facing a funding gap, and we are depending on grassroots donors to help us hit our goals so we don’t have to reduce our Get-Out-The-Vote (GOTV) efforts as we head into the fall.** [**Will you donate $25 or more today to help us prepare to turn voters out and ensure our state courts remain fair and independent?

\----------- Forwarded message ---------

Fellow activist, During these unprecedented times, our nation is navigating a new reality, and our rights and freedoms are consistently at risk of being stripped away. **NOW is the time that we need to invest in our year-round work engaging voters.**

We are preparing for our critical Get-Out-The-Vote (GOTV) door-knocking and digital communication program ahead of the judicial election to begin October through November. Unfortunately, too many **institutions are failing to meet this moment with much-needed EARLY funding.**

Judicial elections could not be more important, yet we are not seeing traditional funders step up to ensure we can counter far-right funders that are already pumping dark money into Pennsylvania. We must fully fund our GOTV program to ensure voters turn out in this important local, municipal, and judicial election year. While it can be common to face scarce funding during odd-year elections, the judges and justices we elect this fall will play a critical role in protecting our voting rights, and all the other freedoms we’ve fought so hard to gain. We cannot afford to slow down or play catch up.

**More than ever before, we are depending on the power of individual grassroots donations to fuel our organization. That is why we are reaching out today. **
[**We are facing the decision to reduce our GOTV efforts as we near the November election, and we cannot let that happen. Will you help fill our budget gap by pitching in $25 today?

clean_body: | | | As Kadida mentioned below, traditional institutions and foundations are falling short of meeting this critical moment, and we need your help. We’ve been sounding the alarm: Republicans see these judicial elections as their best chance to reverse our Democratic majority on the PA Supreme Court and establish a MAGA-controlled court. State supreme courts impact everything from voting rights to reproductive rights, environmental protections, redistricting, and much more. Their work is critical – which is why the GOP is working overtime to replace Democrat-elected justices ahead of the 2026 elections and why we need to ensure that voters in PA understand what’s at stake. However, we are facing a funding gap, and we are depending on grassroots donors to help us hit our goals so we don’t have to reduce our Get-Out-The-Vote (GOTV) efforts as we head into the fall. Together, Katy Personette Chief Development and Grants Officer \----------- Forwarded message --------- Fellow activist, During these unprecedented times, our nation is navigating a new reality, and our rights and freedoms are consistently at risk of being stripped away. NOW is the time that we need to invest in our year-round work engaging voters. We are preparing for our critical Get-Out-The-Vote (GOTV) door-knocking and digital communication program ahead of the judicial election to begin October through November. Unfortunately, too many institutions are failing to meet this moment with much-needed EARLY funding. Judicial elections could not be more important, yet we are not seeing traditional funders step up to ensure we can counter far-right funders that are already pumping dark money into Pennsylvania. We must fully fund our GOTV program to ensure voters turn out in this important local, municipal, and judicial election year. While it can be common to face scarce funding during odd-year elections, the judges and justices we elect this fall will play a critical role in protecting our voting rights, and all the other freedoms we’ve fought so hard to gain. We cannot afford to slow down or play catch up. More than ever before, we are depending on the power of individual grassroots donations to fuel our organization. That is why we are reaching out today. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: This isn’t hyperbole. If MAGA is successful with their anti-retention campaign against three Supreme Court justices who were elected as democrats, we will face a constitutional crisis. We are counting on your support to invest in our work and boost our GOTV program to ensure our state courts remain fair and independent. Friend, Anger is not getting us anywhere. I am dealing with it too, **we all are.** The news is infuriating. What Trump and MAGA are doing is a desecration of our country and our Constitution. Rage may feel good for a split second, but in the end it is counterproductive. **It is human nature, but we cannot get stuck there.** Every time we turn to our phones to check in on what is going on, our hearts drop. It does not matter if it is innocent folks working hard at manual labor jobs, struggling to provide for their families, only to be torn away from them, or children simply playing, only to be bombed and starved by U.S.-funded Israeli troops. We are living in a bleak time, and unfortunately, I have more awful news to share with you; it is about to get worse. **The Israeli military is now ramping up efforts to storm Gaza, killing indiscriminately in a bid to permanently seize the land. ** Earlier this week, they even stormed Palestinian banks in the West Bank and stole the money. Their "double tap" operation is as cruel as it gets; they bomb a hospital once, wait until rescue workers and journalists arrive, then bomb it again. This is who and what we are funding. **The ironic part is that Israeli troops are entering Gaza at the same time American troops are preparing to enter our own cities.** They have already been deployed in Washington, D.C., and now they are gearing up for Chicago and New York. We have to stick together in times like this, and by together, I mean Americans and humans against the corporate monstrosities that have taken over the powers that be in this country, including the DNC. The corporate-controlled media may not cover it, but people are talking. More importantly, we are rallying around elected leaders and new candidates who are speaking out. The only way we fix this is at the ballot box. In the meantime, **we use our microphone strategically and effectively.** At the end of the day, no matter how they try to spin it, more people agree with us than with them. They can take their trillions of dollars and shove it. We want to live in a country that embraces everyone, regardless of where they come from, their economic means, their skin color, or their religion. That is what it means to be a Democrat. That is why we fight, why we will not give up, and why we are going to win. We have a lot of wrongs we must undo.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: I’m officially in the race for U.S. Senate.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-cooper?refcode=082825_1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-cooper?refcode=082825_1]
Hi, Peter,
I’m Roy Cooper, and I am running to be the next U.S. Senator from North Carolina. I believe that our brightest days are still ahead, but we have to work together to fix what’s broken in Washington.
Politicians in DC are running up our debt, ripping away our health care, disrespecting our veterans, cutting help for the poor and putting our Medicare at risk — just to give tax breaks to the very rich. I’ve had enough.
We have to change things, but I need you with me. Together, we can win this Senate race and help Democrats take back the majority. Will you split a contribution of $20 or another amount that’s right for you between my campaign and The Real Texas PAC to get us started off strong? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-cooper?refcode=082825_1]
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-cooper?refcode=082825_1]
These are no ordinary times, Peter . I believe elected leaders should work to create safety, prosperity and opportunity for every American. Republicans in Washington don’t seem to share that sense of duty.
When I look at what’s happening in Washington now, lawmakers are tearing down our middle class to put even more money in billionaires’ pockets. They’re cutting critical jobs at agencies that help keep our country running. Not even our National Parks or Weather Service are safe.
They’re punching down — attacking the most vulnerable among us — to make themselves seem strong. Something has to give.
There’s another path, Peter. When I was Governor of North Carolina, we expanded Medicaid. We passed pay raises for public school teachers and we built a strong economy by investing in clean energy and investing in our people.
Washington can look like this, too. It’s time to elect leaders who are ready to do the hard work of strengthening our middle class, restoring voting rights and reproductive rights, protecting our environment and ensuring every child has the excellent education they deserve.
If this is the America you believe in, this campaign is for you, Peter .
We’re in for a tough election here in North Carolina, but with the help of committed supporters, we’ve won the toughest races before. I’m grateful to have The Real Texas's support in this crucial race, and I’d like to have yours, too. Your donation today will help us take on the challenge of the most competitive Senate campaign in 2026. Please give whatever is right for you and split a donation between our team and The Real Texas today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-cooper?refcode=082825_1]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation to Roy Cooper and The Real Texas PAC will go through immediately: DONATE $5 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-cooper?express_lane=true&refcode=082825_1&amount=5]

Let’s do this together,
Roy Cooper

| | | How the hell is this nut still in charge of our nation's health care system?
* He's gotten rid of some of the best scientists and health care experts on Earth, and replaced them with lunatics driven by conspiracy theories.
* He's blocked millions of Americans from Covid shots, basically ensuring another wave of infections and deaths in coming months
* He's said a measles outbreak is not a big deal,
* He asserted the MMR vaccine contains "aborted fetus debris"—a baseless, debunked statement that fueled vaccine distrust.
* There's also been the other incredibly bizarre crap, like dumping a dead bear in Central Park, hosting a brain worm in his head, and swimming in a feces-tainted river.

He's doesn't have the knowledge or experience necessary for the job, and he's relying on bullshit to fill the gaps. And he's going to get people sick, and killed. [**He needs to go NOW. Add your name: "Don't let RFK Jr. destroy our health care system. He needs to go NOW!"**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T308ce071-4727-47c8-8b47-934a59333086/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

Lexington Herald Leader: Gov. Andy Beshear adds Kentucky to two suits over Trump funding freezes

Peter,

100 days into the Trump administration, we saw a tactic being used that was not only unlawful but just plain cruel: Donald Trump decided to withhold $430 million in federal funding to vital programs at the state level—even though Congress had already promised it.

**Just recently, Trump announced the freezing of $6.8 billion in education funding, $3.6 million in unemployment insurance funding, and $32 million from the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure program.** This is money already spent by Congress—which controls the funding for our entire nation—to be distributed to states. Donald Trump does not have the power or the authority to withhold these funds, but he’s trying to do so anyway, just to bully states into supporting his agenda.

Gov. Andy Beshear is not accepting these unlawful freezes. He’s already added Kentucky to three multi-state lawsuits that would require the Trump administration end the funding freeze and allow money already decided by Congress to be directed to the states immediately.

Peter, these funds are meant to keep our schools strong, build the infrastructure our people use every day, and make sure families have what they need to live their lives with dignity.

But, thanks to Trump's broken promises, Kentucky could be forced to do more with less— _leaving classrooms underfunded and communities without support, and slowing down one of our biggest growing industries: electric vehicle battery manufacturing._ **That’s why Andy has joined lawsuits to stop these cuts and protect every dollar our state was promised.**

These cases are about real Kentuckians— _our students, our workers, and our neighbors._ Andy’s working hard to ensure Kentuckians receive every penny of money they were promised by Congress, because that’s what true leadership is about. But Peter, he’s not just protecting our state, he’s working to support other leaders across the country who are fighting for their own communities, too.

Andy Beshear adds Kentucky to two suits over Trump funding freezes Peter, 100 days into the Trump administration, we saw a tactic being used that was not only unlawful but just plain cruel: Donald Trump decided to withhold $430 million in federal funding to vital programs at the state level—even though Congress had already promised it. Just recently, Trump announced the freezing of $6.8 billion in education funding, $3.6 million in unemployment insurance funding, and $32 million from the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure program. This is money already spent by Congress—which controls the funding for our entire nation—to be distributed to states. Donald Trump does not have the power or the authority to withhold these funds, but he’s trying to do so anyway, just to bully states into supporting his agenda. Gov. Andy Beshear is not accepting these unlawful freezes. He’s already added Kentucky to three multi-state lawsuits that would require the Trump administration end the funding freeze and allow money already decided by Congress to be directed to the states immediately. Peter, these funds are meant to keep our schools strong, build the infrastructure our people use every day, and make sure families have what they need to live their lives with dignity. But, thanks to Trump's broken promises, Kentucky could be forced to do more with less— leaving classrooms underfunded and communities without support, and slowing down one of our biggest growing industries: electric vehicle battery manufacturing. That’s why Andy has joined lawsuits to stop these cuts and protect every dollar our state was promised. These cases are about real Kentuckians— our students, our workers, and our neighbors. Andy’s working hard to ensure Kentuckians receive every penny of money they were promised by Congress, because that’s what true leadership is about. | | Patriot, I know you’ve seen how the Left is creating a generation of fearful and confused children. And some of the worst culprits in this ungodly indoctrination are at your very own local library! Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_. But today, all that has changed. The president of the American Library Association (ALA) is a self-described “Marxist lesbian.” Radical librarians call _Adventure of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic” _Little House_ series. And they bring men in wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... A is for Activist. An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for...”

| | For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating “the environment” to a type of religion. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family – for now. But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! [**I hope you see why I need your help today to TAKE BACK OUR LIBRARIES.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.” I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood. But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian. When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So together with a small Christian book publisher aptly named **BRAVE Books** , I wrote “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit. And then we decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with a wholesome Story Hour of our own. Our idea was to read the classic books you and I grew up with plus new wholesome **BRAVE Books** that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism. And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected our request to host our Story Hour. >> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep us out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), **BRAVE Books** was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” our supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on. I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. In the end we got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those Story Hours where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America,” and read wholesome and Godly books. It was incredible. But here’s the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking **BRAVE Books** how they could host Story Hours of their own. So **BRAVE Books** has organized a nationwide grassroots “See You at the Library” movement to take back our libraries. Now with the guidance of **BRAVE Books** , committed conservatives just like you book event rooms at their local library for conservative Story Hours that fill children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. And whenever we can, **BRAVE Books** authors like swimmer **Riley Gaines** , TV personality **Missy Robertson** , and myself stand shoulder-to-shoulder with conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots at these Story Hours... ...for a very simple mission – to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. 2025 was the third year of “See You at the Library” and I’m proud to say that because of the amazing support of patriots like you, we were invited by President Trump’s DOE to kick off our event at the Library of Congress! What a testimony it was to bring our message of freedom, America’s greatness, and God’s love to children and families in the heart of our nation’s capital. Now we have a new and historic goal for 2026 – the 250th birthday of our nation! We aim to reach 250,000 children in the next year. But we can’t do it without you. __**[_I hope you’ll be able to give a sponsorship gift of $35, $50, $75, $100, $125 or more today..._..](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Your sponsorship gift will be used to send a “Story Hour Kit” to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing an event at their library. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for the little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. **BRAVE Books** is a small Christian company. They don’t have the millions behind them like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our Story Hours for over 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries. Knowing that, **[_please consider a sponsorship gift of $125._](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** That’s enough to sponsor one entire “Story Hour Kit” yourself. Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. **_[Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower will be necessary for the success of the next “Story Hour Kit” to be sent.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)_**

Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America,

Kirk Cameron

| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/114165148/566159740/1328794144?refcode=ea.b06738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ms=ea.b06738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImIwNjczOGRmLTJhODQtZjAxMS1iNDg0LTYwNDViZGViNzQxMyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=fSZ-cFNJL3BaKDbJy7AiQt5BPTCfhYA2CKfh8VhPwaM=&emci=9e6738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&emdi=b06738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ceid=4823105)

[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/114165149/566159741/-1772575153?refcode=ea.b06738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ms=ea.b06738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImIwNjczOGRmLTJhODQtZjAxMS1iNDg0LTYwNDViZGViNzQxMyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=fSZ-cFNJL3BaKDbJy7AiQt5BPTCfhYA2CKfh8VhPwaM=) Hey there, it's Julia Louis-Dreyfus. I played a narcissistic, megalomaniac sociopath who became president of the United States on the TV show Veep. Does that remind you of anyone? Yeah. Only this time, it's not so funny. Donald Trump is rolling out the red carpet for Big Oil while communities across the country are crushed by record-breaking heat and climate disasters. He’s even treating our public lands like some kind of fossil fuel clearance sale. **That’s why I'm all-in to support my dear friend Jane Fonda's climate PAC. She’s working to elect climate champions — from city councils to Congress — who can take on Trump’s fossil fuel agenda and actually deliver solutions for people like you.[Jane tells me her team needs to reach their $30,000 goal by Sunday's deadline — can you chip in whatever you can to help? ](https://click.everyaction.com/k/114165150/566159742/-1772575153?refcode=ea.b06738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ms=ea.b06738df-2a84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImIwNjczOGRmLTJhODQtZjAxMS1iNDg0LTYwNDViZGViNzQxMyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=fSZ-cFNJL3BaKDbJy7AiQt5BPTCfhYA2CKfh8VhPwaM=)** I’ve seen Jane’s commitment to this fight up close. When she came on my podcast _Wiser Than Me_ , she asked if I’d join her in taking on Big Oil’s massive referendum campaign here in California. I obviously said yes. (Can you say no to Jane Fonda?) Together, we helped defeat a $60 million effort by the oil industry to overturn protections for our communities. Now, Jane and I are teaming up again, this time to stop a Texas oil company trying to restart the pipeline that spilled over 120,000 gallons of crude oil off the coast of Santa Barbara back in 2015. What I’ve learned from working alongside Jane is this: **When Washington won’t protect us, we have to build power everywhere else.** That’s what JanePAC does. State and local leaders have become our last safeguard against Trump’s assault on environmental protections, reproductive freedom, and even democracy itself. You may not hear about county commissioners or city council races on your news alerts, but those leaders can shield their communities from corporate polluters and Trump's merry band of yes-men when federal leadership fails. **Here's the problem: These climate champions are too often outspent by candidates backed by oil and gas money. We see it all the time. Together, we helped defeat a $60 million effort by the oil industry to overturn protections for our communities. Now, Jane and I are teaming up again, this time to stop a Texas oil company trying to restart the pipeline that spilled over 120,000 gallons of crude oil off the coast of Santa Barbara back in 2015. What I’ve learned from working alongside Jane is this: When Washington won’t protect us, we have to build power everywhere else. That’s what JanePAC does. State and local leaders have become our last safeguard against Trump’s assault on environmental protections, reproductive freedom, and even democracy itself. Fellow Conservative,

You may not know me yet, but my name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m a lifelong Minnesotan, former Navy SEAL, and Marine Corps veteran running for U.S. Senate in 2026. I’m stepping into this fight because Minnesota—and our country—needs a new voice to stand up for our values, and I’m asking for your help to make it happen.

I grew up in Bloomington, Minnesota, playing hockey and learning teamwork from my working-class parents. _**On my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after 9/11, I enlisted in the Marine Corps to serve our nation.**_

**Over 21 years, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries as a Marine and Navy SEAL, putting my life on the line to defend our freedoms.** I earned my undergraduate degree from the University of Minnesota, a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But at my core, I’m a regular guy who wants to make my mom proud and fight for the Minnesota I love.

Right now, Minnesota and America face a critical moment. The radical policies of Tim Walz and his lieutenant governor—who’s running to replace retiring Senator Tina Smith—threaten our way of life. From the unrest in Minneapolis in 2020 to attacks on our police, their agenda doesn’t reflect the Minnesota I know. _**This open Senate seat in 2026 is our chance to take back our state and stop the left’s push toward extremism. Just like in Georgia, where one seat flipped the Senate majority in 2021, Minnesota’s vote could decide the future of the U.S. Senate.

**_ **But here’s the challenge: I’m a new face, and the Democrats are already raising millions to keep this seat.** I’ve noticed you haven’t been active lately, Fellow Conservative, and I get it—the news can feel overwhelming, and it’s easy to think the fight’s already won. But I can’t do it without you. | Fellow Conservative, You may not know me yet, but my name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m a lifelong Minnesotan, former Navy SEAL, and Marine Corps veteran running for U.S. Senate in 2026. I’m stepping into this fight because Minnesota—and our country—needs a new voice to stand up for our values, and I’m asking for your help to make it happen. I grew up in Bloomington, Minnesota, playing hockey and learning teamwork from my working-class parents. On my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after 9/11, I enlisted in the Marine Corps to serve our nation. Over 21 years, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries as a Marine and Navy SEAL, putting my life on the line to defend our freedoms. I earned my undergraduate degree from the University of Minnesota, a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But at my core, I’m a regular guy who wants to make my mom proud and fight for the Minnesota I love. Right now, Minnesota and America face a critical moment. The radical policies of Tim Walz and his lieutenant governor—who’s running to replace retiring Senator Tina Smith—threaten our way of life. From the unrest in Minneapolis in 2020 to attacks on our police, their agenda doesn’t reflect the Minnesota I know. This open Senate seat in 2026 is our chance to take back our state and stop the left’s push toward extremism. Just like in Georgia, where one seat flipped the Senate majority in 2021, Minnesota’s vote could decide the future of the U.S. Senate. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114166361/566161776/-975735282?refcode=em_logoheader&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMWQyMDE2OC0yYzg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UvKyx7kIwZSfUlMq98xAOEFqCbdz3lz-UmtgE6REw8g=)
Peter,

I still remember sitting at the kitchen table with my daughter years ago, helping her study for a civics test. Like every kid in America, she had to memorize the three branches of government and what they do.

**Thinking back to that memory, it struck me — with all the noise, the headlines, and the partisan bickering we see about Congress every day — it’s worth asking a pretty basic question:_What the heck does a representative actually do?_**

That question is at the heart of this campaign. **[And if you believe the answer should be “fight for Iowans, not stand by partisan elites,” then I’m asking you to chip in right now to help us reach our end-of-month goal. Every contribution matters in this race against Mariannette Miller-Meeks>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114166362/566161784/-1612730695?refcode=em25_250827_EOM1_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_250827_EOM1_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=b1d20168-2c84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMWQyMDE2OC0yYzg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UvKyx7kIwZSfUlMq98xAOEFqCbdz3lz-UmtgE6REw8g=)**

If you asked Mariannette Miller-Meeks, her answer would probably be something like: professionally ignore your constituents, get cozy with corporate backers, and hold onto every scrap of political power you can. _That’s all she’s shown us she cares about._

But here’s the real answer: a representative is supposed to meet with the people they represent, listen to them, and stand up to party bosses to defend Iowa values. Your representative should work on committees to shape laws that actually _help_ families and communities back home.

And then there’s the part of the job most people never see in the headlines: Helping a veteran cut through red tape to get the benefits they earned. Making sure a retiree doesn’t lose their Social Security check. Working with a local school or small business to help them apply for federal funding that could change lives here at home.

**That’s what a representative can do when they actually care about the people they serve. And that’s the part of this job I look forward to most.**

But I can only serve you if we win the election next November. And to win, we need to build a campaign strong enough to take on the entrenched power of someone like Mariannette Miller-Meeks. That means hitting every fundraising goal, including the one we face at the end of this month.

**[Will you chip in whatever you can today to help us reach that goal — and to bring real representation back to Iowa’s 1st District?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114166363/566161786/-1612730695?refcode=em25_250827_EOM1_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_250827_EOM1_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=b1d20168-2c84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMWQyMDE2OC0yYzg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UvKyx7kIwZSfUlMq98xAOEFqCbdz3lz-UmtgE6REw8g=)**

clean_body: | = Peter, I still remember sitting at the kitchen table with my daughter years ago, helping her study for a civics test. Like every kid in America, she had to memorize the three branches of government and what they do. Thinking back to that memory, it struck me — with all the noise, the headlines, and the partisan bickering we see about Congress every day — it’s worth asking a pretty basic question:What the heck does a representative actually do? That question is at the heart of this campaign. = If you asked Mariannette Miller-Meeks, her answer would probably be something like: professionally ignore your constituents, get cozy with corporate backers, and hold onto every scrap of political power you can. That’s all she’s shown us she cares about. But here’s the real answer: a representative is supposed to meet with the people they represent, listen to them, and stand up to party bosses to defend Iowa values. Your representative should work on committees to shape laws that actually help families and communities back home. And then there’s the part of the job most people never see in the headlines: Helping a veteran cut through red tape to get the benefits they earned. Making sure a retiree doesn’t lose their Social Security check. Working with a local school or small business to help them apply for federal funding that could change lives here at home. That’s what a representative can do when they actually care about the people they serve. And that’s the part of this job I look forward to most. But I can only serve you if we win the election next November. And to win, we need to build a campaign strong enough to take on the entrenched power of someone like Mariannette Miller-Meeks. That means hitting every fundraising goal, including the one we face at the end of this month. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through Ballots dropped YESTERDAY and there are various events this week where you can chime in and help us elect the first Latina to Congress!

| | **My role as your representative is to work for you and listen to your concerns.** This month, I have been travelling across the district listening to the people of Northwest Washington. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114166864/566163267/-1930544823?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2YjUyYjhhNy0yZDg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4AS2Fi0Gc00wGUNo4YwMp9WWoVB3LI4xjz9VhB2TBPo=&emci=7aed4cf0-bb7e-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&emdi=6b52b8a7-2d84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ceid=9494239) **[Read More](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114166865/566163270/-1930544823?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2YjUyYjhhNy0yZDg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4AS2Fi0Gc00wGUNo4YwMp9WWoVB3LI4xjz9VhB2TBPo=&emci=7aed4cf0-bb7e-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&emdi=6b52b8a7-2d84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ceid=9494239)** President Trump's Big Ugly Law, which was signed into law on July 4, is negatively impacting Edmonds College and its students who rely on federal assistance. | | Hi Friend, I’ve spent my life relying on public transit. As someone who was born with congenital blindness, I know firsthand what it means when buses don’t show up, stations aren’t accessible, or entire neighborhoods are left off the map. Every person deserves access to safe, reliable, and accessible public transit. But too often, our systems are built without individuals with disabilities, the elderly, and low-income riders in mind — leaving people cut off from jobs, schools, health care, and opportunity. That has to change. [**I’m fighting in Congress to make transit justice a reality — but I need you with me. Will you add your name to demand accessible transit for every community?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114167352/566164708/824584376?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTEzNTIxZTctMmY4NC1mMDExLWI0ODQtNjA0NWJkZWI3NDEzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=HBqRz6k3N1vF4yU79V3GcJ3cGAv6dHkCcHeFhE5wk-w=&emci=91bf8b78-977f-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&emdi=113521e7-2f84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ceid=22554739) | [Add your name »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114167353/566164709/824584376?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTEzNTIxZTctMmY4NC1mMDExLWI0ODQtNjA0NWJkZWI3NDEzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=HBqRz6k3N1vF4yU79V3GcJ3cGAv6dHkCcHeFhE5wk-w=&emci=91bf8b78-977f-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&emdi=113521e7-2f84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ceid=22554739)

[**So I’m asking again: Will you stand with me and add your name today?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114167354/566164710/824584376?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTEzNTIxZTctMmY4NC1mMDExLWI0ODQtNjA0NWJkZWI3NDEzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=HBqRz6k3N1vF4yU79V3GcJ3cGAv6dHkCcHeFhE5wk-w=&emci=91bf8b78-977f-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&emdi=113521e7-2f84-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ceid=22554739)

MONDAY:
Celebrate worker power with TOP and allies Labor Day in Houston
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Workers%20over%20billionaires%20graphic%20-%20Labor%20Day%202025.jpeg]
Working people built this nation and we know how to take care of each other. And we'll never stop fighting for our families and the rights and freedoms that ensure access to opportunity and a better life for ALL who call this country home. Join TOP and Houston-area allies MONDAY, SEPT. 1 for a "Workers Over Billionaires" Labor Day celebration.
Register here and share with your networks! [https://actionnetwork.org/events/workers-over-billionaires-labor-day-celebration/]
At this event, we'll continue the movement that progressive organizations across the country collectively launched on May 1, standing in solidarity with all our communities under attack from the Trump regime and fighting for real wins for all our people.
Trump is wrong on bail
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Justice%20gavel%20bail.jpg]
Unhinged as ever, Trump is abusing his power to appear "tough" on crime. On Monday, he signed an executive order seeking to end cashless bail nationwide.
Trump’s out-of-touch approach to bail and public safety is a waste of taxpayer money that upholds a two-tiered justice system — one for the wealthy and well-connected like him, and another for everyone else. It won’t make Texas any safer. Texans need investments in justice, not mass incarceration.
Thousands sit locked up in Texas jails only because they can’t afford bail [https://www.texastribune.org/2024/08/13/texas-jails-overcrowding-inmates/] — not because they pose a public safety risk. Studies show that the majority of those in jail in our state have not been convicted of a crime; these Texans simply can’t buy their freedom.
We should instead create a legal system that humanely addresses root causes of crime, while protecting the rights of all Texans — no matter one’s race, age, income, or ZIP Code. This means investing in mental health care, addressing poverty, and offering real life-changing opportunities for community members.
For more information about TOP's Right2Justice campaign, contact Laquita at lgarcia@organizetexas.org [lgarcia@organizetexas.org] .
SURVEY FOR TEXANS:
Help TOP unite around one major campaign priority
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Brighter%20Dallas%20community%20dinner%20July%202025.JPG]
If you live in Texas and care about building a more progressive future for our state, we want to hear from you! TOP is uniting around one major campaign priority that we believe will reflect the Texas we deserve. Your voice is essential in shaping our collective fight for justice and equity.
TEXANS: Click here to take our quick survey. [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc0JcmarckcN1aeYp7Qy807cgCm0rIjxGJsg2s5nfS7STQ-cA/viewform]
For more information about this survey and campaign effort, contact Sofia at slopez@organizetexas.org [slopez@organizetexas.org] .
TOP Tip: Close out Black August with purpose
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Black%20August%201970s.jpeg]
As the month winds down, let’s never forget that Black August is a time to remember the many Black freedom fighters and radical organizers who have been persecuted, imprisoned, and slain by the government. It’s also a time to educate the masses about appalling conditions in U.S. prisons, to demand for the release of political prisoners in our country, and to recognize the history and legacy of Black power building and resistance. Add these Black August books to your reading list this year. [https://tracithomas.substack.com/p/the-nonfiction-files-6-black-august]
Español
LUNES:
Celebremos el poder obrero con TOP y sus aliados el Día del Trabajo en Houston
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Workers%20over%20billionaires%20graphic%20-%20Labor%20Day%202025.jpeg]
Los trabajadores construyeron esta nación y sabemos cómo cuidarnos unos a otros. Nunca dejaremos de luchar por nuestras familias y por los derechos y libertades que garantizan el acceso a oportunidades y una vida mejor para TODOS los que consideran este país su hogar. Únase a TOP y a sus aliados del área de Houston el Lunes 1 de Septiembre para la celebración del Día del Trabajo "Trabajadores por encima de Multimillonarios."
¡Regístrese aquí y compártanlo en sus redes! [https://actionnetwork.org/events/workers-over-billionaires-labor-day-celebration/]
En este evento, continuaremos el movimiento que las organizaciones progresistas de todo el país lanzaron colectivamente el 1 de Mayo, solidarizándonos con todas nuestras comunidades atacadas por el régimen de Trump y luchando por victorias reales para toda nuestra gente.
Trump se equivoca con la fianza
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Justice%20gavel%20bail.jpg]
Tan desquiciado como siempre, Trump abusa de su poder para aparentar ser duro con la delincuencia. El Lunes, firmó una orden ejecutiva que busca poner fin a las fianzas sin efectivo en todo el país.
El enfoque desconectado de Trump en materia de fianzas y seguridad pública es un desperdicio de dinero de los contribuyentes que sostiene un sistema judicial de dos niveles: uno para los ricos y bien conectados como él, y otro para todos los demás. No hará que Texas sea más seguro. Los tejanos necesitan inversiones en justicia, no encarcelamiento masivo.
Miles de personas permanecen encarceladas en las cárceles de Texas solo porque no pueden pagar la fianza [https://www.texastribune.org/2024/08/13/texas-jails-overcrowding-inmates/] , no porque representen un riesgo para la seguridad pública. Los estudios demuestran que la mayoría de las personas encarceladas en nuestro estado no han sido condenadas por ningún delito; estos tejanos simplemente no pueden comprar su libertad.
Deberíamos crear un sistema legal que aborde humanamente las causas profundas de la delincuencia, a la vez que proteja los derechos de todos los tejanos, sin importar su raza, edad, ingresos o código postal. Esto significa invertir en atención de salud mental, atender la pobreza y ofrecer oportunidades reales que transformen la vida de los miembros de la comunidad.
Para más información sobre la campaña Right2Justice de TOP, contacte a Laquita en lgarcia@organizetexas.org [lgarcia@organizetexas.org] .
ENCUESTA PARA TEJANOS:
Ayude a TOP a unirse en torno a una prioridad principal de campaña
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Brighter%20Dallas%20community%20dinner%20July%202025.JPG]
Si vives en Texas y te preocupa construir un futuro más progresista para nuestro estado, ¡queremos saber de ti! TOP se une en torno a una importante prioridad de campaña que creemos que refleja el Texas que merecemos. Tu voz es esencial para dar forma a nuestra lucha colectiva por la justicia y la equidad.
TEJANOS: Haz clic aquí para participar en nuestra breve encuesta. [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfTKxlrQM-gxC6Fgv_7OpkJ3xS11ZBSxGAQ8dx8aOKHnaNwzQ/viewform]
Para obtener más información sobre esta encuesta y la campaña, contacta a Sofía en slopez@organizetexas.org [slopez@organizetexas.org] .
Consejos de TOP: Cerrar el Agosto Negro con propósito
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Black%20August%201970s.jpeg]
Al finalizar el mes, no olvidemos nunca que el Agosto Negro es un momento para recordar a los numerosos luchadores por la libertad y organizadores radicales afrodecendientes que han sido perseguidos, encarcelados y asesinados por el gobierno. También es un momento para educar a las masas sobre las terribles condiciones en las cárceles estadounidenses, exigir la liberación de los presos políticos en nuestro país y reconocer la historia y el legado de la construcción del poder y la resistencia afrodescendiente. Añade estos libros de Agosto Negro a tu lista de lectura este año. [https://tracithomas.substack.com/p/the-nonfiction-files-6-black-august]

name: Rural Americans United
subject: ICYMI: Strategy, Media, and the Future of Rural Washington
body:
Communication is power. Control the message, shape the outcome.
| | | | |
---
| What Is In This Newsletter?

* Strategy, Media, and the Future of Rural Washington
* INATAI Foundation awards Rural Americans United the Community Power grant!
* Shout out to Jayce Wright and Tri Cities NAACP Chapter

---
| |
---
|
Communication is a powerful tool, and controlling communication is almost infinite power.
When social media first launched, I had high expectations that it would democratize the internet, giving individuals the same strength of voice usually reserved for deep-pocketed corporations or governments. To some degree, this did happen. We now have influencers with millions of followers. However, if you consider a scantily clad person on social media doing silly dances to be a strong and influential voice, the definition has shifted.
By and large, the power of communication still lies in the hands of the few, and its importance can be clearly seen in how it has shaped American ideology. The far right has shown its astute planning for the future by playing the long game. This is further reinforced by the rush of MAGA-leaning billionaires buying communication networks, such as Larry Ellison's company acquiring CBS and Paramount, Jeff Bezos purchasing the Washington Post, Elon Musk acquiring Twitter, and Mark Zuckerberg shifting the significant influence of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. And let us not forget the family rivalry of the Murdochs, where patriarch Rupert is fighting a court battle to keep his media empire firmly in the hands of his MAGA-aligned son.
One of the biggest statements on the change and influence of media came from Mark Zuckerberg.
Facebook dropped third-party fact-checking and replaced it with community notes written by the people, like you and me, on the site. This may seem friendly and social, except Mark Zuckerberg's stated premise for doing this was that people are no longer interested in facts but in what they want to believe. He used the election of 47 to support this, suggesting that because 47 is a firehose of false narratives, lies, and deception yet was still elected, people now prefer a relative version of the truth rather than objective facts.
---
| |
---
| How does this affect a candidate running for office in districts such as Washington's 4th and 5th congressional districts?
I was at lunch the other day and, as not too typical, was asked if I would run again. Without hesitation, I said that if the right people asked me, I would, and much to my surprise I already had the list ready in my mind:

* Local 598 out of Hanford

My father retired from Local 598 plumbers and steamfitters. When I ran, they treated me like a stray cat dragging a dead rat around in my mouth. This goes far beyond a point of pride to have them "accept me." It is about union support, and if 598 steps up with an endorsement and significant cash, the other dominoes will fall into place. This is significant.

* The Tamaki family

They bring a substantial amount of credibility and monied resources to the table. I was told that unless they were confident I was going to win, they were only mildly interested in the race. Having their backing demonstrates a commitment to winning this race that it has, if ever, rarely seen.

* Either the Washington State Democratic Senate or House

We saw during the last Legislative District 14 race with our three strong candidates what west side Democrats can do if they give a damn. They pumped large amounts of money and support into the district, which changed the game in many positive ways. My guess is that only about two cents out of every donated dollar for Democratic politics from deep-pocket west side donors makes it east of the mountains, Spokane aside. This needs to change.

* Mainstream Republicans (I would still run as a Democrat)

With a large number of voters identifying as Independent and leaning right, there could be no better endorsement of a centrist, both-sides-of-the-aisle candidate than to have an influential group provide an endorsement--or at least a nod.

* Methow Valley

Our deep-pocket Democrat transplants from the west side. They are thoughtful, invested, and passionate. But are they really committed to the east side in the same way they are to the west side and big marquee races around the country? It is time to prioritize our neighbors and our own backyard ahead of others.
There are, of course, other influential groups, but these five represent the different pillars that must be addressed to truly have a winnable race. And they all point toward raising enough money. As I understand it, I raised more money than any candidate in Congressional District 4 history, and it was still not even close to enough. Why? Simply put, it is impossible to make your name common in every household in a district as large as 4 by either going to every fair, rally, parade, and knocking on twenty thousand doors--or by spending your entire media budget in the last 4 to 6 weeks of the race.
The sad reality is that between low voter turnout, the power of the Republican brand, and most voters being seriously unaware of important facts about the candidates--relying instead on name recognition or party alignment--it cannot be done that way. If I were to run again, hypothetically speaking, I would require at least a ten-month media campaign saturating Congressional District 4 with unique, frequently changing, highly relevant, and personal messaging.
That is why I started talking about the media and its importance and followed with my criteria of which organizations are needed to make it all happen.
I do believe that a good candidate can win without all of these things, but that would be the difference between winning the lottery and operating off a strategic business plan. We only have to look at all, for good or bad, that 47 has accomplished. He has effected more change in less than a year than most presidents accomplish in two terms--all because he had a strategic plan: Project 2025. Here is to our victory.

Rural Americans United provides a vital service for communities in rural Washington State. Through the use of media, we reach those who might otherwise be excluded from political information and the democratic process. Everyone deserves to be informed and included. With voter turnout rates declining, it is more important than ever that we expand our work. With your support, we can.

Jayce is building community and they are shaping history. As Communications Director for [NAACP Chapter 1135-B](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0012ZyZbeqz5s_6G2xzzvwDBj1sDmARNZBb3-uL91nMtm2sf-f_AwM7UkeCHtW6FAd30mSWQNF79nMv6SkwMDDuqOchkETe7d3pmmElnbDWuEjCOT0O_qn2hHYbIOw8tsqMELbeamNoSaKNxbprE7jp8WmiEF840F3S&c=YtJM3iLsJIi7wodF8xS_5uuIokgUizj7mg8_L3JQuamMHtYlawezcA==&ch=hfLFv1xw3eg1lp_NH2ajtd-j1qWNZAN2NX1giNVXUTbZP4LxKzyTuw==), they are making sure voices that have too often been silenced are heard loud and clear. We are proud to have leaders like Jayce on our team.

clean_body: The groundwork we set now will decide what happens in September, November, and beyond. | = Peter, today we're officially launching our End-of-Month drive — with the goal of raising $15,000 before midnight on August 31. This fund is critical to ensuring EMILYs List has the resources to go on offense in upcoming elections and stay on defense against Donald Trump and his Republican lapdogs. | = Here's what's at stake: On offense: Primaries begin in September, and key governors' races are coming in November. The Democratic pro-choice women we've endorsed need strong support to organize on the ground and reach voters before they head to the polls. This fund will help lift them up in some of the toughest, most competitive races in the country. On defense: Trump and his allies are already spreading lies and laying the groundwork to undermine the 2026 election — including vows to end mail-in voting. November 2026 may feel far off, but the disinformation campaign has already begun, and setting the record straight needs to happen NOW. This is what it means to be ready: we can't wait until September, November, or 2026. * **TOP NEWS**

**" October hearing set on legality of new Texas congressional boundaries," **Dallas Morning News' **Gromer Jeffers, Jr.** \-- "A federal judicial panel will hear arguments beginning Oct. 1 for an injunction against the implementation of [new congressional boundaries ](https://substack.com/redirect/b088df9d-fec2-4a0f-b19f-84d89c1a5c87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)approved by the Texas Legislature.

According to three lawyers who were in the El Paso courtroom Wednesday when judges made the decision, the hearing on the congressional boundaries will take place from Oct. 1-10 in El Paso. That would allow enough time for the three-judge panel to make a decision on whether the maps are legal or violate the federal Voting Rights Act before the December filing deadline for the 2026 elections.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/8af4110e-cef3-474f-88e1-5a53774d49c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A written order is expected to be released Thursday morning, the lawyers said.

"They came up with the best time under the circumstances," said **Gary Bledsoe** , the president of the Texas NAACP and one of the group's lawyers. Bledsoe is also a lawyer for U.S. Rep. **Jasmine Crockett** , D-Dallas.

"We think this is a case where the racial bias is just overt," Bledsoe said before getting on a flight back to Austin.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/8af4110e-cef3-474f-88e1-5a53774d49c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A [67-page complaint](https://substack.com/redirect/865af4ff-8095-4585-8527-47625d64dc2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), filed hours after the map was approved by the Legislature, argues that the redistricting plan is discriminatory.

State Rep. **Matt Shaheen** , R-Prosper and chairman of the House Elections Committee, said 2026 candidates would likely run under the new boundaries.

"I have a high level of confidence that after further review the maps passed by the Texas Legislature will stand," Shaheen said.

The new map, approved this month by the Legislature, will reconfigure Texas' congressional districts in an effort to turn five of them to Republican control from Democrat control. The redistricting was requested by President **Donald Trump** in an effort to shore up his Republican majority in Congress heading into the 2026 mid-term elections.

Texas Gov. **Greg Abbott** has said he plans to sign the bill into law.

Bledsoe said Trump's request that Texas embark on mid-decade redistricting will be the center of the plaintiff's case.

"Trump's letter will be exhibit No. 1," he said.

The El Paso federal panel also held a trial in May over whether the 2021 legislative maps passed by the Texas Legislature are legal. It has yet to issue a ruling." * * *
**" Uvalde school didn't release most of its shooting-related documents but says it was a mistake," **AP's **Juan A. Lozano** \-- "The Uvalde school district released only a small fraction of the documents it said would be made public regarding the 2022 [Robb Elementary School](https://substack.com/redirect/05bf36d2-94e0-40e8-9ffc-a5897282a33c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) massacre, with district officials in the small Texas town saying this week it was an honest mistake that they were fixing.

The mix-up was revealed during an Uvalde school board meeting on Monday when the attorney for the district said his law firm mistakenly failed to make public all documents as had been promised in a legal settlement. He blamed it on "reasons that are our firm's business, but it is our error."

"We are not in any way trying to hide anything. We are not in any way trying to not release things," attorney**Robb Decker** said.

Earlier this month, the Uvalde Consolidated Independent School District [released more than 3,500 pages](https://substack.com/redirect/cd8da83b-3155-4c01-8438-2ca5d670c6a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) following years of litigation. The school district had sought to withhold documents connected to the attack that killed [19 students and two teachers](https://substack.com/redirect/c0671227-d49d-414d-9512-263db33cac9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one of the deadliest school shootings in U.S. history. The [school board had voted](https://substack.com/redirect/0713770f-52ac-41c3-9052-b3cd6856bf76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in July to release all the district's records and end the lawsuit pursued by media organizations to make the information public.

The botched release was another misstep for district leaders who have been criticized for fighting the lawsuit and not making this information public sooner.

School district members on Monday regretted having to again apologize to family members of the victims and the community for an error following the shooting. The school district's police and other law enforcement agencies have also been heavily scrutinized for their [delayed response](https://substack.com/redirect/c968fc96-2d50-4c3d-835b-074534ba68b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as terrified students inside a classroom called 911 and parents begged officers to go in.

Family members including **Jesse Rizo** , the uncle of 9-year-old victim **Jackie Cazares** and a member of the school board, were among those pushing to see the records.

**" Bill to let AG prosecute election crimes heads to Abbott, but is it legal?" **Dallas Morning News' **Gromer Jeffers, Jr.** \-- "A bill that would allow the attorney general to prosecute Texas election fraud cases is headed for Gov. **Greg Abbott 's** desk, but it's unclear whether the proposed law is constitutional.

The legislation, approved by the House on Tuesday, would bypass restrictions in the Texas Constitution on the attorney general's ability to prosecute voter fraud cases. The power to prosecute such cases belongs to local district attorneys, a policy that was upheld four years ago when the all-Republican Court of Criminal Appeals ruled that the attorney general's office could not unilaterally prosecute cases involving voter fraud or other election-related crimes.

The court pointed to the separation of powers clause in the state constitution as the reason the attorney general's office could not prosecute election law crimes.

The legislation, approved Tuesday in the House by an 85-54 vote, was accompanied by a resolution that would put to voters the question of whether to change the state constitution to allow the attorney general such powers. But that resolution did not get the 100 votes needed for approval.

State Rep. **Matt Shaheen** , R-Plano and chairman of the House Elections Committee said the bill by itself meets the objective of changing the law even without the needed supermajority on the resolution. Shaheen authored the House legislation, which was identical to the Senate bill the House approved.

Shaheen said changing the Election Code to give the attorney general the power to prosecute election-related crimes was constitutional. Under Texas law, local district attorneys have the power to prosecute election crimes. The attorney general's office can be involved but only with the invitation of a district attorney.

Shaheen said the bill "replaces permissive language stating that the attorney general may prosecute with the mandatory language affirming that the attorney general has jurisdiction to prosecute." Specifically, language in the code changes from "may" to "shall," Shaheen said.

If constitutional, the change would flip the authority of prosecuting election law crimes from local district attorneys to the attorney general.

"By passing SB-12, the legislature ensures that Texas election laws are fully enforceable and that the criminal violations can be prosecuted," Shaheen said. "This legislation strengthens public confidence in Texas elections and safeguards the integrity of our democratic process."

The law falls short, however, of what Abbott outlined when he included the matter in special session agendas.

In his proclamation for the special sessions, Abbott asked lawmakers to consider "legislation proposing a constitutional amendment allowing the Attorney General to prosecute state election crimes."

A spokesperson for the governor declined to comment on the matter Tuesday. Shaheen said he was confident Abbott would sign the legislation.

Democrats blasted the bill as unconstitutional and unnecessary.

State Rep. **Joe Moody** , D-El Paso, said "our constitution wisely gave the keys to local prosecutors."

"This isn't a partisan issue. It's a political philosophy issue," Moody said. "It's something we need to take a long-term view on, because there's a jail cell at the end of that road."

Attorney**Ken Paxton** has long sought the power to prosecute election law cases. In 2024, he campaigned against three Court of Criminal Appeals judges who ruled that his office didn't have the power to prosecute election fraud. **" Harris County constables, sheriffs could contract with HOAs without commissioners' OK under bill heading to Abbott," **Texas Tribune's**Alex Nguyen** \-- "Two bills that focus solely on Harris County law enforcement agencies' contracting and funding advanced to the governor's desk, two days after being added to the second special session's agenda.

Currently, sheriffs and constables in Harris County can contract with homeowner associations, school districts and municipal utility districts to provide additional policing for them. Both the county and contracting groups have to sign off on the contract, and they split portions of the cost depending on the amount of time the deputies spend in the area.

The more prominent of the two proposals, [House Bill 26](https://substack.com/redirect/486cc972-2693-4f16-8655-cefe2b7f8355?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), would allow these law enforcement agencies to enter into such contracts without the need for approval from the county's commissioners court. Meanwhile, [House Bill 192](https://substack.com/redirect/72743e46-a248-4562-b219-18cb1c8cbced?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would require the county to seek voter approval if it adopts a budget that reallocates unspent funding that was appropriated for law enforcement agencies or moves funding previously appropriated for a specific law enforcement position to another agency.

State Rep. **Tom Oliverson** , the Cypress Republican who carried both bills, and his backers said they are about protecting law enforcement including this popular deputy contract program.

Their critics, however, said the legislation would upend the county government's checks and balances, as well as harm taxpayers.

"You already pay your taxes for a constable to patrol your neighborhoods. But now they want to go and bid a contract with your HOAs, to pay them, to contract with them, to patrol your neighborhood more often," state Rep. **Charlene Ward Johnson** , D-Houston, said during a Texas House hearing about HB 26 on Wednesday. "That's double taxation."

The House then cleared HB 26 with a 88-49 vote and HB 192 with a 89-48 vote early Wednesday afternoon. Hours later, the Texas Senate voted 21-5 to approve both bills. These proposals now head to the governor's desk.

The votes came two days after Gov.**Greg Abbott** added the items to the second special session's agenda on Monday, saying that the legislation would improve public safety. Oliverson quickly thanked the governor in[ a post on X](https://substack.com/redirect/925d89bb-4eb8-436f-8c31-1d3c66d0fddc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for "protecting neighborhood law enforcement contracts for the vast majority of unincorporated Harris County and ISD's that depend on them."

Oliverson said the legislation is needed because the deputy contract program is under attack, despite its popularity and importance to unincorporated areas. The county also [discussed earlier this month ](https://substack.com/redirect/926df263-ddb3-44b1-bc51-0c137b0a05bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)raising the contract's costs for some groups in order to help cover constable pay raises, the Houston Chronicle reported.

"Unfortunately, there's a lot of friction going on between the law enforcement departments and Commissioners Court with regards to the terms and conditions of those contracts," Oliverson said during a House committee hearing for HB 26 on Aug. 22.

The committee then heard testimony from **Tom Ramsey** , a Harris County commissioner who spoke about the importance of such a program to maintain public safety and growth in his precinct, which covers most of[ the county's unincorporated](https://substack.com/redirect/9686a518-a863-4411-ab4f-fe090fbd7495?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) areas. It also received signed letters from all eight Harris County constables that show their bipartisan support for a proposal that would "remove [the program] from the threat of any volatile partisan whims of our Commissioners Court."

"Us going and negotiating directly with some of those neighborhoods that have been sorely overlooked all these years is going to be a great thing if this bill passes," Constable **Alan Rosen** , a Democrat, added in his testimony.

Some Harris County commissioners, however, told the Texas Tribune that they oppose the proposals.

Commissioner **Rodney Ellis** called the legislation part of the state's "ongoing war on local government," while Commissioner **Adrian Garcia** said the bills could create difficulties for maintaining other public safety initiatives and stressed that public safety shouldn't be about who can pay extra.

Garcia also warned that the proposed shift of control over the contracts could "cripple the county budget process."

"How are the 5 members of Commissioners Court expected to set a budget when in the middle of a fiscal year, 9 other independently elected officials could effectively set the whole county's budget because of these contracts," he said in a statement. "On a governance perspective, this legislation would be a budget killer."

The Tribune also reached out to the offices of Commissioner **Lesley Briones** and County Judge **Lina Hidalgo** , but didn't receive comments.

Meanwhile, some officials from other parts of Texas are already wary about the precedent that these proposals could set. They said state lawmakers could come back in future legislative sessions and add counties with fewer than 3.3 million people -- the bills' current threshold, which limits them to just Harris County.

"We defend, we don't defund," Rick Bailey, a Johnson County commissioner, told the Tribune. He registered against HB 26 but didn't testify. "But this has the potential to have some really negative effects on county budgets and local taxpayers."

Oliverson didn't respond to the criticism posed on the House floor on Wednesday. His office also didn't provide a comment in response to requests from the Tribune." Editorial: **" State lawmakers are expanding STAAR, not scrapping it. Abbott should veto.," **via San Antonio Express-News**** \-- "Gov. Greg Abbott has made eliminating STAAR, the state's almost universally loathed education assessment, [a top priority this summer](https://substack.com/redirect/311957a9-b240-4719-8513-18c010ced3e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

If he really believes the STAAR must go, then he should veto the legislation that state lawmakers have advanced.

[House Bill 8](https://substack.com/redirect/8cea3098-5e57-4427-9207-cb0dd3cb93b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which the Texas House [passed Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/b538799f-9923-4066-b340-55ce2de2ffa7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and its counterpart, [Senate Bill 9](https://substack.com/redirect/72907464-a70d-4f75-9313-f2fbf584584d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which has cleared the Senate Finance Committee, are much more likely to be an expansion of STAAR -- albeit under a new acronym -- than an elimination of high-stakes testing.

Why do we say this? After all, supporters of the House version, authored by state Rep. **Brad Buckley** , R-Salado, have argued that rather than administering one big high-stakes test at the end of the year, public schools, beginning with the 2027-28 school year, will administer three rounds of testing to track student progress. The bill also bans districts from additional benchmark testing, although districts could use outside tests such as iReady or MAP for the first two rounds of assessments.

Yes, and it's much more complicated than that. Stick with us.

To begin with, the bill continues the Texas Education Agency's creation and use of an end-of-year high-stakes exam, a key factor in determining A-F ratings for schools and districts.

This new end-of-year exam continues many of the disagreeable features of STAAR. Students will be measured by whether they approached, met or mastered grade-level skills, and they will be compared to state benchmarks, rather than norm-referenced standards.

One of the concerns public education experts have raised is the inherent conflict of the TEA creating the exam and then using it to determine school ratings. It would be much cleaner for the exam to be created by a third party.

The TEA would create not only the end-of-year exam but also beginning- and middle-of-year exams. These are supposed to be shorter and diagnostic, providing results to teachers, students and parents within 48 hours -- but they would come from the TEA.

Now, it is true that school districts would not have to use the TEA-created exams for the beginning and middle of the year. They could, instead, contract with a third party -- say, the [Northwest Evaluation Association](https://substack.com/redirect/096ba2a6-f1f5-46de-9e4b-17c275e702d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which creates the MAP assessment -- for these diagnostic exams.

But here is the catch: The state would provide the TEA-created test at no cost, but districts that use third-party assessments would have to pay.

Given that many school districts are facing budget deficits, raising taxes and making difficult cuts, it's easy to see how they may choose the TEA-created test, even if it turns out to be inferior.

"Now we are putting on districts the stress of a state-created, essentially a STAAR test for the middle and the beginning as well as the end of the school year," state Rep. **Gina Hinojosa** , D-Austin, said during debate Tuesday.

This isn't what many families want. They want assessments, like MAP, that are norm-referenced and offered in a way that keeps stress low for children. And they want students, schools and districts rated in a way that truly accounts for academic growth and reflects the various ways schools serve communities through workforce development, after-school programming and engagement.

What's painful about HB8 is that it's a radical departure from [legislation House members passed almost unanimously during the regular session](https://substack.com/redirect/868121ac-1b28-448c-9680-e0de3bf2c93a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Lawmakers must know this is a significantly inferior bill. Or maybe they don't understand what they have approved?

No wonder state Rep. **Diego Bernal** , vice chair of the House Public Education Committee, voted against this bill.

"We're all about to vote for something that we don't fully understand, that we haven't vetted," Bernal said. "Let's push it back. Let's do a commission and get something we can all support."

Abbott should veto this bill. Students and families deserve better." [SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/8e96b88d-508b-4040-94db-d36ebb44a0cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

**" Minneapolis gunman appears to promote "Brandon Herrera for president" in video posted before shooting," **Houston Chronicle's **James Osborne** \-- "A person who appears to be the shooter who killed two and injured 17 at a Minneapolis church Wednesday praised Texas congressional candidate and gun activist **Brandon Herrera** in a video posted before the shooting.
