**" Bill to let AG prosecute election crimes heads to Abbott, but is it legal?" **Dallas Morning News' **Gromer Jeffers, Jr.** \-- "A bill that would allow the attorney general to prosecute Texas election fraud cases is headed for Gov. **Greg Abbott 's** desk, but it's unclear whether the proposed law is constitutional.

The legislation, approved by the House on Tuesday, would bypass restrictions in the Texas Constitution on the attorney general's ability to prosecute voter fraud cases. The power to prosecute such cases belongs to local district attorneys, a policy that was upheld four years ago when the all-Republican Court of Criminal Appeals ruled that the attorney general's office could not unilaterally prosecute cases involving voter fraud or other election-related crimes.

The court pointed to the separation of powers clause in the state constitution as the reason the attorney general's office could not prosecute election law crimes.

The legislation, approved Tuesday in the House by an 85-54 vote, was accompanied by a resolution that would put to voters the question of whether to change the state constitution to allow the attorney general such powers. But that resolution did not get the 100 votes needed for approval.

State Rep. **Matt Shaheen** , R-Plano and chairman of the House Elections Committee said the bill by itself meets the objective of changing the law even without the needed supermajority on the resolution. Shaheen authored the House legislation, which was identical to the Senate bill the House approved.

Shaheen said changing the Election Code to give the attorney general the power to prosecute election-related crimes was constitutional. Under Texas law, local district attorneys have the power to prosecute election crimes. The attorney general's office can be involved but only with the invitation of a district attorney.

Shaheen said the bill "replaces permissive language stating that the attorney general may prosecute with the mandatory language affirming that the attorney general has jurisdiction to prosecute." Specifically, language in the code changes from "may" to "shall," Shaheen said.

If constitutional, the change would flip the authority of prosecuting election law crimes from local district attorneys to the attorney general.

"By passing SB-12, the legislature ensures that Texas election laws are fully enforceable and that the criminal violations can be prosecuted," Shaheen said. "This legislation strengthens public confidence in Texas elections and safeguards the integrity of our democratic process."

The law falls short, however, of what Abbott outlined when he included the matter in special session agendas.

In his proclamation for the special sessions, Abbott asked lawmakers to consider "legislation proposing a constitutional amendment allowing the Attorney General to prosecute state election crimes."

A spokesperson for the governor declined to comment on the matter Tuesday. Shaheen said he was confident Abbott would sign the legislation.

Democrats blasted the bill as unconstitutional and unnecessary.

State Rep. **Joe Moody** , D-El Paso, said "our constitution wisely gave the keys to local prosecutors."

"This isn't a partisan issue. It's a political philosophy issue," Moody said. "It's something we need to take a long-term view on, because there's a jail cell at the end of that road."

Attorney**Ken Paxton** has long sought the power to prosecute election law cases. In 2024, he campaigned against three Court of Criminal Appeals judges who ruled that his office didn't have the power to prosecute election fraud. [They lost reelection bids.](https://substack.com/redirect/14ea2860-ed80-474c-b836-cf2311330ce3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Paxton is running in the 2026 Republican Senate primary against incumbent John Cornyn, so he would be in the attorney general's office in the first year of the proposed law. It would then be used by future attorneys general." [DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/b3f98390-cb8f-4951-b0a3-c90fb218b84d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

**" Harris County constables, sheriffs could contract with HOAs without commissioners' OK under bill heading to Abbott," **Texas Tribune's**Alex Nguyen** \-- "Two bills that focus solely on Harris County law enforcement agencies' contracting and funding advanced to the governor's desk, two days after being added to the second special session's agenda.

Currently, sheriffs and constables in Harris County can contract with homeowner associations, school districts and municipal utility districts to provide additional policing for them. Both the county and contracting groups have to sign off on the contract, and they split portions of the cost depending on the amount of time the deputies spend in the area.

The more prominent of the two proposals, [House Bill 26](https://substack.com/redirect/18e5b383-b2ee-4bfc-bbde-e3c74f0c936c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), would allow these law enforcement agencies to enter into such contracts without the need for approval from the county's commissioners court. Meanwhile, [House Bill 192](https://substack.com/redirect/fc9ca6c5-a866-4bc8-beb8-d1e679636bcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would require the county to seek voter approval if it adopts a budget that reallocates unspent funding that was appropriated for law enforcement agencies or moves funding previously appropriated for a specific law enforcement position to another agency.

State Rep. **Tom Oliverson** , the Cypress Republican who carried both bills, and his backers said they are about protecting law enforcement including this popular deputy contract program.

Their critics, however, said the legislation would upend the county government's checks and balances, as well as harm taxpayers.

"You already pay your taxes for a constable to patrol your neighborhoods. But now they want to go and bid a contract with your HOAs, to pay them, to contract with them, to patrol your neighborhood more often," state Rep. **Charlene Ward Johnson** , D-Houston, said during a Texas House hearing about HB 26 on Wednesday. "That's double taxation."

The House then cleared HB 26 with a 88-49 vote and HB 192 with a 89-48 vote early Wednesday afternoon. Hours later, the Texas Senate voted 21-5 to approve both bills. These proposals now head to the governor's desk.

The votes came two days after Gov.**Greg Abbott** added the items to the second special session's agenda on Monday, saying that the legislation would improve public safety. Oliverson quickly thanked the governor in[ a post on X](https://substack.com/redirect/6ddd1b31-286d-4139-8055-0f15bd925e6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for "protecting neighborhood law enforcement contracts for the vast majority of unincorporated Harris County and ISD's that depend on them."

Oliverson said the legislation is needed because the deputy contract program is under attack, despite its popularity and importance to unincorporated areas. The county also [discussed earlier this month ](https://substack.com/redirect/f16782c6-3f7f-426e-8ecf-6f3a2a3cd242?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)raising the contract's costs for some groups in order to help cover constable pay raises, the Houston Chronicle reported.

"Unfortunately, there's a lot of friction going on between the law enforcement departments and Commissioners Court with regards to the terms and conditions of those contracts," Oliverson said during a House committee hearing for HB 26 on Aug. 22.

The committee then heard testimony from **Tom Ramsey** , a Harris County commissioner who spoke about the importance of such a program to maintain public safety and growth in his precinct, which covers most of[ the county's unincorporated](https://substack.com/redirect/030b8245-c451-4bb9-b990-3c3f35591d08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) areas. It also received signed letters from all eight Harris County constables that show their bipartisan support for a proposal that would "remove [the program] from the threat of any volatile partisan whims of our Commissioners Court."

"Us going and negotiating directly with some of those neighborhoods that have been sorely overlooked all these years is going to be a great thing if this bill passes," Constable **Alan Rosen** , a Democrat, added in his testimony.

Some Harris County commissioners, however, told the Texas Tribune that they oppose the proposals.

Commissioner **Rodney Ellis** called the legislation part of the state's "ongoing war on local government," while Commissioner **Adrian Garcia** said the bills could create difficulties for maintaining other public safety initiatives and stressed that public safety shouldn't be about who can pay extra.

Garcia also warned that the proposed shift of control over the contracts could "cripple the county budget process."

"How are the 5 members of Commissioners Court expected to set a budget when in the middle of a fiscal year, 9 other independently elected officials could effectively set the whole county's budget because of these contracts," he said in a statement. "On a governance perspective, this legislation would be a budget killer."

The Tribune also reached out to the offices of Commissioner **Lesley Briones** and County Judge **Lina Hidalgo** , but didn't receive comments.

Meanwhile, some officials from other parts of Texas are already wary about the precedent that these proposals could set. They said state lawmakers could come back in future legislative sessions and add counties with fewer than 3.3 million people -- the bills' current threshold, which limits them to just Harris County.

"We defend, we don't defund," Rick Bailey, a Johnson County commissioner, told the Tribune. He registered against HB 26 but didn't testify. "But this has the potential to have some really negative effects on county budgets and local taxpayers."

Oliverson didn't respond to the criticism posed on the House floor on Wednesday. His office also didn't provide a comment in response to requests from the Tribune." Editorial: **" State lawmakers are expanding STAAR, not scrapping it. Abbott should veto.," **via San Antonio Express-News**** \-- "Gov. Greg Abbott has made eliminating STAAR, the state's almost universally loathed education assessment, [a top priority this summer](https://substack.com/redirect/bf5e4dd4-3ed1-4f68-8e01-d0136d149f5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

If he really believes the STAAR must go, then he should veto the legislation that state lawmakers have advanced.

[House Bill 8](https://substack.com/redirect/d02c5e44-2578-48e5-bb49-13ae86e197e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which the Texas House [passed Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/61e993d1-8e69-4804-bcb4-dd7118c0e9ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and its counterpart, [Senate Bill 9](https://substack.com/redirect/1dfe48d1-9d30-4a23-96ec-c778a4ea9af0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which has cleared the Senate Finance Committee, are much more likely to be an expansion of STAAR -- albeit under a new acronym -- than an elimination of high-stakes testing.

Why do we say this? After all, supporters of the House version, authored by state Rep. **Brad Buckley** , R-Salado, have argued that rather than administering one big high-stakes test at the end of the year, public schools, beginning with the 2027-28 school year, will administer three rounds of testing to track student progress. The bill also bans districts from additional benchmark testing, although districts could use outside tests such as iReady or MAP for the first two rounds of assessments.

Yes, and it's much more complicated than that. Stick with us.

To begin with, the bill continues the Texas Education Agency's creation and use of an end-of-year high-stakes exam, a key factor in determining A-F ratings for schools and districts.

This new end-of-year exam continues many of the disagreeable features of STAAR. Students will be measured by whether they approached, met or mastered grade-level skills, and they will be compared to state benchmarks, rather than norm-referenced standards.

One of the concerns public education experts have raised is the inherent conflict of the TEA creating the exam and then using it to determine school ratings. It would be much cleaner for the exam to be created by a third party.

The TEA would create not only the end-of-year exam but also beginning- and middle-of-year exams. These are supposed to be shorter and diagnostic, providing results to teachers, students and parents within 48 hours -- but they would come from the TEA.

Now, it is true that school districts would not have to use the TEA-created exams for the beginning and middle of the year. They could, instead, contract with a third party -- say, the [Northwest Evaluation Association](https://substack.com/redirect/87123df5-a655-4d48-885e-272c7baf23cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which creates the MAP assessment -- for these diagnostic exams.

But here is the catch: The state would provide the TEA-created test at no cost, but districts that use third-party assessments would have to pay.

Given that many school districts are facing budget deficits, raising taxes and making difficult cuts, it's easy to see how they may choose the TEA-created test, even if it turns out to be inferior.

"Now we are putting on districts the stress of a state-created, essentially a STAAR test for the middle and the beginning as well as the end of the school year," state Rep. **Gina Hinojosa** , D-Austin, said during debate Tuesday.

This isn't what many families want. They want assessments, like MAP, that are norm-referenced and offered in a way that keeps stress low for children. And they want students, schools and districts rated in a way that truly accounts for academic growth and reflects the various ways schools serve communities through workforce development, after-school programming and engagement.

What's painful about HB8 is that it's a radical departure from [legislation House members passed almost unanimously during the regular session](https://substack.com/redirect/7e0b5d6e-4b48-4dfe-8a16-cfb44923c703?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Lawmakers must know this is a significantly inferior bill. Or maybe they don't understand what they have approved?

**" Dallas property tax rate still up for discussion as council members look for wiggle room," **Dallas Morning News' **Everton Bailey, Jr.** \-- "For the [10th straight year, the Dallas City Council is considering lowering the property tax rate](https://substack.com/redirect/f588a25f-5724-479f-b1f4-3049958c80a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- even though many homeowners will still pay more due to rising home values and costs.

However, the exact new rate is still under discussion, as city officials continue to review a proposed $5.2 billion budget and gather public input before a final vote in mid-September. Council members suggested Wednesday that there may be some changes to the city manager's proposed rate.

Currently, the tax rate is 70.47 cents per $100**** valuation, and City Manager **Kim Tolbert 's** proposed budget for the coming year lowers the rate to 69.97 cents.

However, the City Council voted 10-5 on Wednesday to set a maximum possible rate at 70.22 cents -- still less than this year's rate but more than Tolbert's proposal. Council members said the move would give them wiggle room as they discuss the budget with their constituents.

Council members **Chad West** , **Zarin Gracey** , **Jaime Resendez** , **Laura Cadena** , **Adam Bazaldua** , **Lorie Blair** , **Paula Blackmon** , **Kathy Stewart** , **Bill Roth** , and Deputy Mayor Pro Tem **Gay Donnell Willis** voted in favor of the motion. Mayor **Eric Johnson** , Mayor Pro Tem **Jesse Moreno** and council members **Maxie Johnson** , **Cara Mendelsohn** and**Paul Ridley** voted against it.

Under Tolbert's proposed rate, a home valued at $382,010 -- with a $175,000 homestead exemption -- is projected to lower the average homeowner's tax bill by about $12.66 next year. But tax bills could still rise or fall depending on changes in home values.

Tolbert's proposed budget plan calls for a significant increase in funding for police and fire services amid cuts to city jobs, community pools, libraries, and other consolidations.

Council member **Adam Bazaldua** , who proposed the higher ceiling, argued that setting a lower bar could limit the council's ability to explore alternatives to some of the proposed cuts. If the council approves Tolbert's rate, the city would collect $11 million less in property taxes. If they stick with the proposed 70.22-cent ceiling, the loss would be about $5.5 million.

"I believe it would be preliminary for us to set a ceiling before having a discussion to see if there are potential viable options to save some of the cuts that were brought forth with this proposed budget," Bazaldua said.

The City Council scheduled a Sept. 17 public hearing at City Hall to gather residents' opinions on the tax rate before voting to finalize it and the citywide budget the same day. The new rate and budget would take effect on Oct. 1." [DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/3fb765e5-8799-48b6-bdd6-fe1416912eb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

**" TxDOT is about to open the tallest highway ramp in San Antonio," **AP's **Richard Webner** \-- "If you're a speed demon, the place to drive in South Texas is the Texas 130 toll road in Lockhart, with its 85 miles per hour limit. If you like scenic vistas, check out the country roads of the Hill Country.

But if it's pure height you yearn for -- as much air as possible between you and the ground --the Texas Department of Transportation has something new for you, right here in San Antonio.

On Thursday, TxDOT plans to open a flyover ramp at the interchange between Loop 1604 and Interstate 10 on the Northwest Side. At 128 feet high, the ramp will be the [tallest highway structure](https://substack.com/redirect/74edc786-c925-4d13-b298-67d50f4e586c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Alamo City, and among the tallest in Texas and the entire United States. At 128 feet, it's the height of a 12- or 13-story building.

Linking the westbound lanes of Loop 1604 with the eastbound lanes of I-10, the ramp is the third of eight super-tall flyovers planned at the new interchange. The first, at 123 feet, [opened in December](https://substack.com/redirect/4705f131-c5ac-4f28-9069-41f09f6eeb62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the second, at a puny 101 feet, debuted in June. Another is set to open later this year, and the entire interchange is expected to be complete in 2027, TxDOT said.

The new ramp is 11⁄2 miles long and was built with 10.8 million pounds of steel and more than 35,000 cubic yards of concrete, according to TxDOT.

The new interchange is phase two of TxDOT's $1.2 billion [Loop 1604 North Expansion Project](https://substack.com/redirect/19eb6ef8-53e0-4760-addd-a6dad40b140e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which will enlarge a 23-mile stretch of the highway, between Bandera Road and Interstate 35, from four to 10 lanes, with one high-occupancy vehicle lane -- i.e., carpool lane -- in each direction. It has six phases in all.

The project broke ground in 2021 after being mired for years in funding and environmental problems. TxDOT expects to complete it in 2028. It is designed to relieve the traffic congestion caused by the explosive population growth of San Antonio, especially on the far North Side.

It's unclear exactly where the new flyover ranks among the tallest highway structures in the U.S., but it appears to be near the top.

The ["High Five" interchange](https://substack.com/redirect/1e54e182-7457-423a-84d9-3632cd387246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between the Lyndon B. Johnson Freeway and the Central Expressway in Dallas soars to a maximum height of 140 feet, according to [Texas Monthly](https://substack.com/redirect/7affed7b-efa0-4187-99b1-6649d4e4f6f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A list maintained [by the blog Panethos](https://substack.com/redirect/4322443f-ca77-4fb0-8380-fadbe7396443?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) also ranks the interchange between Interstate 110 and Interstate 105 in Los Angeles as being taller than the new ramp, at 130 feet.

The [$463 million new interchange](https://substack.com/redirect/d9a45525-22b1-4ffe-8b45-06d9b0c59df7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between Loop 1604 and I-10 is replacing a "cloverleaf" built in the 1980s. It will feature a design known as the "Texas stack" in which five levels of roads - the access roads, the main lanes of both highways, and the ramps for both highways - are stacked on top of each other.

Cloverleaf ramps have come to be seen as outdated because their tightly curving ramps slow down traffic and create snags where drivers weave in and out, according to the infrastructure blog [Practical Engineering](https://substack.com/redirect/4466705f-ee8c-461f-a710-8095d1e25d82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

As part of the new interchange, the access roads underneath will be redrawn into a ["fidget spinner" format](https://substack.com/redirect/58163fd2-a600-473c-8302-e09b334b332a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with four partial roundabouts at their crossings, rather than traffic lights, according to Texas Highway Man, a website that closely tracks highway projects in San Antonio." [AP](https://substack.com/redirect/a47654b1-c809-4271-807c-6f736c40aa76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Upstream oil shed almost 3,000 jobs so far this summer. Here's what that might mean," **Houston Chronicle's **Rachel Nostrant** \-- "Texas [oil and gas field employment](https://substack.com/redirect/3c23b306-2e69-4367-b967-8046d2344201?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) slipped over the summer as crude prices hovered just above break-even levels and global supplies stayed abundant. Nearly 3,000 upstream workers, about 1.5% of the sector's workforce, lost their jobs in June and July, according to the Texas Workforce Commission.

The loss of jobs, after a modest increase earlier in the year, highlights a reckoning the oil and gas industry is expected to face if crude oil prices continue their recent downward trend, in addition to unbalanced global supply and demand, a volatile investment market and overall [industry consolidation](https://substack.com/redirect/37d06f6c-5a24-49c9-8856-36a052ff855e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

As a result, upstream workers have found themselves taking the brunt of the impacts, with approximately 1,500 jobs lost in June and another 1,400 in July.

Though the loss of about 3,000 jobs is statistically minor compared to the [63,000 lost](https://substack.com/redirect/0243c146-9dab-4b8e-bde8-49f485fa7bc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) through the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic, they evince what some experts say could be an impending down cycle for the industry.

Rig counts, drilling permits and the price of crude oil - all of which impact the upstream job market - have dropped over the last few months, said **Karr Ingham** , president of the Texas Alliance of Energy Producers.

The price of West Texas Intermediate crude dropped to $62.17 in May, its lowest point since mid-2023, when most economists say the industry made its comeback from the COVID-19 pandemic. Although prices ping-ponged throughout July and August, the price of the benchmark crude still hovers around $63, as of Aug. 26.

"Two months doesn't necessarily make a trend, for sure, but it kind of lines up with what we might expect," Ingham said, referencing the recent loss of jobs.

There has been relative job growth since 2023, so although the June and July losses do not seem close to the layoffs seen in COVID, the numbers do mark stagnation and the potential of more layoffs, Ingham said.

Several workers, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said they were struggling to find employment opportunities, both in on- and off-shore drilling operations. Some questioned whether they should seek work outside of the oil and gas field, while others said they were considering new areas of specialization that may better insulate them from a volatile job cycle.

Consolidation has led to a flurry of layoffs across all sectors of the industry over the past few months. Following its acquisition of Hess in July, Chevron announced it would be laying off [575 Hess](https://substack.com/redirect/0c1658bf-b19b-4e2a-89eb-799bf8eeb5e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) employees from the former company's Houston office. Encino Energy similarly announced plans in June to layoff 121 workers at its Houston base following the company's acquisition by EOG Resources the month prior.

Outsourcing of jobs such as information technology, accounting and security to countries with cheaper labor, such as India and Indonesia, have also seen Texas oil workers left by the wayside over the last few years.

While it may be difficult for office workers to anticipate layoffs, upstream workers should keep their eyes on the price of crude oil and the balance between the global demand for oil compared to the resource's supply over the next few months, Ingham said.

If prices average far lower in 2025 than they did in 2024, and rig counts continue to be generally relatively weak, layoffs would historically be expected to follow.

"The only question is, 'Are we actually headed for $50?'" Ingham said. "I hope not...I don't suspect we're going to get down that far, but none of us know the answer to that question right now."" * **TEXANS IN DC**

**" Elon Musk wants to build $760M tunnels under Houston. He's tapped a Texas congressman to make the pitch," **KUT's **Lauren McGaughy** and Houston Chronicle's **Yilun Cheng** \-- "The devastating flooding in Houston caused by Hurricane Harvey in 2017 killed dozens of people, inundated hundreds of thousands of homes and left the community desperate for a solution.

Since then, local flood experts have extensively studied the possibility of a multibillion-dollar tunnel system across Harris County. Studies have focused on the construction of pipelines, 30 to 40 feet in diameter, that could ferry massive amounts of water out to the Gulf in the event of a storm.

Now, after years of research and discussion, **Elon Musk** wants a piece of the project.

An investigation by The Texas Newsroom and the Houston Chronicle has found that the billionaire, in partnership with Houston-area Rep. **Wesley Hunt** , has spent months aggressively pushing state and local officials to hire Musk's Boring Co. to build [two narrower, 12-foot tunnels](https://substack.com/redirect/8eb069bb-e871-47c1-8d09-443022de15c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) around one major watershed. That could be a potentially cheaper, but, at least one expert said, less effective solution to the region's historic flooding woes.

Hunt's team has said the [Boring project would cost $760 million](https://substack.com/redirect/f951da0a-ce07-4562-a473-7708c7aaa071?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and involve the company getting 15% of the cost up front from state and local coffers.

Within two months of this push, the Harris County Commissioners Court unanimously voted to study a pilot program that included a look at smaller tunnels, with specifications similar to what Boring had pitched.

Both Musk and Hunt stand to benefit should Boring be selected to build any part of the project. Hunt is [reportedly considering a challenge](https://substack.com/redirect/96a73a45-75bc-4bc3-99c9-cff0b73015c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** in next year's Republican Senate primary. And landing a job like this would also be a significant win for Boring, which has not completed a major public project in Texas and faces criticisms for its [ventures elsewhere](https://substack.com/redirect/6ab68482-44ab-4512-b063-584040007eae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

The discussions about the Boring pitch have happened mostly out of the public eye. [Hunt mentioned the project](https://substack.com/redirect/9e90507a-1799-4672-adab-b6e6b289a02b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in passing at a town hall in Houston in February. Since then, he has refused to answer the newsrooms' questions about when Musk sold him on the idea and why he became its pitchman.

Efforts to reach Musk and representatives with Boring were not returned.

Experts and some local officials question whether Musk and his company are the right pick for the job. The Boring Co. has focused on transportation tunnels, not flood mitigation.

"If you build a smaller tunnel, OK, it'll be cheaper, but it can carry less water," said **Larry Dunbar** , a veteran water resources engineer who has advised Houston-area governmental agencies on drainage issues. "So what have you saved? Have you reduced the flooding upstream by an inch? And are you going to spend multimillions of dollars to do that? Well, maybe that's not worth it."

In response to the newsrooms' questions, state and local officials said no public money has been allocated to Boring. County officials added that they have not chosen a tunnel contractor and any process to do so would follow normal procurement rules.

Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** , [whose staff met with Hunt's team](https://substack.com/redirect/344771e4-a200-4a04-aeee-249819a3a7cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during the legislative session to discuss the proposal, remains open to the idea. As president of the Texas Senate with close ties to President**Donald Trump** , he is a powerful ally.

"If Elon Musk and the Boring Company, or any other company, can build two massive tunnels under the Houston bayous in a few years to save the city from flooding, I am always going to be interested to listen," Patrick, a Republican, told the newsrooms. "The truth is, Elon Musk is one of the only people in the world who could accomplish this."" * **TRUMP ADMINISTRATION**

**" Mystery surrounds $1.2 billion Army contract to build huge detention tent camp in Texas desert," **AP's **Michael Biesecker** and**Joshua Goodman** \-- "When President **Donald Trump 's** administration last month awarded a contract worth up to $1.2 billion to build and operate what it says will become [the nation's largest immigration detention complex](https://substack.com/redirect/5e34cc65-1818-43f1-8f7a-2b2d12aeb958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it didn't turn to a large government contractor or even a firm that specializes in private prisons.

Instead, it handed the project on a military base to Acquisition Logistics LLC, a small business that has no listed experience running a correction facility and had never won a federal contract worth more than $16 million. The company also lacks a functioning website and lists as its address a modest home in suburban Virginia owned by a 77-year-old retired Navy flight officer.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cca27941-f163-4140-a8ea-ea7bfadba2b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The mystery over the award only deepened last week as the new facility began to accept its first detainees. The Pentagon has refused to release the contract or explain why it selected Acquisition Logistics over a dozen other bidders to build the massive tent camp at Fort Bliss in west Texas. At least one competitor has filed a complaint.

The secretive -- and brisk -- contracting process is emblematic, experts said, of the government's broader rush to fulfill [the Republican president's pledge](https://substack.com/redirect/5c1f5876-3269-42f1-b19a-c76bb86f439f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to arrest and deport [an estimated 10 million migrants](https://substack.com/redirect/f26d3642-5c10-4c94-8336-eb9ec9a50eef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) living in the U.S. without permanent legal status. As part of that push, the government is turning increasingly to the military to handle tasks that had traditionally been left to civilian agencies.

A member of Congress who recently toured the camp said she was concerned that such a small and inexperienced firm had been entrusted to build and run a facility expected to house up to 5,000 migrants.

"It's far too easy for standards to slip," said Rep.**Veronica Escobar** , a Democrat whose district includes Fort Bliss. "Private facilities far too frequently operate with a profit margin in mind as opposed to a governmental facility."

Attorney**Joshua Schnell** , who specializes in federal contracting law, said he was troubled that the Trump administration has provided so little information about the facility.

"The lack of transparency about this contract leads to legitimate questions about why the Army would award such a large contract to a company without a website or any other publicly available information demonstrating its ability to perform such a complicated project," he said.

**Ken A. Wagner** , the president and CEO of Acquisition Logistics, did not respond to phone messages or emails. No one answered the door at his three-bedroom house listed as his company's headquarters. Virginia records list Wagner as an owner of the business, though it's unclear whether he might have partners.

Defense Secretary**Pete Hegseth** approved using Fort Bliss for the new detention center, and the administration has hopes to build more at other bases. A spokesperson for the Army declined to discuss its deal with Acquisition Logistics or reveal details about the camp's construction, citing the litigation over the company's qualifications.

The Department of Homeland Security, which includes U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, declined to answer questions about the detention camp it oversees.

Named Camp East Montana for the closest road, the facility is being built in the sand and scrub Chihuahuan Desert, where summertime temperatures can exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit and heat-related deaths are common. The 60-acre site is near the U.S.-Mexico border and the El Paso International Airport, a key hub for [deportation flights](https://substack.com/redirect/078cf85c-b6fe-477a-bc86-b3bebbd11b97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

The camp has drawn comparisons to ["Alligator Alcatraz,"](https://substack.com/redirect/401be5a2-2afa-4380-8004-ce57c580315b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a $245 million tent complex erected to hold ICE detainees in the Florida Everglades. That facility has been the subject of complaints about unsanitary conditions and lawsuits. A federal judge recently [ordered that facility to be shut down](https://substack.com/redirect/765d3bf1-66dc-453d-8eb7-a51eea415cee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

The vast majority of the roughly 57,000 migrants detained by ICE are housed at [private prisons](https://substack.com/redirect/3b435cbc-cb30-4278-a507-ae51c3c42e22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) operated by companies like Florida's Geo Group and Tennessee-based CoreCivic. As those facilities fill up, ICE is also exploring temporary options at military bases in California, New York and Utah.

At Fort Bliss, construction began within days of the Army issuing the contract on July 18. Site work began months earlier, before Congress had passed Trump's big tax and spending cuts bill, which includes a record $45 billion for immigration enforcement. The Defense Department announcement specified only that the Army was financing the initial $232 million for the first 1,000 beds at the complex.

Three white tents, each about 810 feet long, have been erected, according to satellite imagery examined by The Associated Press. A half dozen smaller buildings surround them." TOP NEWS " October hearing set on legality of new Texas congressional boundaries," Dallas Morning News' Gromer Jeffers, Jr. \-- "A federal judicial panel will hear arguments beginning Oct. 1 for an injunction against the implementation of by the Texas Legislature. According to three lawyers who were in the El Paso courtroom Wednesday when judges made the decision, the hearing on the congressional boundaries will take place from Oct. 1-10 in El Paso. That would allow enough time for the three-judge panel to make a decision on whether the maps are legal or violate the federal Voting Rights Act before the December filing deadline for the 2026 elections. A written order is expected to be released Thursday morning, the lawyers said. "They came up with the best time under the circumstances," said Gary Bledsoe , the president of the Texas NAACP and one of the group's lawyers. Bledsoe is also a lawyer for U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett , D-Dallas. "We think this is a case where the racial bias is just overt," Bledsoe said before getting on a flight back to Austin. A , filed hours after the map was approved by the Legislature, argues that the redistricting plan is discriminatory. State Rep. Matt Shaheen , R-Prosper and chairman of the House Elections Committee, said 2026 candidates would likely run under the new boundaries. "I have a high level of confidence that after further review the maps passed by the Texas Legislature will stand," Shaheen said. The new map, approved this month by the Legislature, will reconfigure Texas' congressional districts in an effort to turn five of them to Republican control from Democrat control. The redistricting was requested by President Donald Trump in an effort to shore up his Republican majority in Congress heading into the 2026 mid-term elections. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has said he plans to sign the bill into law. Bledsoe said Trump's request that Texas embark on mid-decade redistricting will be the center of the plaintiff's case. "Trump's letter will be exhibit No. 1," he said. The El Paso federal panel also held a trial in May over whether the 2021 legislative maps passed by the Texas Legislature are legal. It has yet to issue a ruling." " Uvalde school didn't release most of its shooting-related documents but says it was a mistake," AP's Juan A. Lozano \-- "The Uvalde school district released only a small fraction of the documents it said would be made public regarding the 2022 massacre, with district officials in the small Texas town saying this week it was an honest mistake that they were fixing. The mix-up was revealed during an Uvalde school board meeting on Monday when the attorney for the district said his law firm mistakenly failed to make public all documents as had been promised in a legal settlement. He blamed it on "reasons that are our firm's business, but it is our error." "We are not in any way trying to hide anything. We are not in any way trying to not release things," attorneyRobb Decker said. Earlier this month, the Uvalde Consolidated Independent School District following years of litigation. The school district had sought to withhold documents connected to the attack that killed , one of the deadliest school shootings in U.S. history. The in July to release all the district's records and end the lawsuit pursued by media organizations to make the information public. The botched release was another misstep for district leaders who have been criticized for fighting the lawsuit and not making this information public sooner. School district members on Monday regretted having to again apologize to family members of the victims and the community for an error following the shooting. The school district's police and other law enforcement agencies have also been heavily scrutinized for their as terrified students inside a classroom called 911 and parents begged officers to go in. Family members including Jesse Rizo , the uncle of 9-year-old victim Jackie Cazares and a member of the school board, were among those pushing to see the records. "There's no excuse for that sir," Rizo said. "You can call it a mistake, you can call it an error. It's a costly error, a very costly error." This week's revelation means that around nine of every 10 records and emails were not released on Aug. 11, when the school board had said it had made public all its records. Board members said about 26,000 more pages of documents and 8,600 more emails were expected to be released. More than 3,400 pages of the withheld documents were released as of Wednesday. Decker said all would be made available to the public by next week. Still, many of the documents released by Wednesday offered few new revelations." #TXLEGE " Bill to let AG prosecute election crimes heads to Abbott, but is it legal?" Dallas Morning News' Gromer Jeffers, Jr. \-- "A bill that would allow the attorney general to prosecute Texas election fraud cases is headed for Gov. Greg Abbott 's desk, but it's unclear whether the proposed law is constitutional. The legislation, approved by the House on Tuesday, would bypass restrictions in the Texas Constitution on the attorney general's ability to prosecute voter fraud cases. The power to prosecute such cases belongs to local district attorneys, a policy that was upheld four years ago when the all-Republican Court of Criminal Appeals ruled that the attorney general's office could not unilaterally prosecute cases involving voter fraud or other election-related crimes. The court pointed to the separation of powers clause in the state constitution as the reason the attorney general's office could not prosecute election law crimes. The legislation, approved Tuesday in the House by an 85-54 vote, was accompanied by a resolution that would put to voters the question of whether to change the state constitution to allow the attorney general such powers. But that resolution did not get the 100 votes needed for approval. State Rep. Matt Shaheen , R-Plano and chairman of the House Elections Committee said the bill by itself meets the objective of changing the law even without the needed supermajority on the resolution. Shaheen authored the House legislation, which was identical to the Senate bill the House approved. Shaheen said changing the Election Code to give the attorney general the power to prosecute election-related crimes was constitutional. Under Texas law, local district attorneys have the power to prosecute election crimes. The attorney general's office can be involved but only with the invitation of a district attorney. Shaheen said the bill "replaces permissive language stating that the attorney general may prosecute with the mandatory language affirming that the attorney general has jurisdiction to prosecute." Specifically, language in the code changes from "may" to "shall," Shaheen said. If constitutional, the change would flip the authority of prosecuting election law crimes from local district attorneys to the attorney general. "By passing SB-12, the legislature ensures that Texas election laws are fully enforceable and that the criminal violations can be prosecuted," Shaheen said. "This legislation strengthens public confidence in Texas elections and safeguards the integrity of our democratic process." The law falls short, however, of what Abbott outlined when he included the matter in special session agendas. In his proclamation for the special sessions, Abbott asked lawmakers to consider "legislation proposing a constitutional amendment allowing the Attorney General to prosecute state election crimes." A spokesperson for the governor declined to comment on the matter Tuesday. Shaheen said he was confident Abbott would sign the legislation. Democrats blasted the bill as unconstitutional and unnecessary. State Rep. Joe Moody , D-El Paso, said "our constitution wisely gave the keys to local prosecutors." "This isn't a partisan issue. It's a political philosophy issue," Moody said. "It's something we need to take a long-term view on, because there's a jail cell at the end of that road." AttorneyKen Paxton has long sought the power to prosecute election law cases. In 2024, he campaigned against three Court of Criminal Appeals judges who ruled that his office didn't have the power to prosecute election fraud. Paxton is running in the 2026 Republican Senate primary against incumbent John Cornyn, so he would be in the attorney general's office in the first year of the proposed law. It would then be used by future attorneys general." ($) " Harris County constables, sheriffs could contract with HOAs without commissioners' OK under bill heading to Abbott," Texas Tribune'sAlex Nguyen \-- "Two bills that focus solely on Harris County law enforcement agencies' contracting and funding advanced to the governor's desk, two days after being added to the second special session's agenda. Currently, sheriffs and constables in Harris County can contract with homeowner associations, school districts and municipal utility districts to provide additional policing for them. Both the county and contracting groups have to sign off on the contract, and they split portions of the cost depending on the amount of time the deputies spend in the area. The more prominent of the two proposals, , would allow these law enforcement agencies to enter into such contracts without the need for approval from the county's commissioners court. Meanwhile, would require the county to seek voter approval if it adopts a budget that reallocates unspent funding that was appropriated for law enforcement agencies or moves funding previously appropriated for a specific law enforcement position to another agency. State Rep. Tom Oliverson , the Cypress Republican who carried both bills, and his backers said they are about protecting law enforcement including this popular deputy contract program. Their critics, however, said the legislation would upend the county government's checks and balances, as well as harm taxpayers. "You already pay your taxes for a constable to patrol your neighborhoods. But now they want to go and bid a contract with your HOAs, to pay them, to contract with them, to patrol your neighborhood more often," state Rep. Charlene Ward Johnson , D-Houston, said during a Texas House hearing about HB 26 on Wednesday. "That's double taxation." The House then cleared HB 26 with a 88-49 vote and HB 192 with a 89-48 vote early Wednesday afternoon. Hours later, the Texas Senate voted 21-5 to approve both bills. These proposals now head to the governor's desk. The votes came two days after Gov.Greg Abbott added the items to the second special session's agenda on Monday, saying that the legislation would improve public safety. Oliverson quickly thanked the governor in for "protecting neighborhood law enforcement contracts for the vast majority of unincorporated Harris County and ISD's that depend on them." Oliverson said the legislation is needed because the deputy contract program is under attack, despite its popularity and importance to unincorporated areas. The county also the contract's costs for some groups in order to help cover constable pay raises, the Houston Chronicle reported. "Unfortunately, there's a lot of friction going on between the law enforcement departments and Commissioners Court with regards to the terms and conditions of those contracts," Oliverson said during a House committee hearing for HB 26 on Aug. 22. The committee then heard testimony from Tom Ramsey , a Harris County commissioner who spoke about the importance of such a program to maintain public safety and growth in his precinct, which covers most of areas. It also received signed letters from all eight Harris County constables that show their bipartisan support for a proposal that would "remove [the program] from the threat of any volatile partisan whims of our Commissioners Court." "Us going and negotiating directly with some of those neighborhoods that have been sorely overlooked all these years is going to be a great thing if this bill passes," Constable Alan Rosen , a Democrat, added in his testimony. Some Harris County commissioners, however, told the Texas Tribune that they oppose the proposals. Commissioner Rodney Ellis called the legislation part of the state's "ongoing war on local government," while Commissioner Adrian Garcia said the bills could create difficulties for maintaining other public safety initiatives and stressed that public safety shouldn't be about who can pay extra. Garcia also warned that the proposed shift of control over the contracts could "cripple the county budget process." "How are the 5 members of Commissioners Court expected to set a budget when in the middle of a fiscal year, 9 other independently elected officials could effectively set the whole county's budget because of these contracts," he said in a statement. "On a governance perspective, this legislation would be a budget killer." The Tribune also reached out to the offices of Commissioner Lesley Briones and County Judge Lina Hidalgo , but didn't receive comments. Meanwhile, some officials from other parts of Texas are already wary about the precedent that these proposals could set. They said state lawmakers could come back in future legislative sessions and add counties with fewer than 3.3 million people -- the bills' current threshold, which limits them to just Harris County. "We defend, we don't defund," Rick Bailey, a Johnson County commissioner, told the Tribune. He registered against HB 26 but didn't testify. "But this has the potential to have some really negative effects on county budgets and local taxpayers." Oliverson didn't respond to the criticism posed on the House floor on Wednesday. The United States Military is the strongest, finest armed force the world has ever known. Its purpose is to support and defend the Constitution and the people of this country, from our enemies, foreign and domestic.
#
Ladies and Gentlemen, this is Paul Eaton. Major General, U.S. Army, retired.
I want to try to impress upon you the significance of Donald Trump’s authoritarian decision to force the National Guard, and potentially the Active Duty United States Military, into law enforcement roles on American soil.
In short, the Military is not Donald Trump’s personal instrument. Commander in Chief he may be, but there are laws specifically aimed at restricting his personal direction of the Military for domestic purposes.
The most important of these is the Posse Comitatus Act of 1878. It draws a clear line between domestic law enforcement and the Military, and prohibits the use of federal military forces for domestic law enforcement - except by acts of Congress.
These restrictions are not modern; they go back thousands of years. The term “Crossing the Rubicon” endures from Ancient Rome as the transition point from Republic to Empire. Roman generals were forbidden from bringing standing armies into Italy, past the Rubicon river. They understood the danger of a military force posed against civilian leadership.
When Julius Caesar invaded Rome at the head of his army, when he crossed the Rubicon, he committed a treasonous act. The rest, as they say, is history.
The United States Military is the strongest, finest armed force the world has ever known. Its purpose is to support and defend the Constitution and the people of this country, from our enemies, foreign and domestic. When the military is used on our own soil, there is great danger that the line between countryman and enemy becomes blurred. We are seeing this already with masked ICE personnel executing indiscriminate mass sweeps that, at times, include US citizens and legal residents. Sweeps that are at times, performed brutally.
This is a perilous moment, but I continue to have great faith in the fine women and men serving in uniform. They are our neighbors, sons, daughters, parents, and siblings. They love this country, and its people. They swear an oath to support and defend our Constitution, and they take that oath seriously.
But as Donald Trump purges principled and experienced leaders and attempts to bend the military to his will, we must face reality with open eyes.
We must continue advocating, not only for ourselves, but for those who wear our country’s uniform. VoteVets does that work each and every day. And if you want to support that mission, please:

# Trump's Economy surges above all expectations
The U.S. **[economy surged at a 3.3%](https://substack.com/redirect/5f3be43f-9bfe-41ba-8e1d-a052f5bd4070?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** annualized pace in Q2 2025, exceeding forecasts, as robust consumer spending defied tariff uncertainties, signaling resilience amid global trade tensions, the Commerce Department reported Thursday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5f3be43f-9bfe-41ba-8e1d-a052f5bd4070?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Consumer Spending Drives Growth:** Personal consumption expenditures rose 1.6%, surpassing the initial 1.4% estimate, fueling economic expansion despite tariff-related concerns.
* **Trade Balance Boosts GDP:** Net exports added nearly 5 percentage points to Q2 growth, with exports declining less than expected at 1.3% versus the prior 1.8% estimate.
* **Slower Growth Expected Ahead:** Economists predict a slowdown to around 1.5% growth as tariffs impact consumer spending, with Q3 tracking at 2.2% per the Atlanta Fed.
* **Federal Reserve Monitors Demand:** Final sales to private domestic purchasers jumped 1.9%, a key demand indicator watched by the Fed, up from the previous 1.2% estimate.

# Nvidia beats earnings, stocks dip on guidance but investors buy the dip
Nvidia's stock dipped **[despite beating Q2 2026 earnings](https://substack.com/redirect/0017114b-2d9a-40bf-9cb3-06d85239304b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** expectations with $46.74 billion in revenue, as investors fretted over softer-than-expected data center sales, signaling intense scrutiny of the AI chip giant's growth trajectory.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/06fdc8ce-4741-4c1b-8882-1612c2e34e83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **Gaming Division Rebounds:** Nvidia's gaming sector reported $4.3 billion in sales, up 49% year-over-year, with GPUs now tuned to run OpenAI models on personal computers.
* **Robotics Growth Emerging:** The robotics division saw $586 million in sales, a 69% annual increase, positioning it as a key growth area despite its small share of Nvidia's business.
* **China Export Challenges:** No H20 chip shipments to China occurred due to U.S. export restrictions, impacting revenue, though a $180 million H20 inventory release boosted Q2 margins.

* **Key Candidates Emerge** : Potential successors include Fed Governors Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller, former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh, and former St. Louis Fed President Jim Bullard.
* **Fed Renovation Criticism** : Bessent criticized the Fed's $2.5 billion building renovation, questioning its priority given the institution's $100 billion annual operating losses.

# US Bank stocks soar as the prospect of September rate cuts becomes tantalizingly close
U.S. bank stocks soared to a **[three-year high Tuesday,](https://substack.com/redirect/7a72914f-c3db-4f77-b900-d4dbcdb2d583?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** fueled by hopes of Federal Reserve rate cuts in September, sparking a rally that echoes the industry's historic 1995 boom.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7a72914f-c3db-4f77-b900-d4dbcdb2d583?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bank Index Outperforms:** The KBW Nasdaq Bank Index, tracking 24 major U.S. banks, surged 32% over the past year, outpacing the S&P 500 and Nasdaq by 16 and 10 points, respectively.
* **Historical Parallels Drawn:** Analysts compare the current rally to 1995, when Fed rate cuts and bank mergers drove a multiyear banking boom, though today's market faces different competitive dynamics.
* **Fed 's Role Pivotal:** Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's recent Jackson Hole speech, signaling potential rate cuts, boosted bank stocks, as lower rates could ease pressure on lending margins.
* **Modern Challenges Emerge:** Increased competition from tech stocks and a consolidated banking sector distinguish today's rally from the 1990s, potentially limiting the duration of the current surge.

* * *
* * *
# Wall Street awaits Nvidia's Q2 Earnings report at market close with bated breath
In a bold move, the U.S. Commerce Department will **[publish GDP data on blockchain](https://substack.com/redirect/7fe73fef-b4ba-444b-81b5-ccec86915c21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , a first for federal agencies, aiming for tamper-proof transparency, announced Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick Tuesday at the White House.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7fe73fef-b4ba-444b-81b5-ccec86915c21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Blockchain Enhances Data Integrity:** Using blockchain ensures GDP data is immutable, reducing risks of manipulation and fostering trust in economic reporting.
* **Broader Government Adoption Planned:** The initiative may expand to other agencies, modernizing data distribution across federal systems once technical details are finalized.
* **Financial Markets Impact Expected:** Instant blockchain access to GDP data could stabilize markets by reducing information disparities and minimizing volatility from scheduled releases.
* **Aligns with Crypto Agenda:** The move supports President Trump's pro-crypto stance, building on a January 2025 executive order to advance digital asset innovation.

* * *
* * *
# California's High Speed Rail "boondoggle" just had another $175m cut from its budget
Amtrak's sleek **[NextGen Acela trains,](https://substack.com/redirect/f3a9ab2e-9287-45d6-bd76-8da8cc6b73b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** hitting 160 mph, debuted Thursday, linking D.C., New York, and Boston, as the Trump administration moves to reclaim Union Station's management to boost safety.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f3a9ab2e-9287-45d6-bd76-8da8cc6b73b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **New Trains Enhance Travel** : NextGen Acela offers 27% more seats, free high-speed Wi-Fi, USB ports, and modern amenities, with 28 trains set to roll out by 2027.
* **Economic Impact Significant** : Assembled in New York by Alstom, the fleet uses parts from 180 suppliers across 29 states, creating approximately 15,000 U.S. jobs.
* **Union Station Safety Focus** : Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy pushes for improved public safety at D.C.'s Union Station, aligning with Trump's crime crackdown in the capital.
* **Amtrak Faces Leadership Gap** : With no CEO named since March, Amtrak, led by President Roger Harris, navigates its modernization amid record passenger numbers last year.

Yesterday, our country failed our kids and I will not allow elected leaders to move on or forget this horror.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=1786%2E791427%2EzOt1PR)

Dear Friend,
Our Minneapolis community has suffered a heartbreaking tragedy.
Yesterday morning parents dropped their babies off at Annunciation Catholic School in Minneapolis to start their day in prayer, and only moments later got a call that will forever change their lives: A shooter had opened fire, taking two students’ lives and injuring over a dozen more.
The loss of life is unthinkable. As a mom and Minneapolis resident, my heart is utterly shattered. I will keep praying for all the families impacted by this tragedy. I am especially thinking of the two beautiful children who lost their lives in this senseless act of violence.
While we do not yet know all of the details of the shooter’s motivations, we do know that children and schools are all too often the victims of horrific gun violence in this country.
We cannot continue to fail our kids with the lack of federal action. It is beyond despicable that elected leaders are more concerned with appeasing the gun lobby than keeping our children safe. The horror that children and educators went through yesterday, while they were praying, should not have happened. I am committed to do everything I can to stop these tragedies from occurring ever again.
Yesterday our country failed our kids and I will not allow elected leaders to move on or forget this horror. That is my promise as the representative of this great Minneapolis community and someone who has fought for gun violence prevention legislation from the day I first began running for office.
In the meantime, if you are looking for a way to send help to the victims and their families, the Minneapolis Foundation has set up a text-to-donate line to raise money for relief efforts.
To donate, please text **ACF1** to **41444.**
Thank you in advance for any support you can show to our community today.
— Ilhan Omar

| | **Kevin Rinke Endorses Citizen-Only Voting Amendment, Calls It “The Most Important Issue” for 2026**
_Business leader says protecting election integrity is key to preserving the American Dream_******LANSING, MI** – Business leader and former gubernatorial candidate Kevin Rinke this week announced his strong endorsement of the Citizen Only Voting Amendment, calling it _“the most important issue”_ facing Michigan voters in 2026.
Rinke emphasized that protecting the integrity of Michigan’s elections is essential to safeguarding both the American Dream and the Michigan Dream. He stressed that citizens must have confidence that every ballot is cast legally and counted fairly in order to preserve faith in democracy for generations to come. Rinke made the announcement at a Republican delegate event in Shelby Township.
“My dead father got five ballots last election. My dead mother got three. My dead father-in-law got multiple ballot applications. That’s wrong. We need elections that people can believe in. One vote, one citizen—that’s how our system is supposed to work. When that trust is broken, our democracy is at risk. We are the greatest republic and the greatest melding of freedom in the history of the world. But if we give that away, we won’t get it back—it will be ten times harder to restore. Citizen-only voting is the most important issue. Before I put myself out there in any other capacity, this is the fight that matters most.” Rinke said.
The Citizen Only Voting amendment will ensure that Michigan’s elections are reserved exclusively for American citizens, restoring confidence in the system and preventing abuse.
“This amendment is about protecting the American Dream—and the Michigan Dream—for our children and grandchildren,” Rinke said. “Faith in our elections is the foundation of our freedoms. Without it, everything else crumbles.”
The Citizens Only Voting initiative continues to gather support from grassroots activists, business leaders, candidates and elected officials across the state. If you haven’t already done so, please reach out and join our movement.

This seems like something out of a twisted novel, folks, but the new top voting lawyer at the Department of Justice was until recently an attorney and activist for a leading anti-voting legal group that has worked for years to spread fear about unproven illegal voting and press election officials to implement stricter, suppressive voting rules.
The lawyer, Maureen Riordan, worked side-by-side with Cleta Mitchell — the right-wing activist who played a key role in President Donald Trump’s failed bid to subvert the results of the 2020 election — following Mitchell’s pledge to “ reclaim our election systems from the left. ”
This appointment, along with the posting of Trump campaign lawyer and election denier Harmeet Dhillon as head of the Civil Rights division, shows how DOJ has gone from a largely consistent defender of voting rights to instead working actively to undermine our fundamental rights.
Again, are we surprised? No. But these moves from the administration highlight how badly we need to fight for our fundamental rights as citizens , from the outside of government.

body:

#

Team, when I accepted the job as Vice Chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, I knew we had our work cut out for us.
But now the President of the United States is attacking the right to vote. He’s trying to put an end to voting by mail, something used safely and securely by millions and millions of people.
As Vice Chair, I’m doing whatever I can to support Senate candidates and help them win their races. With these attacks on our elections, that work is more important than ever.
We’re going to fight for every vote, and I’m ready to do it. But I need your help to raise the resources we’ll need to win.

body:
A Simple Gift That Brought My Grandpa Back to the Table

| | |
---
| | |
# THURSDAY, AUGUST 28, 2025
---|---
**Good Afternoon!** Two weeks ago, our founder Guy decided to try something simple--he handed his dad a pair of [Oricle Hearing Aids](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD-v2yAQwD8N3hKZg9h4YHhSaqnD69oRneFweCIQAY7Vb1_ZHSp17va7P7_T3f38NJ8YYkjrD3ySbj4bRy5YbORMor1Gao2KWQsm98Kv8LSYHoRlq7hiSAZ6uF16dQFl_BbjX5l3TnsiINGR5uNtkL1UcOse2lvBR5ID2BtOiyLyI7cCYAGYFiehC_qY2itQXHEh5VX5YXILSInC2wVHJntyoeVy_cohtQf5-Cu_qVxtfnZRP1p7VSY-GMwM5n3fryu1XIKNdHQwmGvLherFbyXkrV7IMzEb8qYVTBVtCzmZ4Ji4MxjyCZxPDIbt5EmO_-TR-zMCIRgMdVs4E_f7t0P_mL_f_1S6ot1rDzGGOhwnrE8M8Vy5_d_HvzX8DgAA__9oE5qP). None of us expected what came next. After years of sitting quietly at the table, Grandpa Jim was suddenly back--laughing at the right moments, catching every word, and even telling us to quiet down because he could hear so well. What started as a small gift quickly became a story we had to share. -- Cole, _CEO_
* * *
[](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD-v2yAQwD8N3hKZg9h4YHhSaqnD69oRneFweCIQAY7Vb1_ZHSp17va7P7_T3f38NJ8YYkjrD3ySbj4bRy5YbORMor1Gao2KWQsm98Kv8LSYHoRlq7hiSAZ6uF16dQFl_BbjX5l3TnsiINGR5uNtkL1UcOse2lvBR5ID2BtOiyLyI7cCYAGYFiehC_qY2itQXHEh5VX5YXILSInC2wVHJntyoeVy_cohtQf5-Cu_qVxtfnZRP1p7VSY-GMwM5n3fryu1XIKNdHQwmGvLherFbyXkrV7IMzEb8qYVTBVtCzmZ4Ji4MxjyCZxPDIbt5EmO_-TR-zMCIRgMdVs4E_f7t0P_mL_f_1S6ot1rDzGGOhwnrE8M8Vy5_d_HvzX8DgAA__9oE5qP) We've always joked in our family that Grandpa Jim had "selective hearing." Ask him to help with dishes, and suddenly he didn't hear a word. Start talking about football, and he was all ears. But lately, it wasn't a joke anymore. At family dinners, he'd smile and nod--but you could tell he wasn't really following. He'd mishear questions. He'd laugh at the wrong moments. Eventually, he'd just go quiet. It hurt to watch. And if you've seen a loved one slowly drift out of conversations--not because they're checked out, but because they can't hear--you know what I mean. We tried everything. His old hearing aids? He hated them. Said they were uncomfortable and squealed too much. The batteries? He never replaced them. New hearing aid options? Too expensive, too complicated, not interested. [Then I came across Oricle Hearing Aids](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD-v2yAQwD8N3hKZg9h4YHhSaqnD69oRneFweCIQAY7Vb1_ZHSp17va7P7_T3f38NJ8YYkjrD3ySbj4bRy5YbORMor1Gao2KWQsm98Kv8LSYHoRlq7hiSAZ6uF16dQFl_BbjX5l3TnsiINGR5uNtkL1UcOse2lvBR5ID2BtOiyLyI7cCYAGYFiehC_qY2itQXHEh5VX5YXILSInC2wVHJntyoeVy_cohtQf5-Cu_qVxtfnZRP1p7VSY-GMwM5n3fryu1XIKNdHQwmGvLherFbyXkrV7IMzEb8qYVTBVtCzmZ4Ji4MxjyCZxPDIbt5EmO_-TR-zMCIRgMdVs4E_f7t0P_mL_f_1S6ot1rDzGGOhwnrE8M8Vy5_d_HvzX8DgAA__9oE5qP)--a simple, affordable solution that seemed like it might actually work. No appointments. No fittings. No messing with batteries. Just open the box, charge them up, and go. I ordered a pair for him. When they arrived, I handed them over and said, "Just try them for dinner tonight." And he did. That night at dinner, he didn't just hear us--he joined us. He caught a joke from my niece and laughed at the right moment. He answered a question from across the table. He chimed in on a story from the '70s without us needing to repeat the whole thing. Later he told me, "I didn't realize how much I was missing." In fact, he heard so clearly he was telling people to _quiet down_ because the table suddenly felt too loud. And before the night was over, he'd already asked me to order extra pairs--just so he'd have backups in case he misplaced them. That's the thing. Hearing loss doesn't happen all at once--it creeps in slowly. One missed word at a time. And then one day, someone just stops participating. But with these, he was right back in the mix. [**What makes Oricle different?**](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD-v2yAQwD8N3hKZg9h4YHhSaqnD69oRneFweCIQAY7Vb1_ZHSp17va7P7_T3f38NJ8YYkjrD3ySbj4bRy5YbORMor1Gao2KWQsm98Kv8LSYHoRlq7hiSAZ6uF16dQFl_BbjX5l3TnsiINGR5uNtkL1UcOse2lvBR5ID2BtOiyLyI7cCYAGYFiehC_qY2itQXHEh5VX5YXILSInC2wVHJntyoeVy_cohtQf5-Cu_qVxtfnZRP1p7VSY-GMwM5n3fryu1XIKNdHQwmGvLherFbyXkrV7IMzEb8qYVTBVtCzmZ4Ji4MxjyCZxPDIbt5EmO_-TR-zMCIRgMdVs4E_f7t0P_mL_f_1S6ot1rDzGGOhwnrE8M8Vy5_d_HvzX8DgAA__9oE5qP)
* Rechargeable (no tiny batteries to replace)
* Discreet (he's not self-conscious wearing them)
* Clear sound quality (especially for voices)
* Comfortable (no high-pitched squealing or irritation)

And the price? Way less than traditional hearing aids--without needing a prescription or appointment. I honestly wish we'd found these sooner. If someone you care about is struggling to keep up with conversations, this could make a bigger difference than you think. 👉 [**[Click here to check out Oricle]**](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD-v2yAQwD8N3hKZg9h4YHhSaqnD69oRneFweCIQAY7Vb1_ZHSp17va7P7_T3f38NJ8YYkjrD3ySbj4bRy5YbORMor1Gao2KWQsm98Kv8LSYHoRlq7hiSAZ6uF16dQFl_BbjX5l3TnsiINGR5uNtkL1UcOse2lvBR5ID2BtOiyLyI7cCYAGYFiehC_qY2itQXHEh5VX5YXILSInC2wVHJntyoeVy_cohtQf5-Cu_qVxtfnZRP1p7VSY-GMwM5n3fryu1XIKNdHQwmGvLherFbyXkrV7IMzEb8qYVTBVtCzmZ4Ji4MxjyCZxPDIbt5EmO_-TR-zMCIRgMdVs4E_f7t0P_mL_f_1S6ot1rDzGGOhwnrE8M8Vy5_d_HvzX8DgAA__9oE5qP) Whether it's your dad, your grandpa, or your spouse--getting back into the rhythm of everyday conversation is more than a quality-of-life upgrade. clean_body: A Simple Gift That Brought My Grandpa Back to the Table | | | | | | THURSDAY, AUGUST 28, 2025 ---|--- Good Afternoon! Two weeks ago, our founder Guy decided to try something simple--he handed his dad a pair of . None of us expected what came next. After years of sitting quietly at the table, Grandpa Jim was suddenly back--laughing at the right moments, catching every word, and even telling us to quiet down because he could hear so well. What started as a small gift quickly became a story we had to share. -- Cole, CEO We've always joked in our family that Grandpa Jim had "selective hearing." Ask him to help with dishes, and suddenly he didn't hear a word. Start talking about football, and he was all ears. But lately, it wasn't a joke anymore. At family dinners, he'd smile and nod--but you could tell he wasn't really following. He'd mishear questions. He'd laugh at the wrong moments. Eventually, he'd just go quiet. It hurt to watch. And if you've seen a loved one slowly drift out of conversations--not because they're checked out, but because they can't hear--you know what I mean. We tried everything. His old hearing aids? He hated them. Said they were uncomfortable and squealed too much. The batteries? He never replaced them. New hearing aid options? Too expensive, too complicated, not interested. simple, affordable solution that seemed like it might actually work. No appointments. No fittings. No messing with batteries. Just open the box, charge them up, and go. I ordered a pair for him. When they arrived, I handed them over and said, "Just try them for dinner tonight." And he did. That night at dinner, he didn't just hear us--he joined us. He caught a joke from my niece and laughed at the right moment. He answered a question from across the table. He chimed in on a story from the '70s without us needing to repeat the whole thing. Later he told me, "I didn't realize how much I was missing." In fact, he heard so clearly he was telling people to quiet down because the table suddenly felt too loud. And before the night was over, he'd already asked me to order extra pairs--just so he'd have backups in case he misplaced them. That's the thing. Hearing loss doesn't happen all at once--it creeps in slowly. One missed word at a time. And then one day, someone just stops participating. But with these, he was right back in the mix. Rechargeable (no tiny batteries to replace) Discreet (he's not self-conscious wearing them) Clear sound quality (especially for voices) Comfortable (no high-pitched squealing or irritation) And the price? Way less than traditional hearing aids--without needing a prescription or appointment. I honestly wish we'd found these sooner. If someone you care about is struggling to keep up with conversations, this could make a bigger difference than you think. 👉 [[Click here to check out Oricle]**]() Whether it's your dad, your grandpa, or your spouse--getting back into the rhythm of everyday conversation is more than a quality-of-life upgrade. It's a reconnection. Grandpa Jim is back in the conversation. And honestly? Dinner feels a lot better because of it. | | The Flyover, LLC 1910 Thomes Ave. Cheyenne WY 82001 | ---|---

| Hi there – it’s Haley.

I can’t wait to tell you all about my _Made in Michigan_ tour. But first, I need to ask: [_**Will you chip in $25 right now – split between my campaign and Hillary Scholten’s – to help us hit August's $10,000 fundraising goal?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114174097/566184276/-873513011?refcode=BLU_EM_HSC_2025-08-28_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzY4MmUxZS0zYjg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cFVtlvxcx_Zh-WedoyD8rz2q5we-UlwskoIWnpU1X3Y=)

I’ve got to tell you nothing makes me prouder to be from Michigan than meeting the people who make this state what it is: Hardworking, tough-as-nails, and full of heart.

**We were made in Michigan. And we’re proud of it.**

I grew up surrounded by grit and grease – my family ran a landscaping business, and my dad was a teacher in Detroit public schools. That’s where I learned the values of hard work, perseverance, and to always fight for what’s right.

I’ve fought for Michiganders my whole career – from helping lead the auto rescue that helped save over 200,000 Michigan jobs, to flipping a red seat blue in 2018, to delivering for working families in Congress.

Now, I’m running for Senate, and we’re facing our biggest challenge yet: Donald Trump just endorsed my opponent, MAGA Republican Mike Rogers. And a GOP super PAC has already raised $5 million to support him.

_The Hill_ even named Michigan one of the top five Senate seats most likely to flip, and experts say Senate control could be decided by our battleground race.

clean_body: The full force of the GOP and their megadonors are coming after Haley as a TOP target for defeat. | Hi there – it’s Haley. I can’t wait to tell you all about my Made in Michigan tour. We were made in Michigan. And we’re proud of it. I grew up surrounded by grit and grease – my family ran a landscaping business, and my dad was a teacher in Detroit public schools. That’s where I learned the values of hard work, perseverance, and to always fight for what’s right. I’ve fought for Michiganders my whole career – from helping lead the auto rescue that helped save over 200,000 Michigan jobs, to flipping a red seat blue in 2018, to delivering for working families in Congress. Now, I’m running for Senate, and we’re facing our biggest challenge yet: Donald Trump just endorsed my opponent, MAGA Republican Mike Rogers. And a GOP super PAC has already raised $5 million to support him. The Hill even named Michigan one of the top five Senate seats most likely to flip, and experts say Senate control could be decided by our battleground race. I know the stakes. | | Patriot, In the Air Force, I learned that strength and readiness were the keys to peace. America has always led the world because we invest in our men and women in uniform and give them the tools to succeed.

I am Lt. Col. David Flippo (Ret.), a 24-year combat veteran, and I am running for Congress because I believe America must remain the strongest, most capable force for freedom on earth. Our troops deserve nothing less than the best technology, the best training, and the best support this nation can provide.

When America leads with strength, our families are safe, our allies are secure, and America’s enemies are less aggressive.

Hi, it's Oregon Secretary of State, Tobias Read.
I just published a major op-ed in MSNBC because I feel a responsibility to speak out as Oregon’s top elections official.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250826em-msnbc-pet [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250826em-msnbc-pet]
Here’s what's going on:
* Oregon has run all of its elections through the mail for more than 25 years.

* Voting by mail is safe, fair, accurate — and voters across the political spectrum love it.

* Fraud is essentially nonexistent. Ballots are verified with forensic signature matching and overseen by bipartisan boards.

* Last fall, more than 75% of Oregonians cast a ballot — one of the highest participation rates in the country.

President Trump has threatened to eliminate it altogether through executive order. That would be unconstitutional, costly, and dangerous for our democracy.
I made it clear in my MSNBC article: If Congress and the president want to make our elections more secure, they should be expanding vote-by-mail, not shutting it down. And if President Trump tries to impose his executive order, Oregon is prepared to challenge it in court.
But I need the power of the people on my side. Will you add your name today to stand with me and defend vote-by-mail? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/auG4lmiVq06681BB7gmzfw2]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/auG4lmiVq06681BB7gmzfw2]
Together, we can send a powerful message: our democracy belongs to the people, not to presidents who want to undermine it for political gain.
More to come,
Tobias Read
