| Peter, every single day since he took office in January, it seems like Donald Trump has found new ways to abuse his power and make life harder for our families. He’s illegally withheld funding that New Jerseyans rely on for child care, for health care, and for access to healthy food. He’s deployed the National Guard to American cities in a transparent attempt to instill terror and fear. He signed a devastating spending bill that guts Medicaid access and makes everything from groceries to heating your home less affordable — all to give billionaires a giant tax cut. And honestly, that’s just a fraction of it. As Trump has inflicted all this damage on our country, Republican politicians like Jack Ciattarelli have cheered him on every step of the way. There is seemingly nothing Trump can do — no matter how illegal, reckless, or outright devastating for New Jersey families — that would make Jack Ciattarelli say “enough is enough.” And Peter, polls show that Ciattarelli is within a few percentage points of becoming New Jersey’s next governor. If we’re going to win that race and prevent that from happening, we need to work night and day these next 10 weeks to get our message out. I intend to do exactly that, Peter — because the stakes for New Jersey, and for our nation, are too high to give it anything less. But I can’t win this race without your help. Donald Trump just went on Truth Social and called for me to be prosecuted.
Why? Because I led his first impeachment. Because I’ve held him accountable. Because I haven’t stopped. And I never will. This is just Trump’s latest attempt at political retaliation against his perceived enemies.

I’m not surprised that Trump is lashing out again. But even by his standards, this one’s weak. And as much as Trump may hope, this latest smear will not distract from his Epstein files problem.

Adam

#### **Phil Izon's efforts against RCV demonstrate significant accomplishments:**
• **Authored and Sponsored Repeal Legislation:** He personally **wrote the bill to repeal RCV** in his living room, based on returning election laws to their pre-2022 state. He secured **180 sponsors for his initial legislation** , including former Governor Sarah Palin, who was the first to sign, along with former lieutenant governors and former state senators.• **Led a Historic Grassroots Signature Drive:** Izon initiated and led a **"volunteer" signature-gathering campaign** with over 700 volunteers. He personally collected over 2,000 signatures. The campaign submitted approximately **42,000 signatures** to the Alaska Division of Elections, far exceeding the 26,705 required.• **Achieved Ballot Qualification:** His efforts resulted in the certification of **37,043 signatures** , meeting the necessary district-wide thresholds to place the repeal measure on the 2024 ballot.• **Secured Legal Victories Against Challenges:** The repeal measure **"successfully defended the ballot measure with unanimous victories in both the Alaska Superior Court and the Alaska Supreme Court"** against attempts to disqualify it. This involved facing legal challenges regarding signature collection integrity. He specifically states he **"dealt with 2 hours of testimony and 6 hours of deposition to win those cases"****If I had made mistakes on the petition process which I was 100% Responsible for the submission and management of. Then we would not have won the Superior Court and Supreme Court Cases, if my team did not create technology solutions to screen for fraudulent books, we would not have won these cases. It was great management and a great team that won these court cases, ignoring these very important contributions is a slap in the face to me and to my team.** • **Established a National Educational Platform:** He founded the **Ranked Choice Education Association, RCValert.org, RemoveRCV.com, and NoRCV.com** , a group of national organizations providing educational resources to multiple states, including a 30-part animated video series RCV Election Simulators, Interactive Guidebook, Chatbots, and more, to inform the public about RCV's perceived flaws.• **Published Extensive Research:** Izon authored books such as "Rank Choice Voting Illusions of Choice" and "(manufactured) Majority," which delve into the history, funding, and real-world impacts of RCV, particularly in Alaska.• **Advocated and Influenced Across the Nation:** He has become a prominent **national expert against RCV** , delivering presentations and debates to presidential candidates, U.S. Congressional members, state legislators in over 35 states, and multiple secretaries of state. Even debated 3 Oregon Legislative members, 3 Alaska Legislative members, and U.S. Presidential Candidate Chase Oliver on RCV.• **Contributed to RCV Rejections in Other States:** His advocacy is credited with **helping prevent the adoption of RCV in six other states** and inspiring national debates about the system.• **Persisted Despite Overwhelming Odds:** His campaign was **outspent by a margin of 100-to-1** , with opponents contributing approximately $15 million compared to his group's fraction of a million, yet he only lost by a "razor-thin margin" of 0.1% (743 votes).

The campaign submitted approximately 42,000 signatures to the Alaska Division of Elections, far exceeding the 26,705 required.• Achieved Ballot Qualification: His efforts resulted in the certification of 37,043 signatures , meeting the necessary district-wide thresholds to place the repeal measure on the 2024 ballot.• Secured Legal Victories Against Challenges: The repeal measure "successfully defended the ballot measure with unanimous victories in both the Alaska Superior Court and the Alaska Supreme Court" against attempts to disqualify it. This involved facing legal challenges regarding signature collection integrity. He specifically states he "dealt with 2 hours of testimony and 6 hours of deposition to win those cases"If I had made mistakes on the petition process which I was 100% Responsible for the submission and management of. Then we would not have won the Superior Court and Supreme Court Cases, if my team did not create technology solutions to screen for fraudulent books, we would not have won these cases. It was great management and a great team that won these court cases, ignoring these very important contributions is a slap in the face to me and to my team. • Established a National Educational Platform: He founded the Ranked Choice Education Association, RCValert.org, RemoveRCV.com, and NoRCV.com , a group of national organizations providing educational resources to multiple states, including a 30-part animated video series RCV Election Simulators, Interactive Guidebook, Chatbots, and more, to inform the public about RCV's perceived flaws.• Published Extensive Research: Izon authored books such as "Rank Choice Voting Illusions of Choice" and "(manufactured) Majority," which delve into the history, funding, and real-world impacts of RCV, particularly in Alaska.• Advocated and Influenced Across the Nation: He has become a prominent national expert against RCV , delivering presentations and debates to presidential candidates, U.S. Congressional members, state legislators in over 35 states, and multiple secretaries of state. subject: The Mountain Minute: 8/28/2025
body:
The special session leaves Polis with a $783M deficit — here’s how he can fix it without new taxes
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
In case you haven't heard, Charlie Kirk is coming to Colorado State University! Get your tickets [HERE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) before it's too late. Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Fremont County native Gregory Carlson, a nationally known parliamentarian, launched his [bid for county commissioner](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), vowing to address affordability and housing. In Littleton, [Xcel admitted a tech oversight](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) caused repeated summer outages and promised fixes. Denver moved to [dismiss a Trump administration lawsuit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over its immigration policies, insisting it follows federal law.
At the Capitol, Democrats touted progress from the special session on the $1.2 billion budget gap, while Republicans argued it [worsened the crisis](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). District 51 celebrated [strong gains in statewide test scores](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), and concerns mounted as the Northern Integrated Supply Project’s [cost jumped to $2.7 billion](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), prompting a major water district to pull out.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** A shooting at Minneapolis’ Annunciation Catholic School [left 20 people injured](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), though police confirmed the shooter is deceased. In Washington, Trump announced [raising $1.5 billion since returning to the White House](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as he gears up for the 2026 midterms. Meanwhile, Democrats denounced his appointment of Heather Honey to a [DHS election integrity role](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), calling her a conspiracy theorist, while Republicans praised her scrutiny of the system.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Commentators voiced sharp frustration with Colorado’s direction. C. J. Garbo called himself a [“political refugee”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) leaving the state under one-party rule. Another criticized Sen. Sullivan’s remark that [new gun restrictions were “just another form,”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as sheriffs warn of crippling costs. On the budget, critics said the special session only[ “fixed a third and punted two-thirds,”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) while others urged [balancing without new taxes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—by cutting green energy subsidies, reviving fossil fuels, and reducing government overhead.
This is the Mountain Minute for Thursday, August 28, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[The special session leaves Polis with a $783M deficit — here’s how he can fix it without new taxes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RUSS MINARY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Governor Polis recently called—and lawmakers have now concluded—a special session aimed at addressing the estimated State budget deficit of $1.2 to 1.6 BILLION. That means that every man, woman and child in CO has to pay $208 more this year. That’s in addition to all of the other current local, county, state, sales and special district taxes they are already paying. But kids don’t pay taxes; adults do. I think CO taxpayers and citizens already pay enough in taxes._
_While lawmakers passed roughly $300 million in tax changes during the session, the ball is now in Gov. Polis’ court. He has been given authority to sign the bills and make deep spending cuts, up to $300 million, to close the remaining $783 million gap._
_Rather than addressing the real underlying causes and finding ways to cut taxes or reduce costs, State officials blame TABOR or the Trump administration for withholding Federal funding. Irresponsible and out of control spending has put CO in this hole. I and many other CO taxpayers are tired of being treated like an ATM when the State needs more money. Enough is enough._
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[A political refugee in Colorado: The painful choice to leave my homeland](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Author C.J. Garbo announced he and his family are leaving Colorado, calling themselves “political refugees” driven out by one-party rule that silences their values and faith.
* He argues Colorado’s government forces taxpayers to bankroll policies he opposes—funding abortion, drugs, homelessness, and benefits for non-citizens—while disregarding conservative voices.
* Garbo warns that unless Republicans unify around core values, more families will follow his lead, taking their dollars and livelihoods to states where liberty and faith are respected.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Senator Sullivan’s “just another form” gun law remark goes unchecked by media as sheriffs warn of crippling costs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY CORY GAINES, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Senator Sullivan dismissed Colorado’s new gun law as “just another form,” a remark critics say the media let slide without scrutiny.
* Western Slope sheriffs warn the law creates costly, unfunded mandates—diverting limited staff and resources from core public safety duties.
* Colorado Parks and Wildlife must develop the training and database system, using $1.4 million from its own fund, but officials admit the money won’t offset sheriff expenses and gun owners will ultimately bear the costs.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

** ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[From silence to the mic: Why young conservatives say CSU’s TPUSA event matters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | AUGUST 28** _Turning Point USA is bringing Charlie Kirk and the American Comeback Tour to Colorado State University (CSU) on Sept. 18. The chapter will host two events that day—a midday “Prove Me Wrong” debate session and an evening program at the Lory Student Center Ballrooms. Doors open at 5:30 p.m., with priority seating for CSU students, though community members are also welcome. Registration is required and first come, first served._
__

**[Dear Common Sense: What exactly is common sense?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 28** _Dear Common Sense, What exactly is common sense? People talk about it like it’s supposed to be obvious, but honestly, it feels like it’s in short supply these days. Is it just street smarts, or something deeper? Your’s truly, Done with Non-Sense._ __

**[From farm kid to parliamentarian: Gregory Carlson launches Fremont County commissioner bid](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | AUGUST 22** _Gregory Carlson, a Fremont County native known nationally for his work as a parliamentarian, announced his candidacy for District 2 commissioner on Aug. 26 at the Republican meeting in Florence. “After prayerful consideration and the support of my family and friends, I am excited to announce my candidacy for County Commissioner,” Carlson shared in a media release._
__

name: Barack Obama
subject: This is a power grab, and it threatens our democracy

body:
We’re witnessing an egregious, partisan power grab, but we are not powerless to stop it.
|
---

Peter, what’s happening in Texas right now demands our attention.
What we’re witnessing right now is a power grab. Politicians are gerrymandering district lines in order to unfairly pick their voters instead of the other way around.
These folks are going out of their way to silence the will of the people, and deliberately undermine our democracy.
**But let’s be clear:** the American people have the power to stop it. But it depends on how much each of us are willing to stand up for the democratic ideals and principles that generations of Americans fought for. If we care about them as deeply as we claim to, then we are going to have to step up.
That’s exactly why Eric Holder and I started All On The Line. This grassroots movement is using every tool at its disposal to defend democracy in Texas and anywhere else we need to be. [**For those of us who believe in fairness in our elections, it’s an all-hands-on-deck moment. subject: Is it time to axe the Department of Education?
body:
Please see a special message from our sponsor:

Unsubscribe
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xul=2qq8ny363wdaxf3eu1ztoj206x78jniyh5bgbmltatuo87yivlf3943v5ow25silp47xj8weigmothtegoymmh5uflyimbqkwrz2blepb&__stmp=t1pxe5&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh

Please see a special message from our sponsor:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t1pxe5&__onlt=t

Dear Fellow American,

I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future.

A movement is growing, led by progressives—but supported by many well-meaning Americans—to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=rc6qmltxol1js1ckrjy9cyv1eqssunvre6772mixzyiddjj6ad1vjm56o5v7p0htklg0kkqce3ab3w6atpvrnlyaz72upm06z8oqflagbseis8lyrkgy0mgr7wn88nc3f3ldfyszse5r1cfvm7t6&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t1pxe5&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t1pxe5&__onlt=t

Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?

YES
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t1pxe5&__onlt=t

NO
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t1pxe5&__onlt=t

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=rc6qmltxol1js1ckrjy9cyv1eqssunvre6772mixzyiddjj6ad1vjm56o5v7p0htklg0kkqce3ab3w6atpvrnlyaz72upm06z8oqflagbseis8lyrkgy0mgr7wn88nc3f3ldfyszse5r1cfvm7t6&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t1pxe5&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t1pxe5&__onlt=t

And after you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since 1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty." Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans.

The support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention—and for your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

President, Hillsdale College

Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

clean_body: Every day you wait is another day they pull ahead. And if we lose, history won’t care about excuses — only results. | Fellow Conservative, On August 12th, I sent you an email asking for your help to fuel our fight against the far left, which continues to raise mountains of cash. My ask—$9. I asked you and 111,000 other conservatives for help, and in the end, we came up short. I’m not going to sugarcoat it: we are losing this fight — and it’s not because the Left is stronger, it’s because too many conservatives are still sitting on the sidelines.I worry that because we finally have the White House, the US Senate and the House all at the same time and are getting things accomplished, grassroots Republicans are content with our recent wins. We shouldn’t be as there is so much more we have to do to fix America. Democrats pulled in 7.5 million more donations than Republicans in the first half of 2025. That’s not a small gap — that’s a warning siren. If you haven’t given this year, I have to ask you: what will you say to yourself if we lose the Senate because you didn’t act when you could have? You’ll know the truth — that while the Left poured in cash to buy their wins, too many of us watched from the sidelines. If you’ve ever said you stand for liberty, the Constitution, and America’s future — this is the moment to prove it. Not later. Not “when things get worse.” By then, it will be too late. Because we failed to reach our fundraising goal on August 12th, our average gift this month has now fallen to just $7. If we can’t match their enthusiasm soon, we are choosing to let them have it all. Every day you wait is another day they pull ahead. And if we lose, history won’t care about excuses — only results. I’m asking you directly: don’t be one of the conservatives who stayed quiet and then wondered how it all slipped away. For liberty, Ted Cruz P.S. Trump won more than 77 million votes last fall. If even 10% of those voters gave today, we'd erase the Democrats' advantage instantly. Please — be one of them. ] | | Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate PO Box 25400 Houston, TX 77265 -

subject: Updates from the Capitol & Around Our Community
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTE BOLICK
body:
http://www.BolickforArizona.com?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID

Good afternoon, friend,

I hope you’ve had a chance to clean up after the dust and rainstorms that swept across our state earlier this week. At our house, I’ve been busy cleaning up after our three greyhounds, who’ve tracked in plenty of mud!

**
🏗️ Investing in Our Future Workforce
------------------------------------------------------------

I recently attended West-MEC’s (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tUEwL3wK__k&mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) ribbon-cutting ceremony and toured their newest advanced manufacturing building near Deer Valley Airport. I had the pleasure of speaking with board members and two junior high welding students who are active in student government and passionate about their career and technical education. These young men are laser-focused on becoming productive members of society after graduation.

Our future workforce is taking shape—and the future looks bright in North Phoenix!

**
🛡️ Protecting Children and Families
------------------------------------------------------------

Last week, I joined Senate President Warren Petersen and Pinal County Attorney Bradley Miller for a press conference about my bill to create a Sex Offender Management Board. This board will bring experts together to guide policy and ensure the strongest protections for Arizona’s children and families. You can watch a short video HERE (https://x.com/AZSenateGOP/status/1957938418752843926?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) .

👉 Watch (https://youtu.be/qnQTy7-OkEU?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID ) the press conference

**
🏫 School Safety Matters
------------------------------------------------------------

Many of you heard about the tragic stabbing at Maryvale High School. For several legislative sessions, I’ve advocated for stronger school safety reporting tools—like those proposed in Senate Bill 1255 (https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/57leg/1R/bills/SB1255S.pdf?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) —to give families clearer insight into the safety of their children’s schools.

👉 Read (https://www.azsenaterepublicans.gov/post/senator-bolick-calls-for-renewed-focus-on-school-safety-reporting-requirements-following-deadly-mary?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) my press release

**
🚨 Fighting Human Trafficking
------------------------------------------------------------

We recently held our final anti-human trafficking stakeholder meeting at the Capitol to discuss potential legislation for next session. One group we’ve partnered with is the Arizona Missing Children Task Force, whose volunteers work tirelessly to protect vulnerable youth.

If you support their mission (https://missinginamericanetwork.org/why-us%3F?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) , please consider getting involved or donating (https://missinginamericanetwork.org/az-missingchildtaskforce?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) .

**
🔒 Improving Prison Safety
------------------------------------------------------------

Earlier this week, Representative Blackman and I issued a joint statement in response to the Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation & Reentry’s announcement (https://corrections.az.gov/news/adcrr-takes-key-actions-reduce-violence-increase-safety-and-security-arizonas-prisons?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) of new safety measures in our state prison system.

👉 Read (https://www.azsenaterepublicans.gov/post/senator-bolick-representative-blackman-warn-prison-safety-reforms-come-too-late-for-dozens-of-inmat?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) our statement

**
🦚 Preserving Local Wildlife
------------------------------------------------------------

A constituent from Glendale shared a petition to save the beloved peacocks at Sahuaro Ranch Park. If you’ve visited this historic park, you know how special these birds are to the community.

By signing the petition, you’re encouraging city officials to explore alternatives that protect the peacocks’ habitat while ensuring public safety.

👉 Sign (https://www.change.org/p/stop-the-relocation-of-the-sahuaro-ranch-peacocks?utm_medium=custom_url&utm_source=share_petition&recruited_by_id=6ff19830-d374-11e6-9d80-9f174ceaa42d&mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) the petition

📰 Bolick in the News
* Independent Prison Oversight
Read more (https://pro.stateaffairs.com/az/yellow-sheet/justice-civil-rights/ad-hoc-committee-absent-lawmakers?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID )
* Public School Safety Reporting Requirements
Read more (https://pro.stateaffairs.com/az/legislature/bolick-revives-school-safety-bill?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID )
* Sex Offender Management Board
ABC15 Coverage (https://www.abc15.com/news/state/what-we-have-isnt-working-arizona-panel-to-recommend-statewide-policies-for-sex-offenders?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID )
AZ Capitol Times (https://azcapitoltimes.com/news/2025/08/19/arizona-board-to-develop-standards-for-sex-offender-rehabilitation/?utm_campaign=az_morning&utm_content=link&utm_medium=email&utm_source=EspecialMail&mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID )
State Affairs (https://pro.stateaffairs.com/az/yellow-sheet/around-the-state/sex-offender-management-arizona?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID )
InMaricopa (https://www.inmaricopa.com/citing-no-standards-familiar-face-leads-charge-to-set-them-for-sex-offenders/?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID )

🗳️ Help Place My Name on the 2026 Republican Primary Ballot

As many of you may know, I was involved in a car accident at the end of June. I’ve spent the past few weeks focusing on healing and physical therapy, and I’m grateful for the support and well wishes I’ve received.

Now, I’m turning my attention back to serving our community—and I need your help.

If you reside in the following zip codes, there is a good chance I represent you at the state capitol: 85022, 85023, 85024, 85027, 85029, 85032, 85050, 85053, 85085, 85308, 85310, or 85331.

Please take a moment to sign my secure online nomination petition to ensure my name appears on the August 4, 2026, Republican primary ballot.

👉 Click here (https://go.azsos.gov/z9xl?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) to sign the petition

Your support means the world to me, and I’m excited to continue working on behalf of our legislative district.
Sign My Petition (https://go.azsos.gov/z9xl?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID)

🗳️ Help Us Keep This Seat — Support Our Campaign Today

As you may know, I will need to raise a significant amount of resources to retain this highly competitive State Senate seat. Your support is critical to helping us continue the work we’ve started and to ensure our community’s voice remains strong at the Capitol.

If you are so inclined, please consider making a contribution to our campaign today.

👉 Donate (https://secure.anedot.com/vote-bolick-statesenateld2/donate?mc_cid=4cc0dae8cf&mc_eid=UNIQID) Now

Thank you for staying engaged and informed. As always, I welcome your thoughts and feedback.

Warm regards,
Shawnna

Take a look at some of the this country’s most popular programs: Medicare, Social Security, public schools, libraries.
None of those are capitalist inventions. None of these are corporate-backed, and none of these are initiated by tax-based incentives.

Peter, I've officially launched my campaign for Governor of Wisconsin. In a time like this, I know so many Wisconsinites are wondering: Who’s fighting for me? I want you to know — **I am.** I didn’t plan to run for office. I’m a wife, a working mom, a nurse, a small business owner, and a proud Wisconsinite who saw a system failing everyday families and decided to do something to help fix it. In 2020, I ran for State Assembly because I knew our families deserved better. Then I ran for Lieutenant Governor to help Governor Evers lead Wisconsin through some of its toughest moments. Now, I’m stepping up again because Wisconsin is worth fighting for. I’m the granddaughter of dairy farmers from Richland County. I’m the daughter of a working-class union household. My mom was a teaching assistant, and my dad was a veteran who fixed telephones. They raised my siblings and me to work hard, speak up, and never back down. I want you to know that I’ll _never_ back down. Not when we have a president who has destroyed the rule of law, wrecked our economy, and is hell-bent on driving up our debt and taking away our health care. And not when Wisconsin’s radical legislature is failing Wisconsin’s working families and blocking progress at every turn. Wisconsinites deserve leadership they can trust. So while Trump and his allies try to drag us backward by attacking our freedoms, our public schools, and the basic services our families rely on, I know that this is a moment where we have to fight back — and I’m ready to lead. **Let me say it again: I’m not backing down. Not now, not ever.** **[Will you join me and become a Founding Donor of my campaign today? Chip in $5, $25, or whatever you can to fuel our fight for Wisconsin’s future:](https://srod4wi.us/l/o8jipxpJL8Ha)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | [ **CHIP IN $5** ](https://srod4wi.us/l/HTB6tnpGSIyf)

Friend, Today is**National Black Giving Day to support Black-led organizations** , which are often underfunded and get only 1-2% of philanthropic funding.1 We must correct this disparity, as part of the urgent work to close the still-growing racial wealth gap between white and Black communities. [**I want to lift up the Detroit Justice Center**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJVwZNE4rk7Gjpo9SHRfMTrxASej1UmFtQXNfdx8Qq4CVVs8wg51YW0paQH-OHsOSN-VvmVO23CmCcYjw_rMPCxcBRbx4BNq6gYzTcKLWzLZMPAEyiozZQi0F4FbPiiRv33hLwdQhWO6alqeFIG8ojCm9yjb3QoN4Z0y9cuY5lbkc0v00mxXwEXfmUeZP8NTYsUIVAgNhPRSZ-YBHj45hvPcSVLMx60GlN8_4b8P5g2LDwhcjIfBo0rDXi5j9APowu66w1KQ1zQkD1i4FbKYsDz40vK6e9QAaopJrtPzOsYq8A9nM56bi-c_LyzTQ5fmEPbXC1PSowSlYQBKpfUH2jRkhTsVkECdh3RjyejOmbhoJ-ZGg19Y7SBYXqaohacTn-3skAeWcWPsbt0ORXuVjfqg/4jf/120CbshURsOxgEcnEWcrrA/h1/h001.ZUfyZB0Z4wfh4e_SDF-9iWQn8GP8Z8VGN98NppzKShw)**, a Black-led non-profit law firm that’s a national leader in transforming our unjust criminal legal system.** They’ve won meaningful policy changes, including securing our right to protest. Detroit Justice Center uplifts the unique needs of formerly and currently incarcerated people, and has helped shape policies I have introduced in Congress to end mass incarceration and bring about housing justice. They’ve represented 10,000 clients, **including people caught up in the legal system due to poverty, people struggling to keep their water on and stay in their homes, and anti-war student protesters who’ve been targeted because of their advocacy for Palestinian liberation**. Their work is urgently needed as those in power increase political repression and aggressive law enforcement. **Last month, Detroit Justice Center got a notification that an environmental justice grant they applied for was unlawfully terminated by the current administration.** As the administration targets funding for diversity, equity, and inclusion, Detroit Justice Center is also facing a downturn in philanthropic support for racial justice work. **We need to counter these attacks by the Trump administration with thousands of grassroots donations.** [**For National Black Giving Day, will you donate now to support Detroit Justice Center and build the movement for Black liberation?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJVwZNE4rk7Gjpo9SHRfMTrxASej1UmFtQXNfdx8Qq4CWZzhVJskCcBzSreFaKdHArocLVTETGEP1jMoCWuZBQDKeYA5bl8USnXXnDgJ7FgedAYryWYoSIZcdzkKGR5EckLZO5PSnsNtZ36aTXWYyzwlRJbpP0fMhstiFszaFG4HqqZ_cFYgIo6gWztmidiNLM284uMfxPnJexOW6q91zTb9MjFGvJj1qCfUmWP0dHC0vK139eDQA9bs-yufYsEJzDOASnGREhC-QrgT0DnxtoYwIW1om9C8-o9DnZJj49YStwh4qqovWz0jtv_MJO8_jk1fF8CkboBdZ_hDwrggPkj1J53BV9MWigd8RY02EMFuiReD9nk-Z4DlyeSCDq-kXpnhDyHhLlYlTzoVjHJkaFdA/4jf/120CbshURsOxgEcnEWcrrA/h2/h001.ifD_V4iwdaDAFYBXBapJGUMl3gBbliu_joLvmHi6n_E) | [SUPPORT DETROIT JUSTICE CENTER](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJVwZNE4rk7Gjpo9SHRfMTrxASej1UmFtQXNfdx8Qq4CUd9k8jY3fOtm1RqUVfTSpgBkbEyIeYIpiPe6sHF_gWAADRVxWh7_3Y6Xja6UlWmTa-REiZRmMALxt1LxQMDyzzU7y6kSb1iMo__16ns4FECsVClaG0hL-zFtHDw2JwWV26QMsnHGORGb_mm4kMoRqwKBn2Uq5OpszFzjf_Id8kAGMeU6QFrd26pWi67X_5OTYTrIVY1664-MRqJ9Va2BIuUnugqfAcHooPz9y4oNONQ9RD-RV3gkTPgCpg65DUkCoYBGY-SryN7ygd-HTRXqJcXDNDsIeA-k_mNMh6o7wB23bV9sNUYZFZU5FJC1yA8j1x4vt5Fk4Jdj7uAR4Is4UEl3NA8NgSC8TcgKGGght3EQ/4jf/120CbshURsOxgEcnEWcrrA/h3/h001.NDc5cLkeoFIBvyvcbhIbAmWqVbSkSqryNOc7ZacsWaA)

Together, we’ve rallied and educated local residents on alternatives to incarceration—and each year Detroit Justice Center educates the next generation of freedom fighters at our Youth Civic Engagement Fellowship.
**Detroit Justice Center has won fights to secure our right to protest and to expand criminal record expungement opportunities**. They’re providing urgent legal services to keep clients out of jail—through helping pay off people’s court debt, reinstating licenses, and removing obstacles such as warrants for unpaid fees.
They’re also **reuniting families** involved in the criminal legal system, and**keeping people in their homes** by assisting in eviction cases and helping people keep their water on.
Detroit Justice Center’s initiatives include **shifting funds out of policing and increasing investment in non-carceral solutions** , training residents on how to mediate harm without relying on police (also known as restorative justice), and helping people imagine a world without prisons or police.
They envision a “future where every life is valued equally,” including “affordable and safe housing for all.”2 As part of that vision, Detroit Justice Center pushes for economic self-determination, providing legal support to:
* **Community land trusts** , which allow residents to own land and decide what development looks like in their neighborhoods so they don’t get pushed out.
* **Worker-owned cooperatives** , where all members get an equal share of profits and an equal voice in how things run.
* **Returning citizens** who are pursuing dreams of entrepreneurship.

As Detroit Justice Center explains on their website: _“We help establish new ways of organizing society... Resistance, in its most potent form, is not only clear about what it is against, but also specific in what it is aiming for. ...We’re actively building up new structures defined by democracy and dignity.”_ 3
The group has established six community land trusts for community-owned affordable housing in majority-Black Detroit, and helped establish 12 worker-owned cooperatives that are BIPOC* woman-led—including a childcare collective, green grocer, and mobile wellness hub. They’re sharing these models with groups building solidarity economies around the country.

clean_body: Today is dedicated to supporting Black-led non-profit organizations. | | | Friend, Today isNational Black Giving Day to support Black-led organizations , which are often underfunded and get only 1-2% of philanthropic funding.1 We must correct this disparity, as part of the urgent work to close the still-growing racial wealth gap between white and Black communities. , a Black-led non-profit law firm that’s a national leader in transforming our unjust criminal legal system. They’ve won meaningful policy changes, including securing our right to protest. Detroit Justice Center uplifts the unique needs of formerly and currently incarcerated people, and has helped shape policies I have introduced in Congress to end mass incarceration and bring about housing justice. They’ve represented 10,000 clients, including people caught up in the legal system due to poverty, people struggling to keep their water on and stay in their homes, and anti-war student protesters who’ve been targeted because of their advocacy for Palestinian liberation. Their work is urgently needed as those in power increase political repression and aggressive law enforcement. Last month, Detroit Justice Center got a notification that an environmental justice grant they applied for was unlawfully terminated by the current administration. As the administration targets funding for diversity, equity, and inclusion, Detroit Justice Center is also facing a downturn in philanthropic support for racial justice work. We need to counter these attacks by the Trump administration with thousands of grassroots donations. | Photo of me with Detroit Justice Center Community Legal Advocate Sonja Bonnet, after she spoke at a rally about the struggle Black Detroiters face with illegal tax foreclosures. Together, we’ve rallied and educated local residents on alternatives to incarceration—and each year Detroit Justice Center educates the next generation of freedom fighters at our Youth Civic Engagement Fellowship. Detroit Justice Center has won fights to secure our right to protest and to expand criminal record expungement opportunities. They’re providing urgent legal services to keep clients out of jail—through helping pay off people’s court debt, reinstating licenses, and removing obstacles such as warrants for unpaid fees. They’re also reuniting families involved in the criminal legal system, andkeeping people in their homes by assisting in eviction cases and helping people keep their water on. Detroit Justice Center’s initiatives include shifting funds out of policing and increasing investment in non-carceral solutions , training residents on how to mediate harm without relying on police (also known as restorative justice), and helping people imagine a world without prisons or police. They envision a “future where every life is valued equally,” including “affordable and safe housing for all.”2 As part of that vision, Detroit Justice Center pushes for economic self-determination, providing legal support to: Community land trusts , which allow residents to own land and decide what development looks like in their neighborhoods so they don’t get pushed out. Worker-owned cooperatives , where all members get an equal share of profits and an equal voice in how things run. Returning citizens who are pursuing dreams of entrepreneurship. As Detroit Justice Center explains on their website: “We help establish new ways of organizing society... Resistance, in its most potent form, is not only clear about what it is against, but also specific in what it is aiming for. ...We’re actively building up new structures defined by democracy and dignity.” 3 The group has established six community land trusts for community-owned affordable housing in majority-Black Detroit, and helped establish 12 worker-owned cooperatives that are BIPOC woman-led—including a childcare collective, green grocer, and mobile wellness hub. They’re sharing these models with groups building solidarity economies around the country. Thank you, Rashida P.S. Whether or not you can donate, you can also support Detroit Justice Center by forwarding this email to your friends and asking them if they can chip in, or by following and sharing posts from Detroit Justice Center on or . **“Bill to let AG prosecute election crimes heads to Abbott, but is it legal?”** Dallas Morning News' **Gromer Jeffers, Jr.** \-- "A bill that would allow the attorney general to prosecute Texas election fraud cases is headed for Gov. **Greg Abbott’s** desk, but it’s unclear whether the proposed law is constitutional.

The legislation, approved by the House on Tuesday, would bypass restrictions in the Texas Constitution on the attorney general’s ability to prosecute voter fraud cases. The power to prosecute such cases belongs to local district attorneys, a policy that was upheld four years ago when the all-Republican Court of Criminal Appeals ruled that the attorney general’s office could not unilaterally prosecute cases involving voter fraud or other election-related crimes.

The court pointed to the separation of powers clause in the state constitution as the reason the attorney general’s office could not prosecute election law crimes.

The legislation, approved Tuesday in the House by an 85-54 vote, was accompanied by a resolution that would put to voters the question of whether to change the state constitution to allow the attorney general such powers. But that resolution did not get the 100 votes needed for approval.

State Rep. **Matt Shaheen** , R-Plano and chairman of the House Elections Committee said the bill by itself meets the objective of changing the law even without the needed supermajority on the resolution. Shaheen authored the House legislation, which was identical to the Senate bill the House approved.

Shaheen said changing the Election Code to give the attorney general the power to prosecute election-related crimes was constitutional. Under Texas law, local district attorneys have the power to prosecute election crimes. The attorney general’s office can be involved but only with the invitation of a district attorney.

Shaheen said the bill “replaces permissive language stating that the attorney general may prosecute with the mandatory language affirming that the attorney general has jurisdiction to prosecute.” Specifically, language in the code changes from “may” to “shall,” Shaheen said.

If constitutional, the change would flip the authority of prosecuting election law crimes from local district attorneys to the attorney general.

“By passing SB-12, the legislature ensures that Texas election laws are fully enforceable and that the criminal violations can be prosecuted,” Shaheen said. “This legislation strengthens public confidence in Texas elections and safeguards the integrity of our democratic process.”

The law falls short, however, of what Abbott outlined when he included the matter in special session agendas.

In his proclamation for the special sessions, Abbott asked lawmakers to consider “legislation proposing a constitutional amendment allowing the Attorney General to prosecute state election crimes.”

A spokesperson for the governor declined to comment on the matter Tuesday. Shaheen said he was confident Abbott would sign the legislation.

Democrats blasted the bill as unconstitutional and unnecessary.

State Rep. **Joe Moody** , D-El Paso, said “our constitution wisely gave the keys to local prosecutors.”

“This isn’t a partisan issue. It’s a political philosophy issue,” Moody said. “It’s something we need to take a long-term view on, because there’s a jail cell at the end of that road.”

Attorney**Ken Paxton** has long sought the power to prosecute election law cases. In 2024, he campaigned against three Court of Criminal Appeals judges who ruled that his office didn’t have the power to prosecute election fraud. [They lost reelection bids.](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eOQPXJLmqZGCIlkWp25_d_lk_WBk4jvizEFTNwb_CO-1mKyc20KKX9uLCrOqDQxWKwNND1Lg1auvf0P2n8exYy2uEw_MiJkDOyHqBQ6Ji7zBkveSQkBzap2hfO3d-c6jVK5vxS2OH8Cqj9xyPLcwhm29TeDEXk1YpDnHY8dc_g2rVn841x6aK7gU7_LdLUK-cmLXteEkcPIrJkwttNkKAScQn7mTLWSDf_Bk1b3k6A9EnGgM1cPjK8A3BXLSU-_Jk630ZRJtxjO2CpwJbSw-Fm7rToY1i143OgOV0Sjz00e2MYBJzpfwYoEGnikx4HTuRElJ6UsMxngClcJ552QL-tEWoj-VcuNbvFL5KnjNfHugp-7p20bKDzuF3w7uN96lQ3vpuQFGcs5_hRoSp_oNu-z6UMjx6-BNAsTXo6nVl0vqQXPBT9ewFFlrolVI8ecOCWucK2BBmGF4qQKSzPWz4mKIcIomMbWTvyznDtZ4RRq-_bjH9X0sujHHYip1R7_SmW3jShIczjjYEzzhbVWG0O1E-_REOXqinlqlhvSPAWNsWDq9sUeAz7AraJFRJmc1Ow/4jf/8x9M5A1RStOMfOvABkJs3g/h25/h001.NSJTsXzOCufYgSFrRJgWCg9EqE6zYVLEJw7StlPPKmM)

**“Harris County constables, sheriffs could contract with HOAs without commissioners’ OK under bill heading to Abbott,”** Texas Tribune's**Alex Nguyen** \-- "Two bills that focus solely on Harris County law enforcement agencies’ contracting and funding advanced to the governor’s desk, two days after being added to the second special session’s agenda.

Currently, sheriffs and constables in Harris County can contract with homeowner associations, school districts and municipal utility districts to provide additional policing for them. The more prominent of the two proposals, [House Bill 26](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.y1qQg7vX491TJbzrGLYTuEYT0yv_aZw1IceJac_-o0Y-UGIWKkPTFm9Kz5DRdvb_-aYU7NLaOywMgY5yceksY11R687IxggK7vT4AJtOCSTPC5f2-q2rvck2wsAM71XdsIReebgORR8fCGnVV1kfHQSHCqAXxVmkQOHz_F1vPNWuOUWyf0FIRTcNmWvShJfe9kBulfVVE2eP0b0DElAIWZqT2nTLfo-z5oze94BaMTKrnxuJclcBz0WVSNNOexzJyi6Tj6rgGwC0LJlI0KLlltSo3ZemqHkUjhf-k3knXGamLQ0La-DuReDZh5m9397Yv7h6CwzSB9ygLWVFOyMipUHHZ0qP5BSphdRhWjf6oTyzbjkUnDu6BACPfcXRppp2RNeqEGVBdptutY_mKAacwsoVOuBbuLbpSjMtvkqbPW_8UX_RB7wLV0HGAYQ0dN1q5cw6FC7tBoLMuxP4dAqVCt__v3kS-maNIyCrg4Jz0cU-OPoDH269nDM6AHfW-O5h/4jf/8x9M5A1RStOMfOvABkJs3g/h27/h001.tPbO2tf9G36PrjCRQL4sLZRMB1JKEGSodhm3QrwRP3I), would allow these law enforcement agencies to enter into such contracts without the need for approval from the county’s commissioners court. Meanwhile, [House Bill 192](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.y1qQg7vX491TJbzrGLYTuEYT0yv_aZw1IceJac_-o0Y-UGIWKkPTFm9Kz5DRdvb_-aYU7NLaOywMgY5yceksY7fLGv9rC1vdTp0rN2BVKrj7h_W75BX-pFhL4eD_WYV28xtqa4cXgJ9kSYt7sNMiSmMsqZsP-f8zGTilUpbfTkA7hc8-VSy6hhS0g3BsscrDm--zBtw9ve4nw5e41yTiYQfBcCMjb19kwkCRsD4PxZUQ1Xqu4UsUMv_-Hvo1Y9zXDk-1JjGtIj_yL9ats3hGbk1ngApXiHhclAYAfVTYNRjEad24hbV3KfHY0qGNhRx86st292_m4M2mrnCcyJxJ6avND0wJC9uuHT-K-lfgJfcBaNITTh4QDvqYDgYP7rSdB3CRQS58LFcUT42wo_KcbDrzKUyKmvuUvLaZNMQdec_DaOoHOvaRGMif0NKrd3J9f65ICHWzChFodP7vWhOqMvgXa0HHh8utXeTzJ8dv40-aPNtRoGH7YLk848L_anCC/4jf/8x9M5A1RStOMfOvABkJs3g/h28/h001.ZskIBmRUFKetZGQT2VBU7t-HZHBTVhOkoBwH_5Youtg) would require the county to seek voter approval if it adopts a budget that reallocates unspent funding that was appropriated for law enforcement agencies or moves funding previously appropriated for a specific law enforcement position to another agency.

**“Dallas property tax rate still up for discussion as council members look for wiggle room,”** Dallas Morning News' **Everton Bailey, Jr.** \-- "For the [10th straight year, the Dallas City Council is considering lowering the property tax rate](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eOQPXJLmqZGCIlkWp25_d_kt4zZ7BA9X6VHUBegwwAunv0vmal6Jvbdu9RRvniZkL2zXHug_RuBH_3-3c0a7hMBOXA_dSdysqMe-nPuSSdYaYYNJA0dLIWnpFePByChsZxcTBS46vkj21A20V351nwD-_s3cYPgM6RLB1cuhdPxqRAQ9hCaKZ628mo9OihYqbARacBfFycQ-DgpBfto-uKh0_T0N1j7YPNhvOfGQI5hvggA6naaruFr7Igi06q0H1k2mQ6lvBrZwJb5NNIw8MAVK4BiGAIHo82WR_GYi02t5nyFkwrnnNzPBDxO0GKXGPN7DEkTllgBk5G8UEpccZU0TKWPiUKCkpyfv8C-ED0_JRUMCZ9SnbUnrLH_ZdJtKZJ6EP5ESJ6gg6N2R_vcbkVoAqneJfcWhL5uhPui647nDXT2CkZ5fC2VQq-IAQioHLJgF7adyxuS9IRYe6MyQ0lSXxyaPET0Y-peD7yv8mvTQw04152VG5SbmU4SgHbxLj1_WOK7OthfOGqQFIJAwrH4kNOqsQfdY7meudALHkRyO3m1XwYPibkIvAaVooFIWmg/4jf/8x9M5A1RStOMfOvABkJs3g/h46/h001.KHMghBF6eJS0T_V8RYkKve5c7H93SSOgcxhG6wauUY0) — even though many homeowners will still pay more due to rising home values and costs.

However, the exact new rate is still under discussion, as city officials continue to review a proposed $5.2 billion budget and gather public input before a final vote in mid-September. Council members suggested Wednesday that there may be some changes to the city manager’s proposed rate.

Currently, the tax rate is 70.47 cents per $100**** valuation, and City Manager **Kim Tolbert’s** proposed budget for the coming year lowers the rate to 69.97 cents.

However, the City Council voted 10-5 on Wednesday to set a maximum possible rate at 70.22 cents — still less than this year’s rate but more than Tolbert’s proposal. Council members said the move would give them wiggle room as they discuss the budget with their constituents.

Council members **Chad West** , **Zarin Gracey** , **Jaime Resendez** , **Laura Cadena** , **Adam Bazaldua** , **Lorie Blair** , **Paula Blackmon** , **Kathy Stewart** , **Bill Roth** , and Deputy Mayor Pro Tem **Gay Donnell Willis** voted in favor of the motion. Mayor **Eric Johnson** , Mayor Pro Tem **Jesse Moreno** and council members **Maxie Johnson** , **Cara Mendelsohn** and**Paul Ridley** voted against it.

Under Tolbert’s proposed rate, a home valued at $382,010 — with a $175,000 homestead exemption — is projected to lower the average homeowner’s tax bill by about $12.66 next year. But tax bills could still rise or fall depending on changes in home values.

Tolbert’s proposed budget plan calls for a significant increase in funding for police and fire services amid cuts to city jobs, community pools, libraries, and other consolidations.

Council member **Adam Bazaldua** , who proposed the higher ceiling, argued that setting a lower bar could limit the council’s ability to explore alternatives to some of the proposed cuts. If the council approves Tolbert’s rate, the city would collect $11 million less in property taxes. If they stick with the proposed 70.22-cent ceiling, the loss would be about $5.5 million.

“I believe it would be preliminary for us to set a ceiling before having a discussion to see if there are potential viable options to save some of the cuts that were brought forth with this proposed budget,” Bazaldua said.

The City Council scheduled a Sept. 17 public hearing at City Hall to gather residents’ opinions on the tax rate before voting to finalize it and the citywide budget the same day. The new rate and budget would take effect on Oct. 1." **“Johnson County Sheriff Adam King arrested on felony corruption charges,”** Dallas Morning News' **Matt Kyle** \-- "Johnson County Sheriff **Adam King** was arrested Wednesday on charges of abuse of office and witness retaliation, according to jail records.

King was indicted on two charges of corrupt influence: retaliation against a witness, which is a third-degree felony, and one charge of abuse of office, in addition to a charge of official oppression — sexual harassment, a Class A misdemeanor, court records show.

King was booked into the Johnson County jail. Bond had not been set by about 8:15 p.m.

The arresting agency was the Texas Rangers, jail records show.

Johnson County Judge **Christopher Boedeker** said via email that the indictments are a result of a weekslong investigation by the Rangers. Boedeker said as soon as county officials were aware of the allegations, they referred the case to the Rangers.

“While Mr. King is entitled to a presumption of innocence, no person is above the law,” Boedeker said.

According to the indictment, which was sent to _The Dallas Morning News_ by Boedeker, King is accused of sexually harassing multiple female employees of the sheriff’s office between February 2024 and July 2025. The indictment said King made several sexual remarks to female subordinates, including telling them they needed to wear makeup to work and telling one employee if she kept “losing weight,” he would “do ungodly things” to her.

The indictments also accused King of retaliating against two employees who reported the harassment, including threatening to arrest a female employee whom he allegedly had harassed. King also tried to obtain her address after finding out she had filed a human resources complaint against him and spoke to the Rangers about the allegations, the indictment said.

King, a Republican, was first elected as sheriff of Johnson County in 2016.

The Johnson County sheriff’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from _The News_." **“Mystery surrounds $1.2 billion Army contract to build huge detention tent camp in Texas desert,”** AP's **Michael Biesecker** and**Joshua Goodman** \-- "When President **Donald Trump’s** administration last month awarded a contract worth up to $1.2 billion to build and operate what it says will become [the nation’s largest immigration detention complex](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.taRaxrEkWqxIZl3CYy7RU-8zPWZErbzsTpoOJuc75r0pecWlFyt5BeRyk3Wa74L30Z5FQAVAtlMCPTP_mIRIW-TEt_ALkLkQgdYj46jt1lSmeVqrdFZZlcV3Ho0P00wf4FlmlsoRjLTsoIJMfyXuWIvWrn0XU3pHrCSsNDgDDUi3tpzg3fA_zuO9oxN98sjDU6LSIxX1OUDOFjEkLzF6TggBjb4phjCUiX9B9J3bF4rZ5XRcfp6NlBgI0hrnQxkfMUuVRb1NRlBmiVgulmgXkJP3IM8Gn6LdhtNEmuQYj3OpiWHi9F5_LKH07Mp_Fhzt3IBusYccc7OnYq0ZXxhEP_xyZTMNk5BVxeybEAOWEIokjKdRVGbxjlCxM48MwmZ1nCRVJTM6b3EeM0amLOaknJfXlHuzpfqwX-Wvb9r2BDbvSTdejgjArB8KKZq2hp-H9Q65isEndShWUlquku5ZiceujOS8hcmfyNGiX5XwMEjTB6YVDp-tnwTBCgZxIlmjQ904abQnXgwcgcfrO32KCm__hnz1FFJ1Ch5qea_EpaU/4jf/8x9M5A1RStOMfOvABkJs3g/h72/h001.ee9vbvoTR-0g_phtUZ_xFrpUPeHNXYRnZ_RR2S_Qk54), it didn’t turn to a large government contractor or even a firm that specializes in private prisons.

Instead, it handed the project on a military base to Acquisition Logistics LLC, a small business that has no listed experience running a correction facility and had never won a federal contract worth more than $16 million. The company also lacks a functioning website and lists as its address a modest home in suburban Virginia owned by a 77-year-old retired Navy flight officer.

The mystery over the award only deepened last week as the new facility began to accept its first detainees. The Pentagon has refused to release the contract or explain why it selected Acquisition Logistics over a dozen other bidders to build the massive tent camp at Fort Bliss in west Texas. At least one competitor has filed a complaint.

The secretive — and brisk — contracting process is emblematic, experts said, of the government’s broader rush to fulfill [the Republican president’s pledge](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eFAgrMPQAZVqW_ErIbdEgrIiybgN_WkhJXP823_LCqebw1EsJaYeS_UfKK5vP5SSMhalRh0Zg6wUT14mmRKkwyRp9ctpQJHx71g-kNu2WM2vzcGVl5nIEk88vvzOkkeIwzfUPr0k0-_muUF_ZrU-1Mq1PEapYP_N_NqqFeiifaI0Caf4W4lZV-U7ci9EfcqZluoPt5RIwAyfTbMtWqBtNJJ2cfe8kvd-mZ7Nqc-OxgqYY3RBwr3vRDaisamBEm6_llJlxctbKg9xW7pPBqzT9E4oFzknh1A4RAIOj6KD7LvhA4baibucrRs5afZoK0pSMOfWjXhclTSWTR46ZXypj6gVAkg6LhBgVgW7XI1AnW8FtWA19s4EwkprWn-3A5lsWaArDxIcd071A59h02M4B_vu5aDswN-uGzVmMpPmrP8wzkT1zWX3Ay4COjQPJZ9VjT_oAeueQ2mRW5ch9SFwodgtSQ6yteVo3oFNRx8CnKvRTVM7wAOq8rRZ3w5Bca374uIe_f2rIDYBGJGy1ETv2TgfNWw5jbXEjFl-dsUl14gIuGkJUd_vSVSIkTZFTUhWzg/4jf/8x9M5A1RStOMfOvABkJs3g/h73/h001.gK1KfA4zzqxyBAG86msJlGd4HIoA8pf6iD2i18x0qow) to arrest and deport [an estimated 10 million migrants](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.taRaxrEkWqxIZl3CYy7RU2TY3DYz9WriSqkHeF_BaJnqsWvHcLaNQHLUIju3MfnlxfpJj9a06nXi5UR3_NowmuhhknHW_1leQVyruNQ5dCvm_-It6OOIYgYz6Du9cE-q0bWNyY08AC7Z4ZLty2BjY_mIU9eoLw77llf3pmw_DI841DEaJu8ZwmGt75yA54ytmp7Htygy7MBuCf8-S6EJVlqko8vkRVhJEzHcjEivoMiRZMu_X4UlRpJqTH5hDnHrWMFzTS41eiaWsR2SiNpW57oTE8xl_siC3rNBK0OiJlcFeWBQfcfQO-e36obSrrzxBVsvd9Y-sbLetCvUN-FEJe3bgXz5s428l_TDyA19yU7YVqTxjPHAv5hdCxqdP1RT0ZH88AlQ-G7LU-sgkww3BYe3JZxUSOk2PMSFOsVC-79sGsPbsjyIglvzzdvklly6/4jf/8x9M5A1RStOMfOvABkJs3g/h74/h001.loOiOUVAniXhdQ8niUx7wLptKL51bLk_mG82v7q-F5k) living in the U.S. without permanent legal status. As part of that push, the government is turning increasingly to the military to handle tasks that had traditionally been left to civilian agencies.

A member of Congress who recently toured the camp said she was concerned that such a small and inexperienced firm had been entrusted to build and run a facility expected to house up to 5,000 migrants.

“It’s far too easy for standards to slip,” said Rep.**Veronica Escobar** , a Democrat whose district includes Fort Bliss. “Private facilities far too frequently operate with a profit margin in mind as opposed to a governmental facility.”

Attorney**Joshua Schnell** , who specializes in federal contracting law, said he was troubled that the Trump administration has provided so little information about the facility.

“The lack of transparency about this contract leads to legitimate questions about why the Army would award such a large contract to a company without a website or any other publicly available information demonstrating its ability to perform such a complicated project,” he said.

**Ken A. Wagner** , the president and CEO of Acquisition Logistics, did not respond to phone messages or emails. No one answered the door at his three-bedroom house listed as his company’s headquarters. Virginia records list Wagner as an owner of the business, though it’s unclear whether he might have partners.

Defense Secretary**Pete Hegseth** approved using Fort Bliss for the new detention center, and the administration has hopes to build more at other bases. A spokesperson for the Army declined to discuss its deal with Acquisition Logistics or reveal details about the camp’s construction, citing the litigation over the company’s qualifications.

The Department of Homeland Security, which includes U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, declined to answer questions about the detention camp it oversees.

Named Camp East Montana for the closest road, the facility is being built in the sand and scrub Chihuahuan Desert, where summertime temperatures can exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit and heat-related deaths are common. According to three lawyers who were in the El Paso courtroom Wednesday when judges made the decision, the hearing on the congressional boundaries will take place from Oct. 1-10 in El Paso. That would allow enough time for the three-judge panel to make a decision on whether the maps are legal or violate the federal Voting Rights Act before the December filing deadline for the 2026 elections. » A written order is expected to be released Thursday morning, the lawyers said. “They came up with the best time under the circumstances,” said Gary Bledsoe , the president of the Texas NAACP and one of the group’s lawyers. Bledsoe is also a lawyer for U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett , D-Dallas. “We think this is a case where the racial bias is just overt,” Bledsoe said before getting on a flight back to Austin. » A , filed hours after the map was approved by the Legislature, argues that the redistricting plan is discriminatory. State Rep. Matt Shaheen , R-Prosper and chairman of the House Elections Committee, said 2026 candidates would likely run under the new boundaries. “I have a high level of confidence that after further review the maps passed by the Texas Legislature will stand,” Shaheen said. The new map, approved this month by the Legislature, will reconfigure Texas’ congressional districts in an effort to turn five of them to Republican control from Democrat control. The redistricting was requested by President Donald Trump in an effort to shore up his Republican majority in Congress heading into the 2026 mid-term elections. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has said he plans to sign the bill into law. Bledsoe said Trump’s request that Texas embark on mid-decade redistricting will be the center of the plaintiff’s case. “Trump’s letter will be exhibit No. 1,” he said. The El Paso federal panel also held a trial in May over whether the 2021 legislative maps passed by the Texas Legislature are legal. It has yet to issue a ruling."
