Lozano \-- "The Uvalde school district released only a small fraction of the documents it said would be made public regarding the 2022 massacre, with district officials in the small Texas town saying this week it was an honest mistake that they were fixing. The mix-up was revealed during an Uvalde school board meeting on Monday when the attorney for the district said his law firm mistakenly failed to make public all documents as had been promised in a legal settlement. He blamed it on “reasons that are our firm’s business, but it is our error.” “We are not in any way trying to hide anything. We are not in any way trying to not release things,” attorneyRobb Decker said. Earlier this month, the Uvalde Consolidated Independent School District following years of litigation. The school district had sought to withhold documents connected to the attack that killed , one of the deadliest school shootings in U.S. history. The in July to release all the district’s records and end the lawsuit pursued by media organizations to make the information public. The botched release was another misstep for district leaders who have been criticized for fighting the lawsuit and not making this information public sooner. School district members on Monday regretted having to again apologize to family members of the victims and the community for an error following the shooting. The school district’s police and other law enforcement agencies have also been heavily scrutinized for their as terrified students inside a classroom called 911 and parents begged officers to go in. Family members including Jesse Rizo , the uncle of 9-year-old victim Jackie Cazares and a member of the school board, were among those pushing to see the records. “There’s no excuse for that sir,” Rizo said. “You can call it a mistake, you can call it an error. It’s a costly error, a very costly error.” This week’s revelation means that around nine of every 10 records and emails were not released on Aug. 11, when the school board had said it had made public all its records. Board members said about 26,000 more pages of documents and 8,600 more emails were expected to be released. More than 3,400 pages of the withheld documents were released as of Wednesday. Decker said all would be made available to the public by next week. Still, many of the documents released by Wednesday offered few new revelations." | #TXLEGE “Bill to let AG prosecute election crimes heads to Abbott, but is it legal?” Dallas Morning News' Gromer Jeffers, Jr. \-- "A bill that would allow the attorney general to prosecute Texas election fraud cases is headed for Gov. Greg Abbott’s desk, but it’s unclear whether the proposed law is constitutional. The legislation, approved by the House on Tuesday, would bypass restrictions in the Texas Constitution on the attorney general’s ability to prosecute voter fraud cases. The power to prosecute such cases belongs to local district attorneys, a policy that was upheld four years ago when the all-Republican Court of Criminal Appeals ruled that the attorney general’s office could not unilaterally prosecute cases involving voter fraud or other election-related crimes. The court pointed to the separation of powers clause in the state constitution as the reason the attorney general’s office could not prosecute election law crimes. The legislation, approved Tuesday in the House by an 85-54 vote, was accompanied by a resolution that would put to voters the question of whether to change the state constitution to allow the attorney general such powers. But that resolution did not get the 100 votes needed for approval. State Rep. Matt Shaheen , R-Plano and chairman of the House Elections Committee said the bill by itself meets the objective of changing the law even without the needed supermajority on the resolution. Shaheen authored the House legislation, which was identical to the Senate bill the House approved. Shaheen said changing the Election Code to give the attorney general the power to prosecute election-related crimes was constitutional. Under Texas law, local district attorneys have the power to prosecute election crimes. The attorney general’s office can be involved but only with the invitation of a district attorney. Shaheen said the bill “replaces permissive language stating that the attorney general may prosecute with the mandatory language affirming that the attorney general has jurisdiction to prosecute.” Specifically, language in the code changes from “may” to “shall,” Shaheen said. If constitutional, the change would flip the authority of prosecuting election law crimes from local district attorneys to the attorney general. “By passing SB-12, the legislature ensures that Texas election laws are fully enforceable and that the criminal violations can be prosecuted,” Shaheen said. “This legislation strengthens public confidence in Texas elections and safeguards the integrity of our democratic process.” The law falls short, however, of what Abbott outlined when he included the matter in special session agendas. In his proclamation for the special sessions, Abbott asked lawmakers to consider “legislation proposing a constitutional amendment allowing the Attorney General to prosecute state election crimes.” A spokesperson for the governor declined to comment on the matter Tuesday. Shaheen said he was confident Abbott would sign the legislation. Democrats blasted the bill as unconstitutional and unnecessary. State Rep. Joe Moody , D-El Paso, said “our constitution wisely gave the keys to local prosecutors.” “This isn’t a partisan issue. It’s a political philosophy issue,” Moody said. “It’s something we need to take a long-term view on, because there’s a jail cell at the end of that road.” AttorneyKen Paxton has long sought the power to prosecute election law cases. In 2024, he campaigned against three Court of Criminal Appeals judges who ruled that his office didn’t have the power to prosecute election fraud. Paxton is running in the 2026 Republican Senate primary against incumbent John Cornyn, so he would be in the attorney general’s office in the first year of the proposed law. It would then be used by future attorneys general." ($) “Harris County constables, sheriffs could contract with HOAs without commissioners’ OK under bill heading to Abbott,” Texas Tribune'sAlex Nguyen \-- "Two bills that focus solely on Harris County law enforcement agencies’ contracting and funding advanced to the governor’s desk, two days after being added to the second special session’s agenda. Currently, sheriffs and constables in Harris County can contract with homeowner associations, school districts and municipal utility districts to provide additional policing for them. Both the county and contracting groups have to sign off on the contract, and they split portions of the cost depending on the amount of time the deputies spend in the area. The more prominent of the two proposals, , would allow these law enforcement agencies to enter into such contracts without the need for approval from the county’s commissioners court. Meanwhile, would require the county to seek voter approval if it adopts a budget that reallocates unspent funding that was appropriated for law enforcement agencies or moves funding previously appropriated for a specific law enforcement position to another agency. State Rep. Tom Oliverson , the Cypress Republican who carried both bills, and his backers said they are about protecting law enforcement including this popular deputy contract program. Their critics, however, said the legislation would upend the county government’s checks and balances, as well as harm taxpayers. “You already pay your taxes for a constable to patrol your neighborhoods. But now they want to go and bid a contract with your HOAs, to pay them, to contract with them, to patrol your neighborhood more often,” state Rep. Charlene Ward Johnson , D-Houston, said during a Texas House hearing about HB 26 on Wednesday. “That’s double taxation.” The House then cleared HB 26 with a 88-49 vote and HB 192 with a 89-48 vote early Wednesday afternoon. Hours later, the Texas Senate voted 21-5 to approve both bills. These proposals now head to the governor’s desk. The votes came two days after Gov.Greg Abbott added the items to the second special session’s agenda on Monday, saying that the legislation would improve public safety. Oliverson quickly thanked the governor in for “protecting neighborhood law enforcement contracts for the vast majority of unincorporated Harris County and ISD’s that depend on them.” Oliverson said the legislation is needed because the deputy contract program is under attack, despite its popularity and importance to unincorporated areas. The county also the contract’s costs for some groups in order to help cover constable pay raises, the Houston Chronicle reported. “Unfortunately, there’s a lot of friction going on between the law enforcement departments and Commissioners Court with regards to the terms and conditions of those contracts,” Oliverson said during a House committee hearing for HB 26 on Aug. 22. The committee then heard testimony from Tom Ramsey , a Harris County commissioner who spoke about the importance of such a program to maintain public safety and growth in his precinct, which covers most of areas. It also received signed letters from all eight Harris County constables that show their bipartisan support for a proposal that would “remove [the program] from the threat of any volatile partisan whims of our Commissioners Court.” “Us going and negotiating directly with some of those neighborhoods that have been sorely overlooked all these years is going to be a great thing if this bill passes,” Constable Alan Rosen , a Democrat, added in his testimony. Some Harris County commissioners, however, told the Texas Tribune that they oppose the proposals. Commissioner Rodney Ellis called the legislation part of the state’s “ongoing war on local government,” while Commissioner Adrian Garcia said the bills could create difficulties for maintaining other public safety initiatives and stressed that public safety shouldn’t be about who can pay extra. Garcia also warned that the proposed shift of control over the contracts could “cripple the county budget process.” “How are the 5 members of Commissioners Court expected to set a budget when in the middle of a fiscal year, 9 other independently elected officials could effectively set the whole county’s budget because of these contracts,” he said in a statement. “On a governance perspective, this legislation would be a budget killer.” The Tribune also reached out to the offices of Commissioner Lesley Briones and County Judge Lina Hidalgo , but didn’t receive comments. Meanwhile, some officials from other parts of Texas are already wary about the precedent that these proposals could set. They said state lawmakers could come back in future legislative sessions and add counties with fewer than 3.3 million people — the bills’ current threshold, which limits them to just Harris County. “We defend, we don’t defund,” Rick Bailey, a Johnson County commissioner, told the Tribune. He registered against HB 26 but didn’t testify. “But this has the potential to have some really negative effects on county budgets and local taxpayers.” Oliverson didn’t respond to the criticism posed on the House floor on Wednesday. His office also didn’t provide a comment in response to requests from the Tribune." ($) | 2026 “Minneapolis gunman appears to promote “Brandon Herrera for president” in video posted before shooting,” Houston Chronicle's James Osborne \-- "A person who appears to be the shooter who killed two and injured 17 at a Minneapolis church Wednesday praised Texas congressional candidate and gun activist Brandon Herrera in a video posted before the shooting. The shooter, identified by as Robin Westman , 23, opened fire during a children’s Mass at Annunciation Catholic School. In a since-deleted video posted to YouTube, a person believed to be Westman films their arsenal of weapons and ammunition, along with a written manifesto, and says the message is “sponsored” by “Brandon Herrera for president,” before saying they met Herrera at SHOT Show last year. SHOT Show is an annual gun trade show in Las Vegas. Herrera, who at the time was running in a Republican primary in Texas’ 23rd Congressional District against Rep. Tony Gonzales , a campaign event there in 2024 and discussed his visit on his YouTube page. After to Gonzales in a runoff by fewer than 400 votes last year, Herrera is the San Antonio congressman again this cycle. “He and I had a conversation, a brief conversation,” the user believed to be Westman says in the video, which was by PatriotTakes, a left-wing research account. “We agreed on a lot of things. So, y’all should vote for Brandon Herrera for president.” In an , Herrera said he does not remember meeting Westman at SHOT Show but said he would be happy to answer questions from law enforcement. He added that he is coordinating with friends in law enforcement to help victims’ families. “I'm still physically sickened and angry about this clearly hate motivated attack on innocent children, and disgusted that my name came out of this demon's mouth,” Herrera wrote. Mark Oliva , a spokesperson for the National Shooting Sports Foundation, which operates SHOT Show, that the shooter's name was not among the registered attendees at the 2024 event or for prior years. Minneapolis police chief Brian O’Hara that the shooter had timed the release of a manifesto on YouTube, but Minnesota law enforcement have not yet verified that the specific YouTube video mentioning Herrera was posted by the shooter. The poster goes on to apologize to their family and ends by saying, “F–k those kids.” The person in the video also wrote racist slurs, tributes to domestic terrorists and threats against PresidentDonald Trump on his ammunition magazines and gear. In , Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said the shooter had written ‘Kill Donald Trump’ and other disturbing messages on a rifle magazine, referencing details shown in the same video that included the shooter’s comments about Herrera. A popular gun rights YouTuber with over 4 million subscribers known as “the AK guy,” Herrera criticized Gonzales, one of Congress’ more moderate Republicans, for supporting a gun safety bill that expanded background checks in the wake of the 2023 Robb Elementary shooting in Uvalde, which is in the district. Gonzales, who co-chairs the Bipartisan School Safety and Security Caucus, has made school safety one of his signature issues in Congress. Through a spokesperson, he declined to comment on the alleged shooter’s support for Herrera. In a social media post, Gonzales the shooting “tragic and infuriating.” “School security needs to be a top priority for lawmakers across the nation,” he wrote. “Too many lives have been lost. No more excuses.”" “Mark Teixeira, former MLB All Star, kicks off Texas House campaign,” Politico's Gregory Svirnovskiy \-- "Baseball starMark Teixeira launched a campaign to fill an open Texas House seat Thursday, the latest celebrity athlete to dive into politics. Teixeira is running as a Republican in a safe red seat being vacated by GOP Rep.Chip Roy. And he’s already appealing to President Donald Trump in search of a home run on the campaign trail. “As a lifelong conservative who loves this country, I’m running for Congress to fight for the principles that make Texas and America great,” . “It takes teamwork to win — I’m ready to help defend President Trump’s America First agenda, Texas families, and individual liberty.”" | LOCAL GOVERNMENT “Dallas property tax rate still up for discussion as council members look for wiggle room,” Dallas Morning News' Everton Bailey, Jr. \-- "For the — even though many homeowners will still pay more due to rising home values and costs. However, the exact new rate is still under discussion, as city officials continue to review a proposed $5.2 billion budget and gather public input before a final vote in mid-September. Council members suggested Wednesday that there may be some changes to the city manager’s proposed rate. Currently, the tax rate is 70.47 cents per $100** valuation, and City Manager Kim Tolbert’s proposed budget for the coming year lowers the rate to 69.97 cents. However, the City Council voted 10-5 on Wednesday to set a maximum possible rate at 70.22 cents — still less than this year’s rate but more than Tolbert’s proposal. Council members said the move would give them wiggle room as they discuss the budget with their constituents. Council members Chad West , Zarin Gracey , Jaime Resendez , Laura Cadena , Adam Bazaldua , Lorie Blair , Paula Blackmon , Kathy Stewart , Bill Roth , and Deputy Mayor Pro Tem Gay Donnell Willis voted in favor of the motion. Mayor Eric Johnson , Mayor Pro Tem Jesse Moreno and council members Maxie Johnson , Cara Mendelsohn andPaul Ridley voted against it. Under Tolbert’s proposed rate, a home valued at $382,010 — with a $175,000 homestead exemption — is projected to lower the average homeowner’s tax bill by about $12.66 next year. But tax bills could still rise or fall depending on changes in home values. Tolbert’s proposed budget plan calls for a significant increase in funding for police and fire services amid cuts to city jobs, community pools, libraries, and other consolidations. Council member Adam Bazaldua , who proposed the higher ceiling, argued that setting a lower bar could limit the council’s ability to explore alternatives to some of the proposed cuts. If the council approves Tolbert’s rate, the city would collect $11 million less in property taxes. If they stick with the proposed 70.22-cent ceiling, the loss would be about $5.5 million. “I believe it would be preliminary for us to set a ceiling before having a discussion to see if there are potential viable options to save some of the cuts that were brought forth with this proposed budget,” Bazaldua said. The City Council scheduled a Sept. 17 public hearing at City Hall to gather residents’ opinions on the tax rate before voting to finalize it and the citywide budget the same day. The new rate and budget would take effect on Oct. 1." ($) “Johnson County Sheriff Adam King arrested on felony corruption charges,” Dallas Morning News' Matt Kyle \-- "Johnson County Sheriff Adam King was arrested Wednesday on charges of abuse of office and witness retaliation, according to jail records. King was indicted on two charges of corrupt influence: retaliation against a witness, which is a third-degree felony, and one charge of abuse of office, in addition to a charge of official oppression — sexual harassment, a Class A misdemeanor, court records show. King was booked into the Johnson County jail. Bond had not been set by about 8:15 p.m. The arresting agency was the Texas Rangers, jail records show. Johnson County Judge Christopher Boedeker said via email that the indictments are a result of a weekslong investigation by the Rangers. Boedeker said as soon as county officials were aware of the allegations, they referred the case to the Rangers. “While Mr. King is entitled to a presumption of innocence, no person is above the law,” Boedeker said. According to the indictment, which was sent to The Dallas Morning News by Boedeker, King is accused of sexually harassing multiple female employees of the sheriff’s office between February 2024 and July 2025. The indictment said King made several sexual remarks to female subordinates, including telling them they needed to wear makeup to work and telling one employee if she kept “losing weight,” he would “do ungodly things” to her. The indictments also accused King of retaliating against two employees who reported the harassment, including threatening to arrest a female employee whom he allegedly had harassed. King also tried to obtain her address after finding out she had filed a human resources complaint against him and spoke to the Rangers about the allegations, the indictment said. King, a Republican, was first elected as sheriff of Johnson County in 2016. The Johnson County sheriff’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The News." ($) “Dallas ousts newly hired Inspector General due to charter violation,” Dallas Morning News' Devyani Chhetri \-- "The Dallas City Council Inspector General Timothy Menke , a longtime law enforcement executive, Wednesday after weeks of discussing how city officials bungled his hiring process. Last November, voters approved a that established an independent office of inspector general and called for its top officer to be “a competent practicing attorney of recognized ability.” However, Menke, who began his job on June 30 and has decades of experience investigating governmental fraud and misconduct, is not an attorney. During the meeting, council members did not publicly discuss the rationale behind the vote. They also didn’t get into what caused the error. “It’s an unfortunate setback but had to be done to have the IG’s qualifications align with those in the charter,” Deputy Mayor pro tem Gay Donnell Willis , who had long advocated for creating an independent office during the charter process, told The Dallas Morning News. “I am still very much a believer in the need for an independent inspector general to suss out fraud, waste and abuse.” Willis said the council and staff will also explore ways to determine how the oversight occurred, as did council member Paula Blackmon, who noted that officials are now examining ways to improve internal processes. Around the U.S., inspectors general can come from various backgrounds. They could be attorneys, auditors, law enforcement officials and prosecutors. A for the position didn’t specify that the applicant needs to be an attorney, although it does mention that a master’s degree or a doctorate in jurisprudence is preferred, and calls for the applicant to possess a skillset that demonstrates legal acumen. Last year, council members had extensive discussions about picking a skilled firm to lead the recruitment. They wanted to avoid mistakes they had seen in the previous search for the new city manager, which had been riddled with issues. The brochure for the position featured Houston’s skyline instead of Dallas’, and the at the time carried out by former council member Tennell Atkins, former chair of the ad hoc administrative affairs committee, led to a behind-the-scenes fight in the City Council that . The City Council then hired MGT Consulting Group. For weeks, the City Council spent time in closed session interviewing candidates. The Dallas Morning News sought public records regarding the resumes of the candidates who applied for the job and the communication between council members, who held the final approval. The request was sent to the Attorney General’s office for review. The city withdrew its request for the attorney general’s ruling Wednesday and partially released documents that still provide no clarity about the oversight." ($) “Harris County Commissioners approve nearly $470K to sponsor Gay Softball World Series,” Houston Chronicle's John Lomax V \-- "Harris County commissioners Republican Commissioner Tom Ramsey cast the lone dissenting vote on the item that sparked criticism from amid ongoing disputes surrounding the county’s budget deficit. But Commissioner Adrian Garcia , who introduced the item, said half the money was allocated from a tourism fund for games and events that bring people to Harris County. "They're bringing in money, they're renting hotel rooms. This will pay for itself," Garcia said. Last year’s Gay Softball World Series was held in Las Vegas. Around 200 teams will descend on Houston Sept. 21 to Sept. 27 and face off in a series of matches beginning with pool-play elimination and culminating in a series of double elimination games beginning Sept. 25. The event’s organizers have yet to determine the exact fields where the world series will be held, according to . Raquel Hernandez-Boujourne , a Houston businesswoman and Republican running against Garcia in 2026, took to the mic Tuesday to criticize her political opponent for what she viewed as the latest in a long line of poor financial choices. "This county has money, but how it is managed is the issue," Hernandez-Boujourne said. "At a time when our roads are crumbling, families are being crushed by rising property taxes and basic services are underfunded, while jobs are being sacrificed, anyone with common sense knows handing out nearly half a million dollars of our taxpayer money to sponsor a softball tournament is fiscal negligence — and, frankly, this is how we got here today." Several other speakers, including Bob Choate , a conservative activist, and Warren Howell , a Republican candidate for Harris County judge, also criticized the expenditure. Although they decried it as wasteful spending, none of the speakers at Tuesday’s meeting criticized the event’s affiliation with the LGBTQ community. The Montrose Softball League Association, an amateur league of nearly 30 teams, successfully petitioned the Gay Softball World Series to hold its annual tournament in Houston in late July, according to , a Houston LGBTQ publication. The MSLA held its first world series event in 1984, and Paula Metz, the league’s commissioner, told OutSmart she was proud to see it return. "You’d think Houston, being a large city, would be able to accommodate this, right? But it takes a lot. Very few cities can handle over 200 teams in one week," Metz said. "For our team to be able to put together a winning bid is an accomplishment itself."" ($) | BUSINESS NEWS “Upstream oil shed almost 3,000 jobs so far this summer. Here’s what that might mean,” Houston Chronicle's Rachel Nostrant \-- "Texas slipped over the summer as crude prices hovered just above break-even levels and global supplies stayed abundant. Nearly 3,000 upstream workers, about 1.5% of the sector’s workforce, lost their jobs in June and July, according to the Texas Workforce Commission. The loss of jobs, after a modest increase earlier in the year, highlights a reckoning the oil and gas industry is expected to face if crude oil prices continue their recent downward trend, in addition to unbalanced global supply and demand, a volatile investment market and overall . As a result, upstream workers have found themselves taking the brunt of the impacts, with approximately 1,500 jobs lost in June and another 1,400 in July. Though the loss of about 3,000 jobs is statistically minor compared to the through the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic, they evince what some experts say could be an impending down cycle for the industry. Rig counts, drilling permits and the price of crude oil – all of which impact the upstream job market – have dropped over the last few months, said Karr Ingham , president of the Texas Alliance of Energy Producers. The price of West Texas Intermediate crude dropped to $62.17 in May, its lowest point since mid-2023, when most economists say the industry made its comeback from the COVID-19 pandemic. Although prices ping-ponged throughout July and August, the price of the benchmark crude still hovers around $63, as of Aug. 26. “Two months doesn't necessarily make a trend, for sure, but it kind of lines up with what we might expect,” Ingham said, referencing the recent loss of jobs. There has been relative job growth since 2023, so although the June and July losses do not seem close to the layoffs seen in COVID, the numbers do mark stagnation and the potential of more layoffs, Ingham said. Several workers, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said they were struggling to find employment opportunities, both in on- and off-shore drilling operations. Some questioned whether they should seek work outside of the oil and gas field, while others said they were considering new areas of specialization that may better insulate them from a volatile job cycle. Consolidation has led to a flurry of layoffs across all sectors of the industry over the past few months. Following its acquisition of Hess in July, Chevron announced it would be laying off employees from the former company’s Houston office. Encino Energy similarly announced plans in June to layoff 121 workers at its Houston base following the company’s acquisition by EOG Resources the month prior. Outsourcing of jobs such as information technology, accounting and security to countries with cheaper labor, such as India and Indonesia, have also seen Texas oil workers left by the wayside over the last few years. While it may be difficult for office workers to anticipate layoffs, upstream workers should keep their eyes on the price of crude oil and the balance between the global demand for oil compared to the resource’s supply over the next few months, Ingham said. If prices average far lower in 2025 than they did in 2024, and rig counts continue to be generally relatively weak, layoffs would historically be expected to follow. “The only question is, ‘Are we actually headed for $50?’” Ingham said. “I hope not...I don't suspect we're going to get down that far, but none of us know the answer to that question right now.”" ($) | TEXANS IN DC “Elon Musk wants to build $760M tunnels under Houston. He’s tapped a Texas congressman to make the pitch,” KUT's Lauren McGaughy and Houston Chronicle's Yilun Cheng \-- "The devastating flooding in Houston caused by Hurricane Harvey in 2017 killed dozens of people, inundated hundreds of thousands of homes and left the community desperate for a solution. Since then, local flood experts have extensively studied the possibility of a multibillion-dollar tunnel system across Harris County. Studies have focused on the construction of pipelines, 30 to 40 feet in diameter, that could ferry massive amounts of water out to the Gulf in the event of a storm. Now, after years of research and discussion, Elon Musk wants a piece of the project. An investigation by The Texas Newsroom and the Houston Chronicle has found that the billionaire, in partnership with Houston-area Rep. Wesley Hunt , has spent months aggressively pushing state and local officials to hire Musk’s Boring Co. to build around one major watershed. That could be a potentially cheaper, but, at least one expert said, less effective solution to the region’s historic flooding woes. Hunt’s team has said the and involve the company getting 15% of the cost up front from state and local coffers. Within two months of this push, the Harris County Commissioners Court unanimously voted to study a pilot program that included a look at smaller tunnels, with specifications similar to what Boring had pitched. Both Musk and Hunt stand to benefit should Boring be selected to build any part of the project. Hunt is to U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in next year’s Republican Senate primary. And landing a job like this would also be a significant win for Boring, which has not completed a major public project in Texas and faces criticisms for its . The discussions about the Boring pitch have happened mostly out of the public eye. in passing at a town hall in Houston in February. Since then, he has refused to answer the newsrooms’ questions about when Musk sold him on the idea and why he became its pitchman. Efforts to reach Musk and representatives with Boring were not returned. Experts and some local officials question whether Musk and his company are the right pick for the job. The Boring Co. has focused on transportation tunnels, not flood mitigation. “If you build a smaller tunnel, OK, it’ll be cheaper, but it can carry less water,” said Larry Dunbar , a veteran water resources engineer who has advised Houston-area governmental agencies on drainage issues. “So what have you saved? Have you reduced the flooding upstream by an inch? And are you going to spend multimillions of dollars to do that? Well, maybe that’s not worth it.” In response to the newsrooms’ questions, state and local officials said no public money has been allocated to Boring. County officials added that they have not chosen a tunnel contractor and any process to do so would follow normal procurement rules. Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick , during the legislative session to discuss the proposal, remains open to the idea. As president of the Texas Senate with close ties to PresidentDonald Trump , he is a powerful ally. “If Elon Musk and the Boring Company, or any other company, can build two massive tunnels under the Houston bayous in a few years to save the city from flooding, I am always going to be interested to listen,” Patrick, a Republican, told the newsrooms. “The truth is, Elon Musk is one of the only people in the world who could accomplish this.”" ($) | TRUMP ADMINISTRATION “Mystery surrounds $1.2 billion Army contract to build huge detention tent camp in Texas desert,” AP's Michael Biesecker andJoshua Goodman \-- "When President Donald Trump’s administration last month awarded a contract worth up to $1.2 billion to build and operate what it says will become , it didn’t turn to a large government contractor or even a firm that specializes in private prisons. Instead, it handed the project on a military base to Acquisition Logistics LLC, a small business that has no listed experience running a correction facility and had never won a federal contract worth more than $16 million. The company also lacks a functioning website and lists as its address a modest home in suburban Virginia owned by a 77-year-old retired Navy flight officer. | The mystery over the award only deepened last week as the new facility began to accept its first detainees. The Pentagon has refused to release the contract or explain why it selected Acquisition Logistics over a dozen other bidders to build the massive tent camp at Fort Bliss in west Texas. At least one competitor has filed a complaint. The secretive — and brisk — contracting process is emblematic, experts said, of the government’s broader rush to fulfill to arrest and deport living in the U.S. without permanent legal status. As part of that push, the government is turning increasingly to the military to handle tasks that had traditionally been left to civilian agencies. A member of Congress who recently toured the camp said she was concerned that such a small and inexperienced firm had been entrusted to build and run a facility expected to house up to 5,000 migrants. “It’s far too easy for standards to slip,” said Rep.Veronica Escobar , a Democrat whose district includes Fort Bliss. “Private facilities far too frequently operate with a profit margin in mind as opposed to a governmental facility.” AttorneyJoshua Schnell , who specializes in federal contracting law, said he was troubled that the Trump administration has provided so little information about the facility. “The lack of transparency about this contract leads to legitimate questions about why the Army would award such a large contract to a company without a website or any other publicly available information demonstrating its ability to perform such a complicated project,” he said. Ken A. Wagner , the president and CEO of Acquisition Logistics, did not respond to phone messages or emails. No one answered the door at his three-bedroom house listed as his company’s headquarters. Virginia records list Wagner as an owner of the business, though it’s unclear whether he might have partners. Defense SecretaryPete Hegseth approved using Fort Bliss for the new detention center, and the administration has hopes to build more at other bases. A spokesperson for the Army declined to discuss its deal with Acquisition Logistics or reveal details about the camp’s construction, citing the litigation over the company’s qualifications. The Department of Homeland Security, which includes U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, declined to answer questions about the detention camp it oversees. Named Camp East Montana for the closest road, the facility is being built in the sand and scrub Chihuahuan Desert, where summertime temperatures can exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit and heat-related deaths are common. The 60-acre site is near the U.S.-Mexico border and the El Paso International Airport, a key hub for . The camp has drawn comparisons to a $245 million tent complex erected to hold ICE detainees in the Florida Everglades. That facility has been the subject of complaints about unsanitary conditions and lawsuits. A federal judge recently . The vast majority of the roughly 57,000 migrants detained by ICE are housed at operated by companies like Florida’s Geo Group and Tennessee-based CoreCivic. As those facilities fill up, ICE is also exploring temporary options at military bases in California, New York and Utah. At Fort Bliss, construction began within days of the Army issuing the contract on July 18. Site work began months earlier, before Congress had passed Trump’s big tax and spending cuts bill, which includes a record $45 billion for immigration enforcement. The Defense Department announcement specified only that the Army was financing the initial $232 million for the first 1,000 beds at the complex. Three white tents, each about 810 feet long, have been erected, according to satellite imagery examined by The Associated Press. name: Mikie Sherrill
subject: All eyes on New Jersey
disclaimer_text: Paid for by State Democrats Committee (StateDemocrats
body:
the stakes here are very high
#
Peter, every single day since he took office in January, it seems like Donald Trump has found new ways to abuse his power and make life harder for our families.
He’s illegally withheld funding that New Jerseyans rely on for child care, for health care, and for access to healthy food.
He’s deployed the National Guard to American cities in a transparent attempt to instill terror and fear.
He signed a devastating spending bill that guts Medicaid access and makes everything from groceries to heating your home less affordable — all to give billionaires a giant tax cut.
And honestly, that’s just a fraction of it.
**As Trump has inflicted all this damage on our country, Republican politicians like Jack Ciattarelli have cheered him on every step of the way.**
There is seemingly nothing Trump can do — no matter how illegal, reckless, or outright devastating for New Jersey families — that would make Jack Ciattarelli say “enough is enough.”
**And Peter, polls show that Ciattarelli is within a few percentage points of becoming New Jersey’s next governor.**
If we’re going to win that race and prevent that from happening, we need to work night and day these next 10 weeks to get our message out.
I intend to do exactly that, Peter — because the stakes for New Jersey, and for our nation, are too high to give it anything less. But I can’t win this race without your help.
**[Let’s send a message that the people reject Donald Trump and Jack Ciattarelli’s disastrous agenda, Peter. Let’s send a message that we won’t stand for their attacks on working families or on the rule of law — and that we’re ready to lead the way with a better path forward. subject: Incredible news
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Haley Stevens for Senate
body:
I’m grateful to have you on my team, null, and now I’m asking you to be on Sherrod’s.

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. [To unsubscribe from this email list, please click here.](https://act.haleyformi.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?&t=1&akid=701%2E49239%2EWTRqgM)

null, I’m reaching out with some incredible news:
**My friend Sherrod Brown just announced that he’s running for Senate again in Ohio! I’m so proud to support him, and I’m counting on you to join me.[Will you chip in $5 or more now – split between Sherrod and me – to help give his campaign the strongest kickoff possible?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/4976?t=3&akid=701%2E49239%2EWTRqgM)**
As Sherrod says himself, he never planned to return to public office. But he sees what’s happening in Washington, and he’s called to jump back in the fight. He’s the exact leader we need at this moment.
Sherrod has spent his life fighting for the Dignity of Work – the idea that hard work should pay off for everyone, no matter who you are, where you come from, or what kind of work you do. Right now, this principle is under threat.
Billionaires and corporations are profiting like never before – while workers and everyday people are struggling just to make ends meet. _The system is rigged in favor of the wealthiest among us, and Sherrod is running to change that._
**If there’s one thing I know about Sherrod, it’s that he never backs down from a tough fight. But this is going to be one of the most competitive Senate races on the map in 2026, and he needs to build a massive grassroots movement to win.**
**[I’m grateful to have you on my team, null, and now I’m asking you to be on Sherrod’s. With so much at stake, will you give $5 or more now – split between Sherrod and me – to help fuel our grassroots movement and flip Ohio’s Senate seat?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/4976?t=4&akid=701%2E49239%2EWTRqgM)**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Haley Stevens and Sherrod Brown will go through immediately:_ | | | [Donate $5](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/4977?t=5&akid=701%2E49239%2EWTRqgM)

I’m so grateful to have you in this fight – and I know Sherrod is too.

Thank you,

Haley Stevens
|

**A note from Haley Stevens:** null, I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. That’s why I’ve fought so hard for working families my entire life. Now, I’m running for Michigan’s open Senate seat to continue fighting for the people and communities I love. The path to the Senate majority runs right through Michigan, which means this race is shaping up to be the most competitive and expensive in the entire country. The GOP is already coming after me as a top target for defeat, so I’m counting on your grassroots support to fight back and win. name: Deb Haaland
subject: I’m worried
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
Thank you in advance for opening this email.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=4084%2E400544%2EL4HBsH)
This isn’t the update I hoped to send — but I need to be transparent with you: **I’m worried.**
**Our grassroots fundraising has taken a bigger hit this summer than we anticipated. We had to cut our campaign projections in July. Now, we’re nearing the end of August, and we’re not on track to meet our monthly goal.**
At the same time, a **Republican opponent has officially launched his campaign.** We knew this would happen eventually, but the timing couldn’t be _worse_.
We’re entering one of the most critical phases of this race, and we’re operating with fewer resources than we need to compete in one of the largest states in the country.
**As you know, I’ve never had the means to self-fund a campaign, and I don’t come from wealth.** What I do have is this grassroots team — tens of thousands of folks like you who believe that New Mexico needs a governor who understands what it means to struggle and who will fight fiercely for our home and our people.
Our average online donation this month is just **$23**. It’s that steady stream of people-powered support that allows us to build support across our beautiful state. It helps us pay for critical campaign investments, distribute literature, run digital ads, and connect with voters in the places that are too often ignored.
**The reality is this: If we don’t have strong fundraising numbers, Donald Trump and Republicans will put millions of dollars into flipping this state. We can’t let this happen.** That’s why this major fundraising slump is concerning, and it’s why I’m asking for your support today.
**My campaign could use your help as we work to meet our urgent $180,000 end-of-month goal. Will you donate $5 or your most generous donation today to power our campaign forward? You can use the link below to make sure your donation goes through instantly:**
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250828_1_eom?personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250828_1_eom?amount=5&refcode=em20250828-4084&refcode2=4084_400544_L4HBsH&akid=4084%2E400544%2EL4HBsH)
Thank you again for everything you’re doing to support our campaign. I know there is no obstacle we can’t overcome if we continue standing together.
Be fierce,
Deb
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_footer?refcode=em20250828-1&t=2&refcode2=4084_400544_L4HBsH&akid=4084%2E400544%2EL4HBsH)**

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with grassroots supporters like you. However, if you would like to change your subscription preferences, here are some options:
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails-dh/?t=3&akid=4084%2E400544%2EL4HBsH)

* [Unsubscribe](https://act.debhaaland.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe-dh/?t=4&akid=4084%2E400544%2EL4HBsH)

Friend,
Our plan to beat Kevin Kiley and flip this seat has been the same since Day 1, and a new district map doesn't change that. We're going to take you through this point-by-point, but if you only have a moment can you support Heidi's people-powered campaign to flip this seat today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20250828_em_fr_b1_THH_BIG]
Heidi didn't join this race when news outlets and analysts started reporting on how redistricting could make this one of the few races that decides control of Congress— she joined months ago when Kevin Kiley's absence forced her to.
She joined when she saw how working families were struggling due to his inaction.
She joined when she saw Kiley failing to push back against an out-of-control and authoritarian Trump administration.
She joined when she was tired of watching Kiley pick fights with Gavin Newsom instead of addressing the issues that matter.
Friend, Heidi's experience working in the EPA will help our district fight to protect our environment from wildfires, her experience working as Nevada County Supervisor will help her deliver on the issues that matter to real working people, and her dedication to service will help us create a better future for everyone in our district.
But who's in our district?
While our plan to flip this seat hasn't changed, it does require consistent community outreach to communicate Heidi's winning message with voters. Once congressional maps are finalized, our campaign needs to hit the ground running.
And to do that we need your help, Friend. Will you please chip in what you can to help us raise the remaining $12,563 we need to reach our August fundraising goal and gather the resources to communicate with voters as soon as we can? Heidi Hall has spent her three-decade public service career working with others to solve problems, protect our land and water, improve health, and build opportunities for others, all while raising two boys primarily as a single mom.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20250828_em_fr_b1_THH_BIG [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20250828_em_fr_b1_THH_BIG]
Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.
Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

Carolina, United We Dream \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Bruna, United We Dream Date: Tuesday, August 26, 2025 Subject: DACA recipients will lose their access to health coverage through the ACA Peter, it’s Bruna from United We Dream — I’m reaching out because our fight for immigrant justice and dignity is more urgent than ever. Due to a decision by the administration, as of August 25, DACA recipients are no longer eligible for health insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act (ACA) 1. For many DACA recipients, access to affordable health care is not just a policy issue; it's a lifeline. Approximately 11,000 DACA recipients nationwide will lose health coverage without access to the ACA. Health care is a fundamental human right, and everyone should have access to it, regardless of their immigration status. This is yet another attempt at intimidation by the administration, but we know that the power to initiate real change rests with us — the people.We know that immigrants are exercising the strength and resilience of our communities to create a future where we can all thrive. Through collective action, advocacy, and community support, we have the strength to push back against policies that undermine our shared values and to fight for the rights of all immigrants. United We Dream is committed to this essential work, but we need your support. Your contribution will fuel our efforts to advocate for policies that ensure justice and dignity for immigrant communities. #

Check out this old pic. What do you see? [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114182629/566212091/1388073184?refcode=AU_JC_FR_GEN_EOM_NO_20250828_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODUyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNjk2NzM1YS01Mzg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JoIY7Xh9HyVZnhIEWGl32bDN3svihB2CvpGXvu3tdRc=) Beneath that bowl cut, there’s a little kid who had _no idea_ what life had in store for him. His world revolved around Legos and backyard adventures. I grew up in a working-class family. I worked construction and at Arby’s — anything I could do to help. After high school, I joined the National Guard to help pay for college. Then 9/11 happened. I felt called to serve, became a paratrooper, then an Army Ranger, and deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan. When I came home, I helped fellow veterans rebuild their lives and later ran for Congress to continue serving my community. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114182630/566212092/1388073184?refcode=AU_JC_FR_GEN_EOM_NO_20250828_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODUyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNjk2NzM1YS01Mzg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JoIY7Xh9HyVZnhIEWGl32bDN3svihB2CvpGXvu3tdRc=) Because when Donald Trump first took office, I saw what was coming. He attacked health care, vilified immigrants, and tried to dismantle the democratic institutions I risked my life to defend. That’s what drove me to run in 2018 — and it’s why I’m still in this fight today. Now, during Trump’s second term, the fight continues. His economic policies are driving up costs for working families. He’s sowing fear, targeting immigrant communities, workers, and civil servants. body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=em20250828-821&t=1001&akid=830%2E251025%2EtOtB51 ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=em20250828-821&t=1002&akid=830%2E251025%2EtOtB51 ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter,

I’ll be honest up front. I’m about to ask for your help. But before you
close out of the email, I just ask that you give me one minute of your
time so I can share with you why this is so important and what your help
would mean.

You’re still reading? Amazing... I appreciate you. 🙏

The Democratic Party is in a do-or-die moment. We lost a winnable election
to a creepy authoritarian billionaire. But our party leaders and
establishment consultants learned the exact wrong lessons. They want to
entrench us even further as the milquetoast, say-nothing,
stand-for-nothing party. A party with no excitement, no moral clarity, and
no agenda.

Michigan is the epicenter of the battle for the soul of the Democratic
Party. If we screw it up here, we’re doomed elsewhere. We are the key
swing state with a wide-open primary to determine who’ll fight the
Republicans for a must-win U.S. Senate seat.

The same establishment leaders who botched the last election have their
thumb on the scales in this primary. They’ve handpicked a Democrat who
votes at times like a Republican, who schmoozes with corporate PACs, and
wins over AIPAC folks. They believe the way to win is to be as quiet as
possible about key issues. And they’ll sell their loyalty to whoever
writes the largest check as long as it affords them enough money for an
extra TV ad or two.

They’re dead wrong. And if their milquetoast moderate wins this primary,
we could lose not only Michigan’s Senate seat, but any shot we have at
reshaping the future of this party to give us a fighting chance at taking
power back from Donald Trump.

Now, it’s easy to critique. And folks will say, “Abdul, what do you
propose?” I’ll answer that.

* How about a Democratic Party with candidates we are — for once —
excited to vote for? Candidates who aren’t afraid to speak their minds
and capture attention in an age where social media is such a critical
and powerful tool.
* How about a Democratic Party that stands for something concrete?
Medicare for All. Tax the billionaires. Stop funding genocide in Gaza.
* How about a Democratic Party that brings in new voters, young voters,
and disillusioned voters? Offer a real alternative to the false choice
between “status quo moderation” and “right-wing authoritarianism.”

My friends, we can be that Democratic Party. But if we lose to the
establishment here in Michigan, we may be set back in that mission for
years to come.

So today, I’m asking you for help. Not just to elect me as the next U.S.
Senator from Michigan — but to transform the Democratic Party as we know
it into an exciting, purpose-driven, and tent-expanding team that can
defeat Trumpism and wannabe oligarchs for decades to come.

I don’t want to come off as cocky or overconfident, but depending on the
poll, we’re nearly tied for first or second place in this race. Winning
isn’t some unachievable hurdle. And if we out-raise our opponents in this
critical quarter, we will do two things:

1. We will have enough resources to spread the word about our campaign
and build a solid lead heading into the primary.
2. We will attract serious attention from the national politicians and
pundits who will see that we represent the best path forward for the
Democrats to win in November.

Not everyone can give the same amount — and that’s the beauty of a
people-powered campaign. Some will step up with larger gifts, others with
smaller ones. Together, we build something stronger than corporate PACs
ever could.

* If you have done well and can afford it, please consider giving a bit
more for those who can’t. [ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20250828-1-ak?amount=500&refcode=em20250828-821&refcode2=830_251025_tOtB51&akid=830%2E251025%2EtOtB51 ]Click here to donate $1,000, $500, $100,
or as much as you can.
* If you can pitch in at the grassroots level, [ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20250828-1-ak?amount=25&refcode=em20250828-821&refcode2=830_251025_tOtB51&akid=830%2E251025%2EtOtB51 ]click here to donate
$25 or any amount you’re comfortable with.
* If you can’t give right now, that’s okay. Help share our message on
social media, forward this email to a friend, or [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/339?utm_source=em20250828-821&t=1004&akid=830%2E251025%2EtOtB51 ]sign up to
volunteer. Your support is just as essential to this movement as any
donation.

I can’t thank you enough for reading my email. I know it was long. But I
hope it left you feeling a sense of purpose and hope heading into this
primary.

We have work to do, but we can win.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with grassroots supporters like you. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

We need to connect the dots and expose their lies. | | | Hi Peter — it’s Congressman Maxwell Frost. Since January, some politicians and pundits have been fixated on calling every outrageous thing Trump does a “distraction.” When they call something a “distraction,” they are implying that we shouldn't pay attention to it — that we should pay attention to that _other_ thing instead. Right now, some folks want us to believe that there's really two different things going on. **But these aren’t two separate stories. It’s all part of the _same_ story.** On one side, we saw Republicans pass their Big Ugly Law — the largest transfer of wealth from the working class to billionaires in history. They’re gutting Medicaid, slashing nutritional assistance, and leaving families drowning under rising cost of living. On the other side, we see the federal government occupying our cities, masked ICE agents terrorizing our communities and kidnapping people and deporting families, and Republicans redrawing Congressional districts across the country and attacking our right to vote. **These aren’t two different things. It’s the same damn thing.** Because the only way they can pass something like the Big Ugly Law and feel like they won't see any political repercussions is by doing things like deploying the military to our streets, scaring people with ICE, and trying to redraw maps to favor Republicans in every red state. These aren't acts intended to distract from each other. These are acts that are meant to _enable_ each other. It’s all part of ONE story, a story that a lot of us are familiar with: **the billionaires getting richer and working people getting poorer.** Let me give you an example: The first time I went to the Everglades “Alligator Alcatraz” detention facility in Florida, I saw two private planes on the tarmac. I asked “who do those private planes belong to?” They didn’t look like official government planes to me. The answer I got? “Oh, they're executives from two of the biggest corporations that are running the place.” This one facility — part of the national campaign of intimidation and fear against immigrant communities — is also a source of $450 million of Florida taxpayer money going to billionaires and mega corporations. And that’s just the tip of the iceberg. It's the same story that we’ve seen for decades. Corrupt politicians and billionaires taking resources away from working people so they can grow even richer. Our democracy being stripped away all so they can keep getting away with it with no accountability. [**But we can fight back — and we can beat them. It will take all of us finding strength in each other, organizing together, and building the kind of political power for working people that can’t be ignored. clean_body: We need to connect the dots and expose their lies. | | | Hi Peter — it’s Congressman Maxwell Frost. Since January, some politicians and pundits have been fixated on calling every outrageous thing Trump does a “distraction.” When they call something a “distraction,” they are implying that we shouldn't pay attention to it — that we should pay attention to that other thing instead. Right now, some folks want us to believe that there's really two different things going on. But these aren’t two separate stories. It’s all part of the same story. On one side, we saw Republicans pass their Big Ugly Law — the largest transfer of wealth from the working class to billionaires in history. They’re gutting Medicaid, slashing nutritional assistance, and leaving families drowning under rising cost of living. On the other side, we see the federal government occupying our cities, masked ICE agents terrorizing our communities and kidnapping people and deporting families, and Republicans redrawing Congressional districts across the country and attacking our right to vote. These aren’t two different things. It’s the same damn thing. Because the only way they can pass something like the Big Ugly Law and feel like they won't see any political repercussions is by doing things like deploying the military to our streets, scaring people with ICE, and trying to redraw maps to favor Republicans in every red state. These aren't acts intended to distract from each other. These are acts that are meant to enable each other. It’s all part of ONE story, a story that a lot of us are familiar with: the billionaires getting richer and working people getting poorer. Let me give you an example: The first time I went to the Everglades “Alligator Alcatraz” detention facility in Florida, I saw two private planes on the tarmac. I asked “who do those private planes belong to?” They didn’t look like official government planes to me. The answer I got? “Oh, they're executives from two of the biggest corporations that are running the place.” This one facility — part of the national campaign of intimidation and fear against immigrant communities — is also a source of $450 million of Florida taxpayer money going to billionaires and mega corporations. And that’s just the tip of the iceberg. It's the same story that we’ve seen for decades. Corrupt politicians and billionaires taking resources away from working people so they can grow even richer. Our democracy being stripped away all so they can keep getting away with it with no accountability. Your support makes it possible for us to keep organizing working people in our communities, challenging corporate power, and telling the real story — one that connects the dots and exposes their lies. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

Donald Trump and his GOP allies know they're facing a deteriorating political and economic environment, so they're undertaking an **unprecedented partisan redistricting** **effort** to give themselves a leg up in 2026 and beyond.

_This is one of the most competitive Senate races in the country._ That’s why it’s so important that we build the resources early. What we raise today will determine how strong we start September and whether we win in November 2026.

Peter, **Meet Lisa Cook.** She’s the member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors Trump attempted to oust this week. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsQNarR6PCR1lUtXpWTyhe6WJenW09tVt92DRoJgnTPAQyY8E_VLHYuhEAZdtLSQkhXv9X1uCNLiUivNlLHBwbWMt9qFxS_E6816MpU9sdrVgdxihp1OqW0-hsIjgCvw8gz_klD4tEVGhf4vZlaVb9vIsjUeWaew7_tskj_pmVnrzxbXJkAQq1IwGBJwFc9RRcj6IrP3WoDDzihAKkDz1QZO5IWwzlmkmt5tz6ATrhNDEsJtv9zgrbEiWs1pH_nM4y6lwuT9Icn-oFpR2sICve4/4jf/1FIm0llYTKaPR4oqa9lF1g/h0/h001.Rz9dM0t9L2pzcGV69RnA8zD5t-K0WlwWd6iITQKT114) **Trump’s attempt to fire Lisa Cook is shaping up to become the ultimate showdown at the Supreme Court.** It’s no secret that Trump wants control over the Federal Reserve. He’s been pressuring them to lower interest rates for months—even as he creates economic conditions that make that a dangerous idea.**Trump wants full control of the economic narrative because he’s utterly failed to deliver on his campaign promises to lower costs―in fact, he’s increased them, and he wants the Fed to shoulder the blame for his own economic mismanagement.** **Now, Trump is seizing on ginned up allegations to justify firing Cook and replacing her with a loyalist who will do as he says. He wants Cook to take the fall for his own failure.** No formal charges have been filed against Cook, putting the idea that he’s firing her “for cause” in question. Cook is challenging her firing in court. And since September’s interest rate vote is right around the corner, Trump is ready to escalate all the way to the Supreme Court. **In a previous case on the firings of federal employees, the Supreme Court specifically named the Federal Reserve as off limits.** They have created a clear line between regulators that help bail out banks and regulators that protect Americans from Wall Street predators. With his attacks on the Fed, Trump is putting a challenge to the MAGA justices. Do they serve capital, or do they serve the King they’ve created in Trump? The Federal Reserve says it will abide by any court’s decision in the case. **The Supreme Court will get the final say on whether the Federal Reserve maintains its vital independence, or whether Trump gets even more control over our democracy.** Experts say that if Cook loses, “That's the end of Fed independence as it has been constructed and reconstructed over 112 years.”1 **Trump’s authoritarian movements are coming fast and furious.** United for Democracy is keeping the spotlight on the Supreme Court and all the ways it can stand up to Trump or give him even more power. name: Chris Ahuja
subject: Weapons of war don’t belong here.
body:
Other countries acted. So can we.

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=97f443092fb7c091746070aa0&id=049ad4652d&e=5a6ee82cdb)
| | | | | [Donate](https://chrisahuja.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=97f443092fb7c091746070aa0&id=d4982d8d00&e=5a6ee82cdb)

| | Dear Peter,[](https://chrisahuja.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=97f443092fb7c091746070aa0&id=09a237e39b&e=5a6ee82cdb)**We don’t have to live this way. Other countries have faced tragedy—and they acted.** After the Christchurch mosque massacre in 2019, New Zealand banned assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, tightened licensing, and passed a buyback program with overwhelming support. Since then, gun violence has dropped dramatically.**The difference? They made it a priority. Their leaders chose action over excuses.****In the United States, we keep losing lives because politicians would rather protect the gun lobby than protect our kids**. I refuse to accept that. I’m running because Los Angeles—and this country—deserve leaders who will stand up to the NRA and finally deliver real gun safety reforms.**This campaign is people-powered, not lobbyist-backed. To keep building it, I need your help.**[**Can you chip in $25, $50, or $100 today to support a campaign that puts people’s lives ahead of weapons manufacturers?**](https://chrisahuja.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=97f443092fb7c091746070aa0&id=f85e9596f5&e=5a6ee82cdb)**Every time we normalize another mass shooting, we let the status quo win.** I believe we can do better, because other countries have proven it’s possible. The only thing standing in the way is political will. Together, we can change that.**In solidarity,
**[****](https://chrisahuja.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=97f443092fb7c091746070aa0&id=090cd2a3fb&e=5a6ee82cdb)**Chris Ahuja****Democrat for Congress, CD-32**

name: Sen. Jeff Bridges
subject: Polis just testified at the JBC on $1.2B in cuts
body:
As JBC Chair, I pressed Gov. Polis today on the shortfall — and why we need a Treasurer who invests in Colorado.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/ed0e9f3d9b93/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10368637?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=62f7399873&e=b48bb2b4f4)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
Governor Polis just finished testifying at the Joint Budget Committee, which I chair, about how Colorado will address the $1.2 billion shortfall created by HR1—that big whatever bill in Washington. We dug in, debated alternatives, and made sure the plan reflects our Colorado values.
The good news is we just wrapped a successful special session where we closed corporate tax loopholes, and I ran a bill that fully restored funding to Planned Parenthood.
---
[|
---](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=9c9637a510&e=b48bb2b4f4)
| | Despite this good work, the latest shortfall still means less for Medicaid, less for higher education, and less for housing. This time not because of TABOR, but because of Trump.
That’s why I’m running for Treasurer.
Our Treasurer manages investments for the state, and now more than ever we need to invest Colorado dollars in Colorado. **We can make low-interest loans to improve infrastructure, increase renewable energy, and build housing that working Coloradans can actually afford.** It’s an approach we’ve seen in other states, and one we can lead on here in Colorado.
For Denver7 coverage of the recent Special Session head [here](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=e48172450b&e=b48bb2b4f4). If you want Colorado dollars working for Coloradans, [donate here](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=52daef66d3&e=b48bb2b4f4). And if you can, join us for an event in [Denver at Barb Grogan’s](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=a5a83fedad&e=b48bb2b4f4), in [Boulder at KC Becker’s](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=614f286574&e=b48bb2b4f4), or [for a kid-friendly brunch](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=b529726304&e=b48bb2b4f4).
Talk soon,

PS [Lofi with puppies](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=fa88969d1c&e=b48bb2b4f4).

Since the moment I was sworn in this year, the GOP has made me a top target.
In fact, less than two weeks after entering office, GOP leadership started fundraising for their next nominee in Michigan’s 8th – and they put me right at the top of their target list.
And by spring, attack ads were already flooding Mid-Michigan airwaves – paid for by national Republicans and their special interest allies. They’re desperate to flip MI-08, and they’ll say or spend whatever it takes to tear me down.

FIRST he deployed the National Guard to Washington, D.C., militarizing the streets of our capital under the false pretense of “fighting crime.” THEN he threatened to do the same thing in other large cities with Democratic elected officialsall over the country. NOW he’s claiming that people want him to be a dictator! 🚨 This is not the time to stay silent — Pramila knows that now more than ever, it’s critical that we keep resisting both inside and outside of Congress. But Peter, none of the work Pramila does for our movement is possible without your grassroots support. In solidarity, Team Jayapal | | Email us: info@pramilaforcongress.com

Patriot,

>From the kitchen to the coastline, I’ve seen the power of sustainability firsthand.

As a chef, I believe that what we put on our plates is deeply connected to the health of our environment and our communities.

Because when we protect our environment, we’re not just saving trees or oceans. We’re preserving access to clean air, clean water, and real food packed with nutrients.

At my restaurants, I’ve built everything around sustainability, sourcing traceable seafood, supporting responsible aquaculture, and working directly with ranchers and fishermen who care about long-term health over short-term gain.

But no chef, no restaurant, and no individual can do this alone.

We need a national movement to fight for clean water, regenerative agriculture, and responsible stewardship.

That’s where the American Conservation Coalition (ACC) comes in.

**ACC is leading the charge for a cleaner, more sustainable America — _without_ the heavy hand of government mandates.**

They’re building a movement of young, pro-environment conservatives who believe we can protect both our health and our freedoms.

I’m so passionate about their approach that I told the American Conservation Coalition I would help them raise $10,000 before the end of the month to support their mission.

The American Conservation Coalition is building the conservative environmental movement. Their goals? To:

👩🏻🌾 **Restore regenerative farming practices** rooted in health and sustainability
🏞️ **Conserve America’s natural resources** for future generations
☣️ **Reduce toxins** in our food, water, and air
✅ **Promote real solutions** that create healthy communities and families

ACC empowers young conservatives to join the national discussion concerning conservation, clean energy, sportsmen’s rights, regenerative agriculture, and more.

With over 80,000 members, ACC branches complete local clean-up projects, influence local, state, and national environmental policy, and drive change that embraces common-sense solutions to the health crises and environmental problems we face.

Patriot, this isn’t about politics.

It’s about conserving the things that nourish us – our land, oceans, and our children’s future – _not through mandates or government overreach_ , but by protecting what makes this country beautiful.

Chef Andrew Gruel
